; DNS records for example.com — add them at your DNS provider.
; Format: name  type  value

; WHAT TO ADD — one block below = one record in your provider's form
;
;   Type: A
;   Name: relay   — most panels want just relay — some want the full relay.example.com
;   Value: 203.0.113.10
;   TTL: Auto (or 3600)
;
; Cloudflare: set Proxy status to "DNS only" (grey cloud) for EVERY record here. The orange cloud breaks mail and the VPN.
;
; IMPORT INSTEAD OF TYPING
; Cloudflare: DNS → Records → "Import and Export" → "Import DNS records" → upload example.com-dns-zone.txt.
; Then check every imported record is "DNS only" (grey cloud).
; The same example.com-dns-zone.txt works at Route53, Google, Namecheap, GoDaddy, Gandi, Hetzner, deSEC, DNSimple, Porkbun.
; Panels that ask for a spreadsheet instead: use example.com-dns-records.csv.


; Forward record for the PTR hostname (reverse DNS must resolve back to the same IP).
relay.example.com.    IN A    203.0.113.10

; PTR (reverse DNS) is configured NOT here but in the server provider's panel:
; 203.0.113.10 -> relay.example.com — critical for deliverability.

; BIND zone file for example.com - import this at your DNS provider.
; SOA/NS are managed by the provider and are intentionally not included.
$ORIGIN example.com.
$TTL 3600
relay.example.com.    3600    IN A    203.0.113.10

type,name,value,ttl,priority
A,relay.example.com,203.0.113.10,3600,

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — self-hosted services for example.com in a single run.
# GRYONIXNEXUS_DISTRO: debian
# Run: sudo bash setup-mail-server.sh
# The script is self-contained and idempotent: packages, configs (with backups), firewall, services — all in one run; re-running it is safe.
set -euo pipefail

# Pinned, never inherited. Whatever launches this script may have
# tightened its own umask — the app's runner did, to keep the run log
# private — and a script that adopts it writes 0700 directories and
# 0600 files that only root can read. Nothing here notices (it IS
# root), but caddy, mailcow's nginx worker and every other service
# running as somebody else cannot read what was written for them.
# Secrets get an explicit chmod at the point they are created; the
# default has to stay ordinary.
umask 022

log()    { printf '\n==> %s\n' "$*"; }
fail()   { printf 'ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
# Copies a changed file aside, keeping the newest five
backup() {
  [ -f "$1" ] || return 0
  local last
  last="$(ls -1d "$1".bak.* 2>/dev/null | sort | tail -n 1 || true)"
  if [ -n "$last" ] && cmp -s "$1" "$last"; then return 0; fi
  cp -a "$1" "$1.bak.$(date +%s)"
  ls -1d "$1".bak.* | sort | head -n -5 | xargs -r rm -f
}
# Retry a flaky command a few times with a linear backoff. Fresh servers
# pull many large images at once (mailcow alone is ~15), and a single
# transient registry error/timeout would otherwise abort the whole run
# under `set -e` — the user then had to hit Retry by hand. The setup is
# idempotent, so a re-pull just resumes cached layers.
retry()  {
  local tries="$1"; shift
  local i=1
  while true; do
    "$@" && return 0
    if [ "$i" -ge "$tries" ]; then return 1; fi
    printf '\n(retry %d/%d) %s\n' "$i" "$tries" "$*" >&2
    sleep $((i * 5))
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
}

[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || fail "root privileges required: sudo bash $0"

# The distribution was pinned at generation time in the app — here it is only verified.
# The path is a variable so the check can be exercised against a stub
# file — the alternative was a test that runs a doctored copy of this
# block and proves nothing about the artifact that ships. It is not a
# privilege boundary: the script already runs as root.
gd_os_release="${GRYONIXNEXUS_OS_RELEASE:-/etc/os-release}"
[ -r "$gd_os_release" ] || fail "/etc/os-release not found — unsupported OS"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
. "$gd_os_release"
# A derivative (Devuan, Linux Mint, Pop!_OS, …) names its base in
# ID_LIKE and behaves like it for apt and systemd, so it is accepted.
# A distribution we support in its OWN right never passes as another
# one: Ubuntu lists debian in ID_LIKE, and letting that through would
# silently install with the wrong profile instead of saying so.
if [ "${ID:-}" != "debian" ]; then
  gd_like_base=0
  for gd_like in ${ID_LIKE:-}; do
    [ "$gd_like" = "debian" ] && gd_like_base=1
  done
  case "${ID:-}" in debian|ubuntu) gd_like_base=0 ;; esac
  [ "$gd_like_base" = "1" ] || fail "the script was generated for Debian, detected: ${PRETTY_NAME:-${ID:-unknown}}"
  log "${PRETTY_NAME:-${ID:-unknown}} is a Debian derivative — continuing"
fi

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 1/5"
log "Installing packages (non-interactive)"
rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold update -q
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold install -yq --no-install-recommends nftables git ca-certificates curl jq

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 2/5"
log "Firewall (nftables, default-deny)"
# The drop-in directory the ruleset includes, created BEFORE the syntax
# check — `nft -c` parses the include too, and a glob that matches
# nothing is not something every nft version forgives. The placeholder
# is what guarantees at least one match; the agent writes one file PER
# SERVICE next to it (`gryonixnexus-svc-<service>.nft`) when it opens a
# port for something it installs, so removing one service's ports
# cannot close another's — the chain itself is shared, and the agent
# rebuilds it from every drop-in in one transaction (see
# NftablesConfig.agentChainName and the agent's install/firewall.rs).
install -d -m 755 /etc/nftables.d
if [ ! -f /etc/nftables.d/gryonixnexus-00-placeholder.nft ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '# Managed by gryonixNexus — keeps the include glob matching. Do not remove.' \
    > /etc/nftables.d/gryonixnexus-00-placeholder.nft
fi
backup /etc/nftables.conf
cat > /etc/nftables.conf <<'EOF_NFT'
#!/usr/sbin/nft -f
# Managed by gryonixNexus — single-server firewall (default-deny).
flush ruleset

table inet filter {
    chain input {
        type filter hook input priority filter; policy drop;
        iif "lo" accept
        ct state established,related accept
        ct state invalid drop
        meta l4proto icmp icmp type { echo-request, destination-unreachable, time-exceeded, parameter-problem } limit rate 10/second accept
        meta l4proto ipv6-icmp accept
        tcp dport 22 meter gryonixnexus_ssh_throttle4 { ip saddr timeout 60s limit rate 10/minute burst 5 packets } accept comment "SSH, per-source throttle"
        tcp dport 22 meter gryonixnexus_ssh_throttle6 { ip6 saddr timeout 60s limit rate 10/minute burst 5 packets } accept comment "SSH, per-source throttle"
        tcp dport 22 drop comment "SSH: per-source rate exceeded"
        tcp dport { 80 } accept comment "mail + HTTP for ACME"
        jump gryonixnexus_services
    }

        # Filled by the control-plane agent when it installs a service that
        # needs a port open (`flush chain` + `add rule`, never a reload of
        # this file). Empty means nothing extra is open.
        chain gryonixnexus_services {
        }    # No forward chain: Docker hooks its own drop-policy forward
    # chain with per-container accepts; a second drop-policy
    # chain here would override it and cut containers off.
}

include "/etc/nftables.d/gryonixnexus-*.nft"
EOF_NFT
nft -c -f /etc/nftables.conf
nft -f /etc/nftables.conf
systemctl enable --now nftables >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl is-active --quiet docker; then
  systemctl restart docker
fi

# **The same reason as the docker restart above, for the same flush.**
# `flush ruleset` erases EVERY table, and CrowdSec's bans live in a
# table of their own (`ip crowdsec` / `ip6 crowdsec6`, written by the
# firewall bouncer). The bouncer does not notice: its unit stays
# active, `cscli decisions list` keeps answering, and not one of those
# decisions is in the packet filter any more. 20 live decisions, no crowdsec table, silent journal —
# which is strictly worse than having no bouncer, because the dashboard
# goes on reporting a defended host. Restarting it re-creates the
# tables and re-applies what the engine holds.
if systemctl is-active --quiet crowdsec-firewall-bouncer 2>/dev/null; then
  systemctl restart crowdsec-firewall-bouncer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 3/5"
log "Intrusion defence: CrowdSec (watches ssh and Caddy, bans on the firewall)"
(
set -e
curl -fsSL https://install.crowdsec.net | sh
dpkg --configure -a --force-confdef --force-confold || true
# Engine first, in its own call: apt given both packages on one line
# has configured the bouncer first on this fleet, and its
# post-installation script could not mint itself an API key because
# the engine did not exist yet — the unit starts and talks to nothing.
apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold install -y crowdsec
apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold install -y crowdsec-firewall-bouncer-nftables

# acquis.d, not the package's own acquis.yaml: CrowdSec's supported
# directory for additional sources, so an upgrade never fights us for
# the file.
install -d -m 755 /etc/crowdsec/acquis.d
cat > /etc/crowdsec/acquis.d/gryonixnexus.yaml <<'EOF_CS_ACQUIS'
# Managed by gryonixNexus. Journald, not files: this fleet runs Debian with
# rsyslog inactive, so /var/log/auth.log does not exist and a file-based
# acquisition would parse nothing while reporting itself healthy.
source: journalctl
journalctl_filter:
 - "_SYSTEMD_UNIT=ssh.service"
 - "_SYSTEMD_UNIT=sshd.service"
labels:
 type: syslog
---
source: journalctl
journalctl_filter:
 - "_SYSTEMD_UNIT=caddy.service"
labels:
 type: caddy
EOF_CS_ACQUIS

# Move the local API off 8080 BEFORE the engine starts — see the type
# header. All three files have to agree: listen_uri moves the door,
# the other two are how cscli and the bouncer find it. Missing files
# (a postinst that has not run yet) are left alone rather than
# failing the block — the engine start below still gets the newly
# written acquisition either way.
[ -f /etc/crowdsec/config.yaml ] && \
  sed -i "s|^\( *\)listen_uri:.*|\1listen_uri: 127.0.0.1:8237|" /etc/crowdsec/config.yaml
[ -f /etc/crowdsec/local_api_credentials.yaml ] && \
  sed -i "s|^url:.*|url: http://127.0.0.1:8237|" /etc/crowdsec/local_api_credentials.yaml
[ -f /etc/crowdsec/bouncers/crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.yaml ] && \
  sed -i "s|^api_url:.*|api_url: http://127.0.0.1:8237/|" /etc/crowdsec/bouncers/crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.yaml

# --error lowers cscli's log level so an already-installed collection
# is silent; the command still succeeds, which is what makes this
# idempotent on a re-run.
cscli collections install crowdsecurity/sshd crowdsecurity/caddy crowdsecurity/linux --error || true
cscli hub update --error || true

systemctl enable --now crowdsec >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
systemctl restart crowdsec

# A key the bouncer cannot use is the same outcome as no bouncer at
# all — registered only when the config carries no real key yet, so a
# re-run does not mint a new one and restart a bouncer that already
# works.
BOUNCER_CFG=/etc/crowdsec/bouncers/crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.yaml
if [ -f "$BOUNCER_CFG" ]; then
  CURRENT_KEY="$(sed -n 's/^api_key: *//p' "$BOUNCER_CFG" | head -n1 | tr -d '"'\''')"
  if [ -z "${CURRENT_KEY:-}" ] || [ "${CURRENT_KEY:-}" = "<API_KEY>" ]; then
    cscli bouncers delete gryonixnexus-firewall-bouncer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    KEY="$(cscli bouncers add gryonixnexus-firewall-bouncer -o raw)"
    if [ -n "${KEY:-}" ]; then
      sed -i "s|^api_key:.*|api_key: $KEY|" "$BOUNCER_CFG"
    fi
  fi
  # Refused rather than repaired when the bouncer is not aimed at its
  # own table: a bouncer aimed at the table this script's own
  # `flush ruleset` firewall step rewrites would have its bans erased
  # by the next provision, with nothing on either side to say so —
  # the same refusal `bouncer_targets_its_own_table` makes.
  if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*table:[[:space:]]*"?crowdsec6?"?[[:space:]]*$' "$BOUNCER_CFG"; then
    systemctl enable --now crowdsec-firewall-bouncer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    systemctl try-restart crowdsec-firewall-bouncer || true
  fi
fi
) || echo "Intrusion defence (CrowdSec) did not finish installing — continuing without it. Everything else on this server is unaffected." >&2

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 4/5"
log "Metrics history collector (gryonixnexus-metrics)"
backup /opt/gryonixnexus-metrics-collector.sh
cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-metrics-collector.sh <<'EOF_METRICS'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — samples host metrics every 10 seconds and keeps
# downsampled history buckets as CSV files under /var/lib/gryonixnexus/metrics.
# Columns: epoch,cpu%,memUsed,memTotal,diskUsed,diskTotal,netRx/s,netTx/s,
# ioRead/s,ioWrite/s,load1,tempC. Empty field = no data for that sample.
# Power: power-<bucket>.csv, columns epoch,watts,sensor, when a sensor exists.
# Disks: disks-<bucket>.csv, columns epoch,mount,used,total, one row per filesystem.
set -euo pipefail

DIR=/var/lib/gryonixnexus/metrics
STEP=10
install -d -m 755 /var/lib/gryonixnexus "$DIR"

cpu_ticks() { awk '$1=="cpu"{t=0; for(i=2;i<=9;i++) t+=$i; print t, $5+$6; exit}' /proc/stat; }
mem_bytes() { awk '/^MemTotal:/{t=$2*1024} /^MemAvailable:/{a=$2*1024} END{print t-a, t}' /proc/meminfo; }
disk_bytes() {
  { df -B1 --output=target,size,used -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs -x overlay 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | awk 'NR>1 { if ($1=="/") {s=$2; u=$3; f=1} else if (!f && $2+0>s+0) {s=$2; u=$3} } END{print u+0, s+0}'
}
# Every real filesystem once: mount,used,total.
disk_rows() {
  { df -B1 --output=source,target,size,used -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs -x overlay -x squashfs -x efivarfs 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | awk 'NR>1 && NF==4 && $3+0>0 && $2 !~ /,/ && $2 !~ /^\/(boot|snap|run|proc|sys|dev)(\/|$)/ && !seen[$1]++ {print $2","$4","$3}'
}
net_bytes() {
  awk -F: 'NF==2 {name=$1; gsub(/[ \t]/,"",name); if (name ~ /^(lo|veth.*|docker.*|br-.*|virbr.*|wg.*|awg.*|tun.*|tap.*|tailscale.*|zt.*|cali.*|flannel.*|cni.*|ifb.*|dummy.*)$/) next;
                  split($2,a," "); rx+=a[1]; tx+=a[9]} END{print rx+0, tx+0}' /proc/net/dev
}
io_bytes() {
  awk '$3 ~ /^(sd[a-z]+|vd[a-z]+|xvd[a-z]+|hd[a-z]+|nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+|mmcblk[0-9]+)$/ \
         {r+=$6*512; w+=$10*512} END{print r+0, w+0}' /proc/diskstats
}
load_one() { awk '{print $1}' /proc/loadavg; }
temp_c() {
  { cat /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | awk '$1>0 && $1<150000 { if ($1>m) m=$1 } END{ if (m>0) printf "%.1f", m/1000 }'
}
rate() { awk -v c="$1" -v p="$2" -v s="$STEP" 'BEGIN{d=c-p; if (d<0) d=0; printf "%d", d/s}'; }

# Power sensors. Each prints watts, or nothing when absent.
POWERCAP=/sys/class/powercap
rapl_domains() {
  local d
  for d in "$POWERCAP"/intel-rapl:*; do
    case "${d##*/}" in *:*:*) continue ;; esac
    if [ -r "$d/energy_uj" ]; then echo "$d"; fi
  done
}
# Energy counter and its wrap range in microjoules; psys covers the platform.
rapl_uj() {
  local d name domains total=0 range=0
  domains=$(rapl_domains)
  [ -n "$domains" ] || return 0
  for d in $domains; do
    name=$(cat "$d/name" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ "$name" = psys ]; then domains=$d; break; fi
  done
  for d in $domains; do
    total=$(( total + $(cat "$d/energy_uj") ))
    range=$(( range + $(cat "$d/max_energy_range_uj" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))
  done
  echo "$total $range"
}
ipmi_w() {
  if [ ! -e /dev/ipmi0 ] || ! command -v ipmitool >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
  timeout 5 ipmitool dcmi power reading 2>/dev/null \
    | awk -F: '/Instantaneous power reading/ {gsub(/[^0-9.]/, "", $2); if ($2+0>0) printf "%.1f", $2; exit}'
}
hwmon_w() {
  local f name
  for f in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/power1_average /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/power1_input; do
    [ -r "$f" ] || continue
    name=$(cat "${f%/*}/name" 2>/dev/null || true)
    case "$name" in amdgpu|radeon|nouveau|i915|xe) continue ;; esac
    awk '$1>0 {printf "%.1f", $1/1000000}' "$f"
    return 0
  done
}
pi_w() {
  command -v vcgencmd >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  vcgencmd pmic_read_adc 2>/dev/null | awk '
    { key=substr($1, 1, length($1)-2); v=$2; sub(/.*=/, "", v); sub(/[AV]$/, "", v) }
    $1 ~ /_A$/ {a[key]=v}
    $1 ~ /_V$/ {u[key]=v}
    END { for (k in a) if (k in u) w+=a[k]*u[k]; if (w>0) printf "%.1f", w }'
}
ups_w() {
  command -v upsc >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  local ups
  ups=$(upsc -l 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
  [ -n "$ups" ] || return 0
  upsc "$ups" 2>/dev/null | awk -F': ' '
    /^ups.realpower:/ {r=$2} /^ups.load:/ {l=$2} /^ups.realpower.nominal:/ {n=$2}
    END { if (r>0) printf "%.1f", r; else if (l>0 && n>0) printf "%.1f", l*n/100 }'
}


# Keep only the newest <max> rows of <file>.
trim() {
  local file=$1 max=$2 lines tmp
  [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
  lines=$(wc -l < "$file")
  if [ "$lines" -gt "$(( max + max / 10 ))" ]; then
    tmp=$(mktemp "$DIR/.trim.XXXXXX")
    tail -n "$max" "$file" > "$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
    chmod 644 "$file"
  fi
}

# Average the source rows inside the just-closed <period> window and
# append one row to <target>. No-op while the window is still open, when
# it was already written, or when the source has no rows in it (gap).
aggregate() {
  local target=$1 source=$2 period=$3 keep=$4 now start last row
  [ -f "$source" ] || return 0
  now=$(date +%s)
  start=$(( now / period * period - period ))
  last=-1
  if [ -f "$target" ]; then
    last=$(tail -n 1 "$target" | cut -d, -f1)
    case "$last" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last=-1 ;; esac
  fi
  [ "$last" -lt "$start" ] || return 0
  row=$(awk -F, -v s="$start" -v e=$(( start + period )) '
    $1>=s && $1<e {
      n++
      if ($2!="") {c+=$2; cn++}
      mu+=$3; mt=$4; du+=$5; dt=$6
      if ($7!="") {rx+=$7; rxn++}
      if ($8!="") {tx+=$8; txn++}
      if ($9!="") {ir+=$9; irn++}
      if ($10!="") {iw+=$10; iwn++}
      l+=$11
      if ($12!="") {tp+=$12; tn++}
    }
    END {
      if (!n) exit 0
      printf "%d,", s
      if (cn) printf "%.1f", c/cn
      printf ",%d,%d,%d,%d,", mu/n, mt, du/n, dt
      if (rxn) printf "%d", rx/rxn
      printf ","
      if (txn) printf "%d", tx/txn
      printf ","
      if (irn) printf "%d", ir/irn
      printf ","
      if (iwn) printf "%d", iw/iwn
      printf ",%.2f,", l/n
      if (tn) printf "%.1f", tp/tn
      printf "\n"
    }' "$source")
  [ -n "$row" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$row" >> "$target"
  chmod 644 "$target"
  trim "$target" "$keep"
}


# Average watts inside the just-closed <period> window, same rules as above.
aggregate_power() {
  local target=$1 source=$2 period=$3 keep=$4 now start last row
  [ -f "$source" ] || return 0
  now=$(date +%s)
  start=$(( now / period * period - period ))
  last=-1
  if [ -f "$target" ]; then
    last=$(tail -n 1 "$target" | cut -d, -f1)
    case "$last" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last=-1 ;; esac
  fi
  [ "$last" -lt "$start" ] || return 0
  row=$(awk -F, -v s="$start" -v e=$(( start + period )) '
    $1>=s && $1<e && $2!="" {w+=$2; n++; src=$3}
    END { if (n) printf "%d,%.1f,%s\n", s, w/n, src }' "$source")
  [ -n "$row" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$row" >> "$target"
  chmod 644 "$target"
  trim "$target" "$keep"
}

# Average each filesystem inside the just-closed <period> window.
aggregate_disks() {
  local target=$1 source=$2 period=$3 keep=$4 now start last row
  [ -f "$source" ] || return 0
  now=$(date +%s)
  start=$(( now / period * period - period ))
  last=-1
  if [ -f "$target" ]; then
    last=$(tail -n 1 "$target" | cut -d, -f1)
    case "$last" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last=-1 ;; esac
  fi
  [ "$last" -lt "$start" ] || return 0
  row=$(awk -F, -v s="$start" -v e=$(( start + period )) '
    $1>=s && $1<e && NF==4 {u[$2]+=$3; t[$2]=$4; n[$2]++}
    END { for (m in n) printf "%d,%s,%d,%d\n", s, m, u[m]/n[m], t[m] }' "$source")
  [ -n "$row" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$row" >> "$target"
  chmod 644 "$target"
  trim "$target" $(( keep * 16 ))
}

prev_total=0 prev_idle=0 prev_rx=0 prev_tx=0 prev_ir=0 prev_iw=0 have_prev=0
prev_uj=0 prev_rapl_at=0 have_rapl=0

while :; do
  now=$(date +%s)
  read -r total idle < <(cpu_ticks)
  read -r mem_used mem_total < <(mem_bytes)
  read -r disk_used disk_total < <(disk_bytes)
  read -r rx tx < <(net_bytes)
  read -r io_r io_w < <(io_bytes)
  load=$(load_one)
  temp=$(temp_c)

  cpu="" rx_rate="" tx_rate="" ir_rate="" iw_rate=""
  if [ "$have_prev" -eq 1 ]; then
    cpu=$(awk -v t=$((total - prev_total)) -v i=$((idle - prev_idle)) \
      'BEGIN{ if (t>0) { p=(t-i)*100/t; if (p<0) p=0; if (p>100) p=100; printf "%.1f", p } }')
    rx_rate=$(rate "$rx" "$prev_rx")
    tx_rate=$(rate "$tx" "$prev_tx")
    ir_rate=$(rate "$io_r" "$prev_ir")
    iw_rate=$(rate "$io_w" "$prev_iw")
  fi

  printf '%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s\n' \
    "$now" "$cpu" "$mem_used" "$mem_total" "$disk_used" "$disk_total" \
    "$rx_rate" "$tx_rate" "$ir_rate" "$iw_rate" "$load" "$temp" >> "$DIR/10s.csv"
  chmod 644 "$DIR/10s.csv"
  trim "$DIR/10s.csv" 720

  power="" psrc=""
  for probe in ipmi hwmon pi; do
    power=$("${probe}_w")
    if [ -n "$power" ]; then psrc=$probe; break; fi
  done
  rapl=$(rapl_uj)
  if [ -z "$power" ] && [ -n "$rapl" ] && [ "$have_rapl" -eq 1 ]; then
    power=$(awk -v c="${rapl% *}" -v p="$prev_uj" -v r="${rapl#* }" -v s=$(( now - prev_rapl_at )) \
      'BEGIN{d=c-p; if (d<0) d+=r; if (d>0 && s>0) printf "%.1f", d/1000000/s}')
    if [ -n "$power" ]; then psrc=rapl; fi
  fi
  if [ -n "$rapl" ]; then prev_uj=${rapl% *}; prev_rapl_at=$now; have_rapl=1; fi
  if [ -z "$power" ]; then
    power=$(ups_w)
    if [ -n "$power" ]; then psrc=ups; fi
  fi
  if [ -n "$power" ]; then

    trim "$DIR/power-10s.csv" 720
  fi

  disk_rows | awk -v t="$now" '{print t","$0}' >> "$DIR/disks-10s.csv"
  chmod 644 "$DIR/disks-10s.csv"
  trim "$DIR/disks-10s.csv" $(( 720 * 16 ))

  aggregate "$DIR/1m.csv"  "$DIR/10s.csv" 60      720
  aggregate "$DIR/10m.csv" "$DIR/1m.csv"  600     432
  aggregate "$DIR/1h.csv"  "$DIR/10m.csv" 3600    336
  aggregate "$DIR/1d.csv"  "$DIR/1h.csv"  86400   400
  aggregate "$DIR/1w.csv"  "$DIR/1d.csv"  604800  260
  aggregate_power "$DIR/power-1m.csv"  "$DIR/power-10s.csv" 60      720
  aggregate_power "$DIR/power-10m.csv" "$DIR/power-1m.csv"  600     432
  aggregate_power "$DIR/power-1h.csv"  "$DIR/power-10m.csv" 3600    336
  aggregate_power "$DIR/power-1d.csv"  "$DIR/power-1h.csv"  86400   400
  aggregate_power "$DIR/power-1w.csv"  "$DIR/power-1d.csv"  604800  260
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1m.csv"  "$DIR/disks-10s.csv" 60      720
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-10m.csv" "$DIR/disks-1m.csv"  600     432
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1h.csv"  "$DIR/disks-10m.csv" 3600    336
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1d.csv"  "$DIR/disks-1h.csv"  86400   400
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1w.csv"  "$DIR/disks-1d.csv"  604800  260

  prev_total=$total prev_idle=$idle prev_rx=$rx prev_tx=$tx prev_ir=$io_r prev_iw=$io_w
  have_prev=1
  sleep "$STEP"
done
EOF_METRICS

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — VPS — точка входа: WireGuard-туннель и проброс почты на домашний сервер.
# GRYONIXNEXUS_DISTRO: debian
# Запуск: sudo bash setup-vps.sh
# Скрипт самодостаточен и идемпотентен: пакеты, конфиги (с бэкапом), firewall, сервисы — всё в одном запуске; повторный запуск безопасен.
set -euo pipefail

# Pinned, never inherited. Whatever launches this script may have
# tightened its own umask — the app's runner did, to keep the run log
# private — and a script that adopts it writes 0700 directories and
# 0600 files that only root can read. Nothing here notices (it IS
# root), but caddy, mailcow's nginx worker and every other service
# running as somebody else cannot read what was written for them.
# Secrets get an explicit chmod at the point they are created; the
# default has to stay ordinary.
umask 022

log()    { printf '\n==> %s\n' "$*"; }
fail()   { printf 'ОШИБКА: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
# Copies a changed file aside, keeping the newest five
backup() {
  [ -f "$1" ] || return 0
  local last
  last="$(ls -1d "$1".bak.* 2>/dev/null | sort | tail -n 1 || true)"
  if [ -n "$last" ] && cmp -s "$1" "$last"; then return 0; fi
  cp -a "$1" "$1.bak.$(date +%s)"
  ls -1d "$1".bak.* | sort | head -n -5 | xargs -r rm -f
}
# Retry a flaky command a few times with a linear backoff. Fresh servers
# pull many large images at once (mailcow alone is ~15), and a single
# transient registry error/timeout would otherwise abort the whole run
# under `set -e` — the user then had to hit Retry by hand. The setup is
# idempotent, so a re-pull just resumes cached layers.
retry()  {
  local tries="$1"; shift
  local i=1
  while true; do
    "$@" && return 0
    if [ "$i" -ge "$tries" ]; then return 1; fi
    printf '\n(retry %d/%d) %s\n' "$i" "$tries" "$*" >&2
    sleep $((i * 5))
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
}

[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || fail "нужны права root: sudo bash $0"

# Дистрибутив зафиксирован при генерации в приложении — только сверяем.
# The path is a variable so the check can be exercised against a stub
# file — the alternative was a test that runs a doctored copy of this
# block and proves nothing about the artifact that ships. It is not a
# privilege boundary: the script already runs as root.
gd_os_release="${GRYONIXNEXUS_OS_RELEASE:-/etc/os-release}"

. "$gd_os_release"

# ID_LIKE and behaves like it for apt and systemd, so it is accepted.
# A distribution we support in its OWN right never passes as another
# one: Ubuntu lists debian in ID_LIKE, and letting that through would
# silently install with the wrong profile instead of saying so.
if [ "${ID:-}" != "debian" ]; then

# port for something it installs, so removing one service's ports

cat > /etc/nftables.conf <<'EOF_NFT'
#!/usr/sbin/nft -f
# Managed by gryonixNexus — VPS relay: firewall + DNAT of mail ports into the tunnel.
# The public interface is detected automatically by the setup script.
define pub_if = "@PUB_IF@"
define home_ip = 10.8.0.2
define vps_public = 203.0.113.10
# Distinct SNAT source for hairpinned VPN-client traffic (see
# postrouting): kept apart from the relay masquerade so the home
# admin guard can allow VPN clients while blocking public visitors.
define hairpin_src = 10.8.0.254

flush ruleset

table inet filter {
    chain input {
        type filter hook input priority filter; policy drop;
        iif "lo" accept
        ct state established,related accept
        ct state invalid drop
        meta l4proto icmp icmp type { echo-request, destination-unreachable, time-exceeded, parameter-problem } limit rate 10/second accept
        meta l4proto ipv6-icmp accept
        tcp dport 22 meter gryonixnexus_ssh_throttle4 { ip saddr timeout 60s limit rate 10/minute burst 5 packets } accept comment "SSH, per-source throttle"
        tcp dport 22 meter gryonixnexus_ssh_throttle6 { ip6 saddr timeout 60s limit rate 10/minute burst 5 packets } accept comment "SSH, per-source throttle"
        tcp dport 22 drop comment "SSH: per-source rate exceeded"
        udp dport 51820 accept comment "WireGuard"
        # Mail ports are NOT accepted on input: the traffic is
        # DNATed and passes only through the forward chain.
        jump gryonixnexus_services
    }

    # MSS clamping, and it is not an optimisation — without it a
    # relayed HTTPS connection completes its TCP handshake and then
    # HANGS. The client's TLS ClientHello arrived at
    # sequence 1449 with the first 1448 bytes missing, and the home node
    # answered with a SACK naming the hole. A public client sizes its
    # segments for ITS OWN path (mss 1460) and knows nothing about a
    # 1420-byte tunnel in the middle, so every full-size segment falls
    # into an MTU black hole. Nothing earlier caught it because
    # everything tested through this relay until then was small: an
    # ACME challenge, an SMTP handshake, a short message.
    #
    # Both directions, because both ends size their own segments: the
    # client's SYN is clamped on its way OUT through the tunnel, and the
    # home node's SYN-ACK on its way in. `rt mtu` is the route's own MTU,
    # so the number is never hardcoded.
    #
    # Its own chain at mangle priority: the filter chain below runs at
    # `filter` priority and its accept/drop verdicts would end traversal
    # before an option rewrite could happen.
    chain mangle_forward {
        type filter hook forward priority mangle; policy accept;
        oifname "wg0" tcp flags syn tcp option maxseg size set rt mtu
        iifname "wg0" tcp flags syn tcp option maxseg size set rt mtu
    }

    chain forward {
        # policy ACCEPT, and every drop below names an interface.
        # nftables hands the packet to EVERY chain hooked at forward
        # and one drop verdict anywhere is final, so a drop policy
        # here also vetoes the per-container accepts Docker keeps in
        # its own tables: containers on this host lose the network
        # entirely (no pulls, no outbound) while the host itself is
        # fine — it reads as "Docker is broken", not as "the firewall
        # did this". The other rulesets solve that by declaring no
        # forward chain at all; the relay cannot, its forward rules
        # ARE the relay. So the default is inverted instead and
        # default-deny is spelled out for the paths this host routes:
        # anything touching the tunnel, and routing between public
        # interfaces. Traffic we do not own falls through to whoever
        # else is hooked here — on a Docker host, Docker's own chain.
        type filter hook forward priority filter; policy accept;
        iifname "wg0" ct state invalid drop
        oifname "wg0" ct state invalid drop
        ct state established,related accept
        # Inbound mail/HTTP DNATed to the home node.
        iifname $pub_if oifname "wg0" ip daddr $home_ip tcp dport { 25, 80, 143, 443, 465, 587, 993, 4190 } accept
        # Hairpinned tunnel traffic to the deployment's own sites —
        # DNATed back into the tunnel, so both interfaces are wg0.
        iifname "wg0" oifname "wg0" ip daddr $home_ip tcp dport { 25, 80, 143, 443, 465, 587, 993, 4190 } accept
        # Traffic initiated by the home node (outgoing mail,
        # updates in full-tunnel mode) — out through the VPS.
        iifname "wg0" oifname $pub_if accept
        # The default-deny the policy used to provide, restated for
        # the two paths that need it: nothing else enters or leaves
        # the tunnel, and the relay is not an open router between
        # public interfaces. Docker's bridges are named in neither,
        # which is exactly the point — no interface list to go stale.
        iifname "wg0" drop
        oifname "wg0" drop
        iifname $pub_if oifname $pub_if drop
    }

        # Filled by the control-plane agent when it installs a service that
        # needs a port open (`flush chain` + `add rule`, never a reload of
        # this file). Empty means nothing extra is open.
        chain gryonixnexus_services {
        }
}

table ip nat {
    chain prerouting {
        type nat hook prerouting priority dstnat;
        iifname $pub_if tcp dport { 25, 80, 143, 443, 465, 587, 993, 4190 } dnat to $home_ip
        iifname "wg0" ip daddr $vps_public tcp dport { 25, 80, 143, 443, 465, 587, 993, 4190 } dnat to $home_ip
    }
    chain output {
        type nat hook output priority dstnat;
        # This relay reaching its own forwarded sites
        ip daddr $vps_public tcp dport { 25, 80, 143, 443, 465, 587, 993, 4190 } dnat to $home_ip
    }
    chain postrouting {
        type nat hook postrouting priority srcnat;
        # Hairpin VPN-client flows (in on wg0, DNATed back out
        # wg0) get a DISTINCT source so the home admin guard can
        # tell them apart from relayed PUBLIC traffic. Both otherwise
        # masquerade to the same VPS tunnel address, and the guard —
        # which sees only the L3 source — could not distinguish a VPN
        # client from a public visitor, so "VPN-only" blocked everyone.
        # First matching NAT wins, so this precedes the masquerade.
        iifname "wg0" oifname "wg0" ip daddr $home_ip snat to $hairpin_src
        # Relayed public traffic is deliberately left un-NATed here:
        # DNAT alone survives the round trip (conntrack un-DNATs the
        # reply automatically on its way back out $pub_if), so the
        # real client IP rides all the way to home instead of being
        # collapsed into this relay's tunnel address. See homeRuleset
        # and RelayRouteSyncSections for the other half — home has to
        # route the reply back through the tunnel itself, since a
        # foreign public source address is not something its main
        # routing table sends to wg0 by default.
        # Tunnel traffic egressing to the internet: mail leaves
        # from the VPS public IP (matching PTR/SPF).
        oifname $pub_if ip saddr 10.8.0.0/24 masquerade
        oifname "wg0" ip saddr $vps_public masquerade
    }
}

EOF_NFT

# `flush ruleset` erases EVERY table, and CrowdSec's bans live in a

# firewall bouncer). The bouncer does not notice: its unit stays
# active, `cscli decisions list` keeps answering, and not one of those
# decisions is in the packet filter any more. 20 live decisions, no crowdsec table, silent journal —
# which is strictly worse than having no bouncer, because the dashboard
# goes on reporting a defended host. Restarting it re-creates the

dpkg --configure -a --force-confdef --force-confold || true

# post-installation script could not mint itself an API key because
# the engine did not exist yet — the unit starts and talks to nothing.
apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold install -y crowdsec

# rsyslog inactive, so /var/log/auth.log does not exist and a file-based
# acquisition would parse nothing while reporting itself healthy.
source: journalctl

 - "_SYSTEMD_UNIT=ssh.service"
 - "_SYSTEMD_UNIT=sshd.service"

---

  # own table: a bouncer aimed at the table this script's own
  # `flush ruleset` firewall step rewrites would have its bans erased
  # by the next provision, with nothing on either side to say so —

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — samples host metrics every 10 seconds and keeps
# downsampled history buckets as CSV files under /var/lib/gryonixnexus/metrics.
# Columns: epoch,cpu%,memUsed,memTotal,diskUsed,diskTotal,netRx/s,netTx/s,
# ioRead/s,ioWrite/s,load1,tempC. Empty field = no data for that sample.
# Power: power-<bucket>.csv, columns epoch,watts,sensor, when a sensor exists.
# Disks: disks-<bucket>.csv, columns epoch,mount,used,total, one row per filesystem.
set -euo pipefail

DIR=/var/lib/gryonixnexus/metrics
STEP=10
install -d -m 755 /var/lib/gryonixnexus "$DIR"

cpu_ticks() { awk '$1=="cpu"{t=0; for(i=2;i<=9;i++) t+=$i; print t, $5+$6; exit}' /proc/stat; }
mem_bytes() { awk '/^MemTotal:/{t=$2*1024} /^MemAvailable:/{a=$2*1024} END{print t-a, t}' /proc/meminfo; }
disk_bytes() {
  { df -B1 --output=target,size,used -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs -x overlay 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | awk 'NR>1 { if ($1=="/") {s=$2; u=$3; f=1} else if (!f && $2+0>s+0) {s=$2; u=$3} } END{print u+0, s+0}'
}
# Every real filesystem once: mount,used,total.
disk_rows() {
  { df -B1 --output=source,target,size,used -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs -x overlay -x squashfs -x efivarfs 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | awk 'NR>1 && NF==4 && $3+0>0 && $2 !~ /,/ && $2 !~ /^\/(boot|snap|run|proc|sys|dev)(\/|$)/ && !seen[$1]++ {print $2","$4","$3}'
}
net_bytes() {
  awk -F: 'NF==2 {name=$1; gsub(/[ \t]/,"",name); if (name ~ /^(lo|veth.*|docker.*|br-.*|virbr.*|wg.*|awg.*|tun.*|tap.*|tailscale.*|zt.*|cali.*|flannel.*|cni.*|ifb.*|dummy.*)$/) next;
                  split($2,a," "); rx+=a[1]; tx+=a[9]} END{print rx+0, tx+0}' /proc/net/dev
}
io_bytes() {
  awk '$3 ~ /^(sd[a-z]+|vd[a-z]+|xvd[a-z]+|hd[a-z]+|nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+|mmcblk[0-9]+)$/ \
         {r+=$6*512; w+=$10*512} END{print r+0, w+0}' /proc/diskstats
}
load_one() { awk '{print $1}' /proc/loadavg; }
temp_c() {
  { cat /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | awk '$1>0 && $1<150000 { if ($1>m) m=$1 } END{ if (m>0) printf "%.1f", m/1000 }'
}
rate() { awk -v c="$1" -v p="$2" -v s="$STEP" 'BEGIN{d=c-p; if (d<0) d=0; printf "%d", d/s}'; }

# Power sensors. Each prints watts, or nothing when absent.
POWERCAP=/sys/class/powercap
rapl_domains() {
  local d
  for d in "$POWERCAP"/intel-rapl:*; do
    case "${d##*/}" in *:*:*) continue ;; esac
    if [ -r "$d/energy_uj" ]; then echo "$d"; fi
  done
}
# Energy counter and its wrap range in microjoules; psys covers the platform.
rapl_uj() {
  local d name domains total=0 range=0
  domains=$(rapl_domains)
  [ -n "$domains" ] || return 0
  for d in $domains; do
    name=$(cat "$d/name" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ "$name" = psys ]; then domains=$d; break; fi
  done
  for d in $domains; do
    total=$(( total + $(cat "$d/energy_uj") ))
    range=$(( range + $(cat "$d/max_energy_range_uj" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))
  done
  echo "$total $range"
}
ipmi_w() {
  if [ ! -e /dev/ipmi0 ] || ! command -v ipmitool >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
  timeout 5 ipmitool dcmi power reading 2>/dev/null \
    | awk -F: '/Instantaneous power reading/ {gsub(/[^0-9.]/, "", $2); if ($2+0>0) printf "%.1f", $2; exit}'
}
hwmon_w() {
  local f name
  for f in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/power1_average /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/power1_input; do
    [ -r "$f" ] || continue
    name=$(cat "${f%/*}/name" 2>/dev/null || true)
    case "$name" in amdgpu|radeon|nouveau|i915|xe) continue ;; esac
    awk '$1>0 {printf "%.1f", $1/1000000}' "$f"
    return 0
  done
}
pi_w() {
  command -v vcgencmd >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  vcgencmd pmic_read_adc 2>/dev/null | awk '
    { key=substr($1, 1, length($1)-2); v=$2; sub(/.*=/, "", v); sub(/[AV]$/, "", v) }
    $1 ~ /_A$/ {a[key]=v}
    $1 ~ /_V$/ {u[key]=v}
    END { for (k in a) if (k in u) w+=a[k]*u[k]; if (w>0) printf "%.1f", w }'
}
ups_w() {
  command -v upsc >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  local ups
  ups=$(upsc -l 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
  [ -n "$ups" ] || return 0
  upsc "$ups" 2>/dev/null | awk -F': ' '
    /^ups.realpower:/ {r=$2} /^ups.load:/ {l=$2} /^ups.realpower.nominal:/ {n=$2}
    END { if (r>0) printf "%.1f", r; else if (l>0 && n>0) printf "%.1f", l*n/100 }'
}


# Keep only the newest <max> rows of <file>.
trim() {
  local file=$1 max=$2 lines tmp
  [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
  lines=$(wc -l < "$file")
  if [ "$lines" -gt "$(( max + max / 10 ))" ]; then
    tmp=$(mktemp "$DIR/.trim.XXXXXX")
    tail -n "$max" "$file" > "$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
    chmod 644 "$file"
  fi
}

# Average the source rows inside the just-closed <period> window and
# append one row to <target>. No-op while the window is still open, when
# it was already written, or when the source has no rows in it (gap).
aggregate() {
  local target=$1 source=$2 period=$3 keep=$4 now start last row
  [ -f "$source" ] || return 0
  now=$(date +%s)
  start=$(( now / period * period - period ))
  last=-1
  if [ -f "$target" ]; then
    last=$(tail -n 1 "$target" | cut -d, -f1)
    case "$last" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last=-1 ;; esac
  fi
  [ "$last" -lt "$start" ] || return 0
  row=$(awk -F, -v s="$start" -v e=$(( start + period )) '
    $1>=s && $1<e {
      n++
      if ($2!="") {c+=$2; cn++}
      mu+=$3; mt=$4; du+=$5; dt=$6
      if ($7!="") {rx+=$7; rxn++}
      if ($8!="") {tx+=$8; txn++}
      if ($9!="") {ir+=$9; irn++}
      if ($10!="") {iw+=$10; iwn++}
      l+=$11
      if ($12!="") {tp+=$12; tn++}
    }
    END {
      if (!n) exit 0
      printf "%d,", s
      if (cn) printf "%.1f", c/cn
      printf ",%d,%d,%d,%d,", mu/n, mt, du/n, dt
      if (rxn) printf "%d", rx/rxn
      printf ","
      if (txn) printf "%d", tx/txn
      printf ","
      if (irn) printf "%d", ir/irn
      printf ","
      if (iwn) printf "%d", iw/iwn
      printf ",%.2f,", l/n
      if (tn) printf "%.1f", tp/tn
      printf "\n"
    }' "$source")
  [ -n "$row" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$row" >> "$target"
  chmod 644 "$target"
  trim "$target" "$keep"
}


# Average watts inside the just-closed <period> window, same rules as above.
aggregate_power() {
  local target=$1 source=$2 period=$3 keep=$4 now start last row
  [ -f "$source" ] || return 0
  now=$(date +%s)
  start=$(( now / period * period - period ))
  last=-1
  if [ -f "$target" ]; then
    last=$(tail -n 1 "$target" | cut -d, -f1)
    case "$last" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last=-1 ;; esac
  fi
  [ "$last" -lt "$start" ] || return 0
  row=$(awk -F, -v s="$start" -v e=$(( start + period )) '
    $1>=s && $1<e && $2!="" {w+=$2; n++; src=$3}
    END { if (n) printf "%d,%.1f,%s\n", s, w/n, src }' "$source")
  [ -n "$row" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$row" >> "$target"
  chmod 644 "$target"
  trim "$target" "$keep"
}

# Average each filesystem inside the just-closed <period> window.
aggregate_disks() {
  local target=$1 source=$2 period=$3 keep=$4 now start last row
  [ -f "$source" ] || return 0
  now=$(date +%s)
  start=$(( now / period * period - period ))
  last=-1
  if [ -f "$target" ]; then
    last=$(tail -n 1 "$target" | cut -d, -f1)
    case "$last" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last=-1 ;; esac
  fi
  [ "$last" -lt "$start" ] || return 0
  row=$(awk -F, -v s="$start" -v e=$(( start + period )) '
    $1>=s && $1<e && NF==4 {u[$2]+=$3; t[$2]=$4; n[$2]++}
    END { for (m in n) printf "%d,%s,%d,%d\n", s, m, u[m]/n[m], t[m] }' "$source")
  [ -n "$row" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$row" >> "$target"
  chmod 644 "$target"
  trim "$target" $(( keep * 16 ))
}

prev_total=0 prev_idle=0 prev_rx=0 prev_tx=0 prev_ir=0 prev_iw=0 have_prev=0
prev_uj=0 prev_rapl_at=0 have_rapl=0

while :; do
  now=$(date +%s)
  read -r total idle < <(cpu_ticks)
  read -r mem_used mem_total < <(mem_bytes)
  read -r disk_used disk_total < <(disk_bytes)
  read -r rx tx < <(net_bytes)
  read -r io_r io_w < <(io_bytes)
  load=$(load_one)
  temp=$(temp_c)

  cpu="" rx_rate="" tx_rate="" ir_rate="" iw_rate=""
  if [ "$have_prev" -eq 1 ]; then
    cpu=$(awk -v t=$((total - prev_total)) -v i=$((idle - prev_idle)) \
      'BEGIN{ if (t>0) { p=(t-i)*100/t; if (p<0) p=0; if (p>100) p=100; printf "%.1f", p } }')
    rx_rate=$(rate "$rx" "$prev_rx")
    tx_rate=$(rate "$tx" "$prev_tx")
    ir_rate=$(rate "$io_r" "$prev_ir")
    iw_rate=$(rate "$io_w" "$prev_iw")
  fi

  printf '%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s\n' \
    "$now" "$cpu" "$mem_used" "$mem_total" "$disk_used" "$disk_total" \
    "$rx_rate" "$tx_rate" "$ir_rate" "$iw_rate" "$load" "$temp" >> "$DIR/10s.csv"
  chmod 644 "$DIR/10s.csv"
  trim "$DIR/10s.csv" 720

  power="" psrc=""
  for probe in ipmi hwmon pi; do
    power=$("${probe}_w")
    if [ -n "$power" ]; then psrc=$probe; break; fi
  done
  rapl=$(rapl_uj)
  if [ -z "$power" ] && [ -n "$rapl" ] && [ "$have_rapl" -eq 1 ]; then
    power=$(awk -v c="${rapl% *}" -v p="$prev_uj" -v r="${rapl#* }" -v s=$(( now - prev_rapl_at )) \
      'BEGIN{d=c-p; if (d<0) d+=r; if (d>0 && s>0) printf "%.1f", d/1000000/s}')
    if [ -n "$power" ]; then psrc=rapl; fi
  fi
  if [ -n "$rapl" ]; then prev_uj=${rapl% *}; prev_rapl_at=$now; have_rapl=1; fi
  if [ -z "$power" ]; then
    power=$(ups_w)
    if [ -n "$power" ]; then psrc=ups; fi
  fi
  if [ -n "$power" ]; then
    printf '%s,%s,%s\n' "$now" "$power" "$psrc" >> "$DIR/power-10s.csv"
    chmod 644 "$DIR/power-10s.csv"
    trim "$DIR/power-10s.csv" 720
  fi

  disk_rows | awk -v t="$now" '{print t","$0}' >> "$DIR/disks-10s.csv"
  chmod 644 "$DIR/disks-10s.csv"
  trim "$DIR/disks-10s.csv" $(( 720 * 16 ))

  aggregate "$DIR/1m.csv"  "$DIR/10s.csv" 60      720
  aggregate "$DIR/10m.csv" "$DIR/1m.csv"  600     432
  aggregate "$DIR/1h.csv"  "$DIR/10m.csv" 3600    336
  aggregate "$DIR/1d.csv"  "$DIR/1h.csv"  86400   400
  aggregate "$DIR/1w.csv"  "$DIR/1d.csv"  604800  260
  aggregate_power "$DIR/power-1m.csv"  "$DIR/power-10s.csv" 60      720
  aggregate_power "$DIR/power-10m.csv" "$DIR/power-1m.csv"  600     432
  aggregate_power "$DIR/power-1h.csv"  "$DIR/power-10m.csv" 3600    336
  aggregate_power "$DIR/power-1d.csv"  "$DIR/power-1h.csv"  86400   400
  aggregate_power "$DIR/power-1w.csv"  "$DIR/power-1d.csv"  604800  260
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1m.csv"  "$DIR/disks-10s.csv" 60      720
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-10m.csv" "$DIR/disks-1m.csv"  600     432
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1h.csv"  "$DIR/disks-10m.csv" 3600    336
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1d.csv"  "$DIR/disks-1h.csv"  86400   400
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1w.csv"  "$DIR/disks-1d.csv"  604800  260

  prev_total=$total prev_idle=$idle prev_rx=$rx prev_tx=$tx prev_ir=$io_r prev_iw=$io_w
  have_prev=1
  sleep "$STEP"
done
EOF_METRICS
chmod 755 /opt/gryonixnexus-metrics-collector.sh
backup /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-metrics.service

set -euo pipefail

# tightened its own umask — the app's runner did, to keep the run log
# private — and a script that adopts it writes 0700 directories and
# 0600 files that only root can read. Nothing here notices (it IS
# root), but caddy, mailcow's nginx worker and every other service
# running as somebody else cannot read what was written for them.
# Secrets get an explicit chmod at the point they are created; the
# default has to stay ordinary.

log()    { printf '\n==> %s\n' "$*"; }
fail()   { printf 'ОШИБКА: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

backup() {
  [ -f "$1" ] || return 0

  last="$(ls -1d "$1".bak.* 2>/dev/null | sort | tail -n 1 || true)"
  if [ -n "$last" ] && cmp -s "$1" "$last"; then return 0; fi
  cp -a "$1" "$1.bak.$(date +%s)"
  ls -1d "$1".bak.* | sort | head -n -5 | xargs -r rm -f

# pull many large images at once (mailcow alone is ~15), and a single
# transient registry error/timeout would otherwise abort the whole run
# under `set -e` — the user then had to hit Retry by hand. The setup is
# idempotent, so a re-pull just resumes cached layers.
retry()  {
  local tries="$1"; shift
  local i=1
  while true; do
    "$@" && return 0
    if [ "$i" -ge "$tries" ]; then return 1; fi
    printf '\n(retry %d/%d) %s\n' "$i" "$tries" "$*" >&2
    sleep $((i * 5))
    i=$((i + 1))
  done

# The tables are read straight out of /proc rather than through `ss`:
# `ss` is not installed on every image, this section runs BEFORE the

# with no process behind it — it appears in /proc/net/udp and in no

# established socket owns its own pair, not the port. UDP counts only
# when unconnected (remote port 0000), so an in-flight outbound flow
# that happened to pick one of these numbers is not called a listener.
gd_pp_rows() {

        if (proto == "tcp") { if ($4 != "0A") next }
        else { split($3, r, ":"); if (r[2] != "0000") next }

# v6 address cannot collide with the v4 mappings this catalog
# publishes, and guessing about dual-stack sockets would make the check
# red on healthy hosts.
gd_pp_addr() {
  case "${#1}" in
    8)
      if [ "$1" = "00000000" ]; then printf '0.0.0.0'; return 0; fi
      printf '%d.%d.%d.%d' "$((16#${1:6:2}))" "$((16#${1:4:2}))" "$((16#${1:2:2}))" "$((16#${1:0:2}))"

    32)
      case "$1" in
        *[!0]*) printf 'skip' ;;
        *)      printf '0.0.0.0' ;;

    *) printf 'skip' ;;

# `<project>|<container>` of whoever published this port, or nothing.
# Only mappings with `->` are published on the host; a bare `443/tcp`
# is merely EXPOSED by the image and holds nothing.
gd_pp_docker_holder() {
  printf '%s\n' "$GD_PP_DOCKER" | awk -F'|' -v want_port="$1" -v want_proto="$2" '
    NF >= 3 {
      n = split($3, maps, ",")
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        m = maps[i]; gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", m)
        if (m !~ /->/) continue
        split(m, sides, "->")
        host = sides[1]; container = sides[2]
        proto = (container ~ /\/udp$/) ? "udp" : "tcp"
        if (proto != want_proto) continue
        # The number after the LAST colon, so the colons inside an
        # IPv6 literal cannot confuse it. No apostrophe may appear in
        # this comment: the awk program is one single-quoted shell
        # word, and an apostrophe ends it — shellcheck over the dumped
        # artifacts is what caught that.
        k = split(host, hp, ":")
        if (hp[k] != want_port) continue
        print $1 "|" $2
        exit
      }
    }'
}

# Is this mapping already bound? **The address half decides.** Every
# Debian/Ubuntu host answers DNS on 127.0.0.53:53 and 127.0.0.54:53
# (systemd-resolved), while the filters in this catalog publish
# 127.0.0.1:53 — a check that compared port numbers alone would refuse
# to install on every healthy machine in the fleet. Two different
# specific addresses coexist; a wildcard on either side collides with
# anything.
gd_pp_bound() {
  case "$3" in
    *" $1:$2 "*)       return 0 ;;
    *" 0.0.0.0:$2 "*)  return 0 ;;
  esac
  if [ "$1" = "0.0.0.0" ]; then
    case "$3" in *":$2 "*) return 0 ;; esac
  fi
  return 1
}

GD_PP_CONFLICTS=""
while IFS='|' read -r GD_PP_ADDR GD_PP_PORT GD_PP_PROTO GD_PP_PROJECT GD_PP_NAME; do
  [ -n "${GD_PP_PORT:-}" ] || continue
  GD_PP_HOLDER="$(gd_pp_docker_holder "$GD_PP_PORT" "$GD_PP_PROTO")"
  # Our own container holding the port is what a re-install looks like
  # from here, and it is not a conflict. The project name comes from
  # docker's own label, never from a name derived from the request.
  if [ -n "$GD_PP_HOLDER" ] && [ "${GD_PP_HOLDER%%|*}" = "$GD_PP_PROJECT" ]; then continue; fi
  if [ "$GD_PP_PROTO" = tcp ]; then GD_PP_HELD="$GD_PP_HELD_TCP"; else GD_PP_HELD="$GD_PP_HELD_UDP"; fi
  if [ -z "$GD_PP_HOLDER" ] && ! gd_pp_bound "$GD_PP_ADDR" "$GD_PP_PORT" "$GD_PP_HELD"; then continue; fi
  if [ -n "$GD_PP_HOLDER" ]; then
    GD_PP_LINE="$GD_PP_NAME: порт $GD_PP_PORT/$GD_PP_PROTO уже занят контейнером «${GD_PP_HOLDER##*|}» (compose-проект «${GD_PP_HOLDER%%|*}»)"
  else
    GD_PP_LINE="$GD_PP_NAME: порт $GD_PP_PORT/$GD_PP_PROTO уже занят чем-то другим на этом сервере"
  fi
  GD_PP_CONFLICTS="$GD_PP_CONFLICTS
  $GD_PP_LINE"
done <<'EOF_GD_PORTS'
0.0.0.0|25|tcp|mailcowdockerized|Mailcow
0.0.0.0|465|tcp|mailcowdockerized|Mailcow
0.0.0.0|587|tcp|mailcowdockerized|Mailcow
0.0.0.0|143|tcp|mailcowdockerized|Mailcow
0.0.0.0|993|tcp|mailcowdockerized|Mailcow
0.0.0.0|4190|tcp|mailcowdockerized|Mailcow
EOF_GD_PORTS

if [ -n "$GD_PP_CONFLICTS" ]; then
  echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_PORTS_IN_USE"
  fail "эти порты уже заняты на этом сервере, поэтому ничего не установлено:$GD_PP_CONFLICTS

Освободите их — или удалите сервис, который их держит — и запустите скрипт снова.

Если один из них — сам сервис, уже поставленный на эту машину вручную: gryonixNexus не подхватывает установку, которую делал не он. Сделайте бэкап его данных, удалите его и поставьте заново из приложения."
fi

# Did the container that just came up actually GET its ports?
#
# **`docker compose up -d` answers 0 for a container that is already
# running without them.** The
# first run died when `up -d` could not bind 127.0.0.1:53; the firewall
# section of the next run restarted docker, the daemon brought that
# container back up with NO published ports at all, and the re-run's
# `up -d` then found it running, changed nothing and reported success.
# Everything after that — the readiness wait, the Caddy site, the
# credentials in the report — was about a service that did not exist.
#
# A few tries rather than one: `docker ps` right after `up -d` can
# still be a moment behind, and a false "the ports are missing" would
# abort a healthy install, which is the more expensive way to be wrong.
gd_pp_verify() {
  gd_v_project="$1"; gd_v_wanted="$2"; gd_v_name="$3"
  gd_v_try=0
  while [ "$gd_v_try" -lt 5 ]; do
    gd_v_live="$(docker ps --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=$gd_v_project" --format '{{.Ports}}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
    gd_v_missing=""
    for gd_v_map in $gd_v_wanted; do
      gd_v_proto="${gd_v_map##*/}"
      gd_v_port="${gd_v_map%/*}"; gd_v_port="${gd_v_port##*:}"
      case "$gd_v_live" in
        *":$gd_v_port->"*"/$gd_v_proto"*) ;;
        *) gd_v_missing="$gd_v_missing $gd_v_port/$gd_v_proto" ;;
      esac
    done
    [ -n "$gd_v_missing" ] || return 0
    gd_v_missing="${gd_v_missing# }"
    gd_v_try=$((gd_v_try + 1))
    sleep 2
  done
  fail "$gd_v_name запустился, но без нужных ему портов ($gd_v_missing) — их занял кто-то другой на этом сервере. Установка остановлена здесь: всё дальнейшее описывало бы сервис, который не может ответить."
}

# The other way a started service is no service: it holds its ports
# and keeps dying.
#
# The question asked is "did it ever HOLD STILL", not "is it restarting
# right now". The second was tried first and has a blind spot big enough
# to drive the original defect through: a container that runs four
# seconds and dies, for ever, reads `running` on almost every sample,
# because running is most of its cycle. What it never does is stop
# moving. The passing condition is therefore something OBSERVED — a
# watch that ends without having seen the service hold still has not
# seen it work.
#
# A healthy service pays one floor's worth: three quiet looks and it is
# released, so the ordinary cost is fifteen seconds rather than the whole
# window. Immich is the case this must not fail — its server restarts
# once while the database initialises and then holds, which is quiet well
# inside the window.
gd_pp_settled() {
  gd_s_project="$1"; gd_s_name="$2"
  gd_s_ids="$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=$gd_s_project" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  [ -n "$gd_s_ids" ] || return 0
  gd_s_base=""
  gd_s_quiet=0
  gd_s_try=0
  while [ "$gd_s_try" -lt 12 ]; do
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    gd_s_now="$(docker inspect --format '{{.Name}} {{.RestartCount}} {{.State.Status}}' $gd_s_ids 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$gd_s_now" in
      *" restarting"*) gd_s_moving=1 ;;
      "") gd_s_moving=1 ;;
      *) gd_s_moving=0 ;;
    esac
    if [ "$gd_s_moving" = "0" ] && [ "$gd_s_now" = "$gd_s_base" ]; then
      gd_s_quiet=$((gd_s_quiet + 1))
      [ "$gd_s_quiet" -lt 3 ] || return 0
    else
      gd_s_base="$gd_s_now"
      gd_s_quiet=0
    fi
    gd_s_try=$((gd_s_try + 1))
    sleep 5
  done
  fail "$gd_s_name так и не успокоился: за 60 секунд он перезапускался снова и снова вместо того, чтобы остаться поднятым. Порты при этом опубликованы, поэтому больше ничто этого бы не заметило; установка остановлена здесь, чтобы не описывать сервис, который ни разу не работал."
}

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 3/15"
log "Установка пакетов (неинтерактивно)"
rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold update -q
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold install -yq --no-install-recommends nftables git ca-certificates curl jq wireguard wireguard-tools

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 4/15"

backup /etc/sysctl.d/99-gryonixnexus-rpfilter.conf
cat > /etc/sysctl.d/99-gryonixnexus-rpfilter.conf <<'EOF_SYSCTL'
# Managed by gryonixNexus — loose rp_filter: relayed traffic arrives with a
# foreign source IP (the real public visitor, not a tunnel peer), which
# strict reverse-path filtering would otherwise drop as spoofed.
net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 2
net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter = 2
EOF_SYSCTL
sysctl --system >/dev/null

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 5/15"
log "Firewall (nftables, default-deny)"
# The drop-in directory the ruleset includes, created BEFORE the syntax
# check — `nft -c` parses the include too, and a glob that matches
# nothing is not something every nft version forgives. The placeholder
# is what guarantees at least one match; the agent writes one file PER
# SERVICE next to it (`gryonixnexus-svc-<service>.nft`) when it opens a
# port for something it installs, so removing one service's ports
# cannot close another's — the chain itself is shared, and the agent
# rebuilds it from every drop-in in one transaction (see
# NftablesConfig.agentChainName and the agent's install/firewall.rs).
install -d -m 755 /etc/nftables.d
if [ ! -f /etc/nftables.d/gryonixnexus-00-placeholder.nft ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '# Managed by gryonixNexus — keeps the include glob matching. Do not remove.' \
    > /etc/nftables.d/gryonixnexus-00-placeholder.nft
fi
backup /etc/nftables.conf
cat > /etc/nftables.conf <<'EOF_NFT'
#!/usr/sbin/nft -f
# Managed by gryonixNexus — home-server firewall (default-deny).
# Mail ports are reachable ONLY from the WireGuard tunnel (from the VPS).
flush ruleset

table inet filter {
    chain input {
        type filter hook input priority filter; policy drop;
        iif "lo" accept
        ct state established,related accept
        ct state invalid drop
        meta l4proto icmp icmp type { echo-request, destination-unreachable, time-exceeded, parameter-problem } limit rate 10/second accept
        meta l4proto ipv6-icmp accept
        # SSH: throttled per source below rather than flatly accepted
        # (a flood that never fails an auth never gets a CrowdSec
        # ban — see `sshThrottle`). To narrow it to your LAN instead:
        # ip saddr 192.168.1.0/24 tcp dport 22 accept
        tcp dport 22 meter gryonixnexus_ssh_throttle4 { ip saddr timeout 60s limit rate 10/minute burst 5 packets } accept comment "SSH, per-source throttle"
        tcp dport 22 meter gryonixnexus_ssh_throttle6 { ip6 saddr timeout 60s limit rate 10/minute burst 5 packets } accept comment "SSH, per-source throttle"
        tcp dport 22 drop comment "SSH: per-source rate exceeded"
        iifname "wg0" tcp dport { 25, 80, 143, 443, 465, 587, 993, 4190 } accept comment "mail from the tunnel"
        jump gryonixnexus_services
    }

    chain prerouting {
        type filter hook prerouting priority mangle; policy accept;
        # New connections arriving from the relay get a mark so their
        # replies route back through the tunnel instead of the home
        # ISP's default gateway — real public client IPs are outside
        # 10.8.0.0/24, so nothing routes them back here automatically.
        ct state new iifname "wg0" ct mark set 0x1
        # Outbound SMTP goes through the relay so it leaves from the address
        # SPF authorises and PTR names; `!= local` keeps mail ARRIVING
        # for this host out of it.
        ct state new tcp dport 25 fib daddr type != local ct mark set 0x1
        # The relay's own sites go through the tunnel, so VPN clients
        # reach them as the relay's hairpin address.
        ct state new ip daddr 203.0.113.10 tcp dport { 25, 80, 143, 443, 465, 587, 993, 4190 } ct mark set 0x1
        # Restore the mark onto every packet of an already-marked
        # connection (both directions) so the policy-routing table below
        # actually sees it — ct mark alone is invisible to `ip rule`.
        meta mark set ct mark
    }

    # Every relayed service on this host terminates at a LOCAL
    # process (Caddy binds the host's own address directly; mail
    # engines the same) — its replies are OUTPUT packets, never
    # forwarded ones, so `chain prerouting` above never sees them.
    # Without this chain, a relayed HTTPS
    # request's SYN arrived correctly (marked, DNAT-preserved real
    # client IP and all), but Caddy's SYN-ACK carried no mark, fell
    # through to the main routing table, and never found its way
    # back through the tunnel — the connection just hung. `type
    # route hook output` is nftables' own mechanism for exactly
    # this: changing a locally-generated packet's mark and having
    # the kernel redo the route lookup that already happened.
    chain output {
        type route hook output priority mangle; policy accept;
        # Outbound SMTP goes through the relay so it leaves from the address
        # SPF authorises and PTR names; `!= local` keeps mail ARRIVING
        # for this host out of it.
        ct state new tcp dport 25 fib daddr type != local ct mark set 0x1
        # The relay's own sites go through the tunnel, so VPN clients
        # reach them as the relay's hairpin address.
        ct state new ip daddr 203.0.113.10 tcp dport { 25, 80, 143, 443, 465, 587, 993, 4190 } ct mark set 0x1
        meta mark set ct mark
    }

    # The mark reroutes a host process after it picked its
    # source; the tunnel takes only its own address.
    chain postrouting {
        type nat hook postrouting priority srcnat; policy accept;
        oifname "wg0" meta mark 0x1 masquerade
    }

        # Filled by the control-plane agent when it installs a service that
        # needs a port open (`flush chain` + `add rule`, never a reload of
        # this file). Empty means nothing extra is open.
        chain gryonixnexus_services {
        }    # No forward chain: Docker hooks its own drop-policy forward
    # chain with per-container accepts; a second drop-policy
    # chain here would override it and cut containers off.
}

include "/etc/nftables.d/gryonixnexus-*.nft"
EOF_NFT
nft -c -f /etc/nftables.conf
nft -f /etc/nftables.conf
systemctl enable --now nftables >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl is-active --quiet docker; then
  systemctl restart docker
fi

# **The same reason as the docker restart above, for the same flush.**
# `flush ruleset` erases EVERY table, and CrowdSec's bans live in a
# table of their own (`ip crowdsec` / `ip6 crowdsec6`, written by the
# firewall bouncer). The bouncer does not notice: its unit stays
# active, `cscli decisions list` keeps answering, and not one of those
# decisions is in the packet filter any more. 20 live decisions, no crowdsec table, silent journal —
# which is strictly worse than having no bouncer, because the dashboard
# goes on reporting a defended host. Restarting it re-creates the
# tables and re-applies what the engine holds.
if systemctl is-active --quiet crowdsec-firewall-bouncer 2>/dev/null; then
  systemctl restart crowdsec-firewall-bouncer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 6/15"
log "Защита от вторжений: CrowdSec (следит за ssh и Caddy, блокирует через firewall)"
(
set -e
curl -fsSL https://install.crowdsec.net | sh
dpkg --configure -a --force-confdef --force-confold || true
# Engine first, in its own call: apt given both packages on one line
# has configured the bouncer first on this fleet, and its
# post-installation script could not mint itself an API key because
# the engine did not exist yet — the unit starts and talks to nothing.
apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold install -y crowdsec
apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold install -y crowdsec-firewall-bouncer-nftables

# acquis.d, not the package's own acquis.yaml: CrowdSec's supported
# directory for additional sources, so an upgrade never fights us for
# the file.
install -d -m 755 /etc/crowdsec/acquis.d
cat > /etc/crowdsec/acquis.d/gryonixnexus.yaml <<'EOF_CS_ACQUIS'
# Managed by gryonixNexus. Journald, not files: this fleet runs Debian with
# rsyslog inactive, so /var/log/auth.log does not exist and a file-based
# acquisition would parse nothing while reporting itself healthy.
source: journalctl
journalctl_filter:
 - "_SYSTEMD_UNIT=ssh.service"
 - "_SYSTEMD_UNIT=sshd.service"
labels:
 type: syslog
---
source: journalctl
journalctl_filter:
 - "_SYSTEMD_UNIT=caddy.service"
labels:
 type: caddy
EOF_CS_ACQUIS

# Move the local API off 8080 BEFORE the engine starts — see the type
# header. All three files have to agree: listen_uri moves the door,
# the other two are how cscli and the bouncer find it. Missing files
# (a postinst that has not run yet) are left alone rather than
# failing the block — the engine start below still gets the newly
# written acquisition either way.
[ -f /etc/crowdsec/config.yaml ] && \
  sed -i "s|^\( *\)listen_uri:.*|\1listen_uri: 127.0.0.1:8237|" /etc/crowdsec/config.yaml
[ -f /etc/crowdsec/local_api_credentials.yaml ] && \
  sed -i "s|^url:.*|url: http://127.0.0.1:8237|" /etc/crowdsec/local_api_credentials.yaml
[ -f /etc/crowdsec/bouncers/crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.yaml ] && \
  sed -i "s|^api_url:.*|api_url: http://127.0.0.1:8237/|" /etc/crowdsec/bouncers/crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.yaml

# --error lowers cscli's log level so an already-installed collection
# is silent; the command still succeeds, which is what makes this
# idempotent on a re-run.
cscli collections install crowdsecurity/sshd crowdsecurity/caddy crowdsecurity/linux --error || true
cscli hub update --error || true

systemctl enable --now crowdsec >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
systemctl restart crowdsec

# A key the bouncer cannot use is the same outcome as no bouncer at
# all — registered only when the config carries no real key yet, so a
# re-run does not mint a new one and restart a bouncer that already
# works.
BOUNCER_CFG=/etc/crowdsec/bouncers/crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.yaml
if [ -f "$BOUNCER_CFG" ]; then
  CURRENT_KEY="$(sed -n 's/^api_key: *//p' "$BOUNCER_CFG" | head -n1 | tr -d '"'\''')"
  if [ -z "${CURRENT_KEY:-}" ] || [ "${CURRENT_KEY:-}" = "<API_KEY>" ]; then
    cscli bouncers delete gryonixnexus-firewall-bouncer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    KEY="$(cscli bouncers add gryonixnexus-firewall-bouncer -o raw)"
    if [ -n "${KEY:-}" ]; then
      sed -i "s|^api_key:.*|api_key: $KEY|" "$BOUNCER_CFG"
    fi
  fi
  # Refused rather than repaired when the bouncer is not aimed at its
  # own table: a bouncer aimed at the table this script's own
  # `flush ruleset` firewall step rewrites would have its bans erased
  # by the next provision, with nothing on either side to say so —
  # the same refusal `bouncer_targets_its_own_table` makes.
  if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*table:[[:space:]]*"?crowdsec6?"?[[:space:]]*$' "$BOUNCER_CFG"; then
    systemctl enable --now crowdsec-firewall-bouncer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    systemctl try-restart crowdsec-firewall-bouncer || true
  fi
fi
) || echo "Защита от вторжений (CrowdSec) не установилась до конца — установка продолжается без неё. На остальную часть сервера это не влияет." >&2

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 7/15"
log "Коллектор истории метрик (gryonixnexus-metrics)"
backup /opt/gryonixnexus-metrics-collector.sh
cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-metrics-collector.sh <<'EOF_METRICS'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — samples host metrics every 10 seconds and keeps
# downsampled history buckets as CSV files under /var/lib/gryonixnexus/metrics.
# Columns: epoch,cpu%,memUsed,memTotal,diskUsed,diskTotal,netRx/s,netTx/s,
# ioRead/s,ioWrite/s,load1,tempC. Empty field = no data for that sample.
# Power: power-<bucket>.csv, columns epoch,watts,sensor, when a sensor exists.
# Disks: disks-<bucket>.csv, columns epoch,mount,used,total, one row per filesystem.
set -euo pipefail

DIR=/var/lib/gryonixnexus/metrics
STEP=10
install -d -m 755 /var/lib/gryonixnexus "$DIR"

cpu_ticks() { awk '$1=="cpu"{t=0; for(i=2;i<=9;i++) t+=$i; print t, $5+$6; exit}' /proc/stat; }
mem_bytes() { awk '/^MemTotal:/{t=$2*1024} /^MemAvailable:/{a=$2*1024} END{print t-a, t}' /proc/meminfo; }
disk_bytes() {
  { df -B1 --output=target,size,used -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs -x overlay 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | awk 'NR>1 { if ($1=="/") {s=$2; u=$3; f=1} else if (!f && $2+0>s+0) {s=$2; u=$3} } END{print u+0, s+0}'
}
# Every real filesystem once: mount,used,total.
disk_rows() {
  { df -B1 --output=source,target,size,used -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs -x overlay -x squashfs -x efivarfs 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | awk 'NR>1 && NF==4 && $3+0>0 && $2 !~ /,/ && $2 !~ /^\/(boot|snap|run|proc|sys|dev)(\/|$)/ && !seen[$1]++ {print $2","$4","$3}'
}
net_bytes() {
  awk -F: 'NF==2 {name=$1; gsub(/[ \t]/,"",name); if (name ~ /^(lo|veth.*|docker.*|br-.*|virbr.*|wg.*|awg.*|tun.*|tap.*|tailscale.*|zt.*|cali.*|flannel.*|cni.*|ifb.*|dummy.*)$/) next;
                  split($2,a," "); rx+=a[1]; tx+=a[9]} END{print rx+0, tx+0}' /proc/net/dev
}
io_bytes() {
  awk '$3 ~ /^(sd[a-z]+|vd[a-z]+|xvd[a-z]+|hd[a-z]+|nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+|mmcblk[0-9]+)$/ \
         {r+=$6*512; w+=$10*512} END{print r+0, w+0}' /proc/diskstats
}
load_one() { awk '{print $1}' /proc/loadavg; }
temp_c() {
  { cat /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | awk '$1>0 && $1<150000 { if ($1>m) m=$1 } END{ if (m>0) printf "%.1f", m/1000 }'
}
rate() { awk -v c="$1" -v p="$2" -v s="$STEP" 'BEGIN{d=c-p; if (d<0) d=0; printf "%d", d/s}'; }

# Power sensors. Each prints watts, or nothing when absent.
POWERCAP=/sys/class/powercap
rapl_domains() {
  local d
  for d in "$POWERCAP"/intel-rapl:*; do
    case "${d##*/}" in *:*:*) continue ;; esac
    if [ -r "$d/energy_uj" ]; then echo "$d"; fi
  done
}
# Energy counter and its wrap range in microjoules; psys covers the platform.
rapl_uj() {
  local d name domains total=0 range=0
  domains=$(rapl_domains)
  [ -n "$domains" ] || return 0
  for d in $domains; do
    name=$(cat "$d/name" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ "$name" = psys ]; then domains=$d; break; fi
  done
  for d in $domains; do
    total=$(( total + $(cat "$d/energy_uj") ))
    range=$(( range + $(cat "$d/max_energy_range_uj" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))
  done
  echo "$total $range"
}
ipmi_w() {
  if [ ! -e /dev/ipmi0 ] || ! command -v ipmitool >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
  timeout 5 ipmitool dcmi power reading 2>/dev/null \
    | awk -F: '/Instantaneous power reading/ {gsub(/[^0-9.]/, "", $2); if ($2+0>0) printf "%.1f", $2; exit}'
}
hwmon_w() {
  local f name
  for f in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/power1_average /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/power1_input; do
    [ -r "$f" ] || continue
    name=$(cat "${f%/*}/name" 2>/dev/null || true)
    case "$name" in amdgpu|radeon|nouveau|i915|xe) continue ;; esac
    awk '$1>0 {printf "%.1f", $1/1000000}' "$f"
    return 0
  done
}
pi_w() {
  command -v vcgencmd >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  vcgencmd pmic_read_adc 2>/dev/null | awk '
    { key=substr($1, 1, length($1)-2); v=$2; sub(/.*=/, "", v); sub(/[AV]$/, "", v) }
    $1 ~ /_A$/ {a[key]=v}
    $1 ~ /_V$/ {u[key]=v}
    END { for (k in a) if (k in u) w+=a[k]*u[k]; if (w>0) printf "%.1f", w }'
}
ups_w() {
  command -v upsc >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  local ups
  ups=$(upsc -l 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
  [ -n "$ups" ] || return 0
  upsc "$ups" 2>/dev/null | awk -F': ' '
    /^ups.realpower:/ {r=$2} /^ups.load:/ {l=$2} /^ups.realpower.nominal:/ {n=$2}
    END { if (r>0) printf "%.1f", r; else if (l>0 && n>0) printf "%.1f", l*n/100 }'
}


# Keep only the newest <max> rows of <file>.
trim() {
  local file=$1 max=$2 lines tmp
  [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
  lines=$(wc -l < "$file")
  if [ "$lines" -gt "$(( max + max / 10 ))" ]; then
    tmp=$(mktemp "$DIR/.trim.XXXXXX")
    tail -n "$max" "$file" > "$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
    chmod 644 "$file"
  fi
}

# Average the source rows inside the just-closed <period> window and
# append one row to <target>. No-op while the window is still open, when
# it was already written, or when the source has no rows in it (gap).
aggregate() {
  local target=$1 source=$2 period=$3 keep=$4 now start last row
  [ -f "$source" ] || return 0
  now=$(date +%s)
  start=$(( now / period * period - period ))
  last=-1
  if [ -f "$target" ]; then
    last=$(tail -n 1 "$target" | cut -d, -f1)
    case "$last" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last=-1 ;; esac
  fi
  [ "$last" -lt "$start" ] || return 0
  row=$(awk -F, -v s="$start" -v e=$(( start + period )) '
    $1>=s && $1<e {
      n++
      if ($2!="") {c+=$2; cn++}
      mu+=$3; mt=$4; du+=$5; dt=$6
      if ($7!="") {rx+=$7; rxn++}
      if ($8!="") {tx+=$8; txn++}
      if ($9!="") {ir+=$9; irn++}
      if ($10!="") {iw+=$10; iwn++}
      l+=$11
      if ($12!="") {tp+=$12; tn++}
    }
    END {
      if (!n) exit 0
      printf "%d,", s
      if (cn) printf "%.1f", c/cn
      printf ",%d,%d,%d,%d,", mu/n, mt, du/n, dt
      if (rxn) printf "%d", rx/rxn
      printf ","
      if (txn) printf "%d", tx/txn
      printf ","
      if (irn) printf "%d", ir/irn
      printf ","
      if (iwn) printf "%d", iw/iwn
      printf ",%.2f,", l/n
      if (tn) printf "%.1f", tp/tn
      printf "\n"
    }' "$source")
  [ -n "$row" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$row" >> "$target"
  chmod 644 "$target"
  trim "$target" "$keep"
}


# Average watts inside the just-closed <period> window, same rules as above.
aggregate_power() {
  local target=$1 source=$2 period=$3 keep=$4 now start last row
  [ -f "$source" ] || return 0
  now=$(date +%s)
  start=$(( now / period * period - period ))
  last=-1
  if [ -f "$target" ]; then
    last=$(tail -n 1 "$target" | cut -d, -f1)
    case "$last" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last=-1 ;; esac
  fi
  [ "$last" -lt "$start" ] || return 0
  row=$(awk -F, -v s="$start" -v e=$(( start + period )) '
    $1>=s && $1<e && $2!="" {w+=$2; n++; src=$3}
    END { if (n) printf "%d,%.1f,%s\n", s, w/n, src }' "$source")
  [ -n "$row" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$row" >> "$target"
  chmod 644 "$target"
  trim "$target" "$keep"
}

# Average each filesystem inside the just-closed <period> window.
aggregate_disks() {
  local target=$1 source=$2 period=$3 keep=$4 now start last row
  [ -f "$source" ] || return 0
  now=$(date +%s)
  start=$(( now / period * period - period ))
  last=-1
  if [ -f "$target" ]; then
    last=$(tail -n 1 "$target" | cut -d, -f1)
    case "$last" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last=-1 ;; esac
  fi
  [ "$last" -lt "$start" ] || return 0
  row=$(awk -F, -v s="$start" -v e=$(( start + period )) '
    $1>=s && $1<e && NF==4 {u[$2]+=$3; t[$2]=$4; n[$2]++}
    END { for (m in n) printf "%d,%s,%d,%d\n", s, m, u[m]/n[m], t[m] }' "$source")
  [ -n "$row" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$row" >> "$target"
  chmod 644 "$target"
  trim "$target" $(( keep * 16 ))
}

prev_total=0 prev_idle=0 prev_rx=0 prev_tx=0 prev_ir=0 prev_iw=0 have_prev=0
prev_uj=0 prev_rapl_at=0 have_rapl=0

while :; do

  read -r total idle < <(cpu_ticks)

  aggregate_power "$DIR/power-10m.csv" "$DIR/power-1m.csv"  600     432

  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1m.csv"  "$DIR/disks-10s.csv" 60      720
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-10m.csv" "$DIR/disks-1m.csv"  600     432
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1h.csv"  "$DIR/disks-10m.csv" 3600    336
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1d.csv"  "$DIR/disks-1h.csv"  86400   400
  aggregate_disks "$DIR/disks-1w.csv"  "$DIR/disks-1d.csv"  604800  260

# Managed by gryonixNexus — WireGuard on the home server (tunnel client).
# This file contains a private key: mode 600, never publish it.
[Interface]
Address = 10.8.0.2/24
PrivateKey = TEST-PRIVATE-KEY=

[Peer]
# VPS — the public entry point
PublicKey = TEST-PUBLIC-KEY=
Endpoint = 203.0.113.10:51820
# Full tunnel: all outbound traffic goes via the VPS so that mail
# leaves from the VPS IP (matching PTR/SPF). wg-quick sets up the
# routes — in its OWN table, which is also what keeps them out of
# docker's way: a split list written here instead lands 32 prefixes in
# the MAIN table, and docker then refuses to allocate any bridge subnet
# at all.
#
# What a default route costs is the exemption for the tunnel's OWN
# packets, which wg-quick makes with `fwmark 51820` and which any
# other mangle rule on the host can clear — mailcow's netfilter
# container sets a mark on every outgoing packet, and mailcow is a
# service from this same catalogue. The encrypted UDP then matches the
# default route wg-quick just installed, is encrypted again, and the
# machine sends hundreds of megabytes a second to itself with no
# internet at all. Same live run, same afternoon.
#
# So the relay's own address is pinned in the main table by
# `gryonixnexus-tunnel-endpoint.service`, before this interface comes
# up. A unit and not a `PreUp` here: a failing hook takes the whole
# interface down with it, and Ubuntu 26.04 confines wg-quick with an
# AppArmor profile allowing only `ip`, `nft` and `sysctl` — a hook
# needing a shell pipeline is denied, silently, under `|| true`.
AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0
PersistentKeepalive = 25
EOF_WG

# tunnel comes up.** wg-quick answers a full tunnel by moving every
# route into its own table and exempting the encrypted packets with
# `fwmark 51820`; any other mangle rule on this host that rewrites
# marks clears that exemption — mailcow's netfilter container sets one
# on every outgoing packet, and mailcow is a service from this same
# catalogue. The encrypted UDP then matches the default route wg-quick
# has just installed, is encrypted again, and the machine sends
# hundreds of megabytes a second to itself with no internet at all.
#
# A /32 in the MAIN table is immune to that: wg-quick's own rules

#!/bin/bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — mirrors the main routing table's
# locally-connected routes (Docker's bridges included) into a
# policy-routing table that defaults via the tunnel, so a relayed
# connection's reply — marked by nftables' prerouting chain — finds
# its way back through wg0 instead of the home ISP's default
# gateway, while traffic actually destined for a container (the other
# leg of the very same DNATed connection) still reaches the local
# bridge. Re-run periodically (see the .timer unit): Docker creates
# and destroys bridges as services are installed and removed.
set -euo pipefail

TABLE=100
MARK=0x1

ip rule del fwmark "$MARK" table "$TABLE" 2>/dev/null || true
ip rule add fwmark "$MARK" table "$TABLE"

ip route flush table "$TABLE" 2>/dev/null || true
# Mirror every locally-connected route (Docker's bridges included) so
# relayed traffic whose real destination is a container keeps going
# there; only a genuine default-route destination falls to the
# tunnel. Word-splitting on $route is deliberate: each line from
# `ip route show` is a multi-field route spec that `ip route add`
# expects as separate arguments. Gateway routes stay out: a
# host route to the relay would pull its own sites off the tunnel.
while IFS= read -r route; do
  [ -n "$route" ] || continue
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  ip route add $route table "$TABLE" 2>/dev/null || true
done < <(ip route show table main scope link || true)

ip route add default dev "wg0" table "$TABLE"
EOF_ROUTESYNC

[Unit]
Description=gryonixNexus relay route sync (mirrors Docker's bridges into the tunnel policy-routing table)
After=wg-quick@wg0.service docker.service
Requires=wg-quick@wg0.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
# No RemainAfterExit: this unit is re-triggered by its own timer every
# 2 minutes, and a oneshot service that stays "active (exited)" after
# its first run does not actually re-execute on a later `start` — the
# manager sees it's already active and treats the job as redundant.
# The timer's second tick fired (LastTriggerUSec
# advanced) but the script never ran a second time, and a docker
# bridge created between runs stayed unmirrored — exactly the failure
# this timer exists to prevent.
ExecStart=/opt/gryonixnexus-relay-route-sync.sh

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

#!/bin/bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — restarts the tunnel after a silent spell.
set -euo pipefail
unit="wg-quick@wg0"
systemctl is-active --quiet "$unit" || exit 0

uptime_s="$(cut -d. -f1 /proc/uptime)"
started_us="$(systemctl show -p ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic --value "$unit")"
running_for=$(( uptime_s - ${started_us:-0} / 1000000 ))

handshake="$(wg show wg0 latest-handshakes 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==1{print $2}' || true)"

  quiet_for=$(( $(date +%s) - handshake ))
else
  quiet_for=$running_for
fi

if [ "$running_for" -gt 300 ] && [ "$quiet_for" -gt 300 ]; then
  logger -t gryonixnexus-tunnel "no handshake for ${quiet_for}s, restarting $unit"
  systemctl restart "$unit"
  systemctl start gryonixnexus-relay-route-sync.service || true
fi
EOF_WATCHDOG
