# wrapper changes already reach them.
if grep -q '^DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION=' mailcow.conf; then
  sed -i 's/^DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION=.*/DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION=native/' mailcow.conf
else
  echo 'DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION=native' >> mailcow.conf
fi
# A clone made under a tight umask stays broken forever without this:
# git has no mode flag, and a re-run skips the clone (.git is already
# there). mailcow's containers drop to their own users — nginx's config
# says `user nginx` — and mount this tree, so root-only modes make the
# worker fail to even traverse /web and every PHP path answers a bare
# nginx 404, the whole API included. mailcow.conf keeps 600: it holds
# the database passwords.
chmod -R a+rX .
chmod 600 mailcow.conf
# Pull/up wrapped in retry: on a fresh public server the first pull of
# mailcow's ~15 images often trips a transient registry timeout, which
# under `set -e` aborted the install and forced a manual Retry.
retry 4 docker compose pull -q
retry 2 docker compose up -d

cd /opt/mailcow-dockerized
# Enable the REST API once (key generated on this server, kept by
# re-runs). docker-compose passes API_KEY/API_ALLOW_FROM into the php
# container; the last assignment in the .env-style file wins, so
# appending works even next to the commented template lines.
if ! grep -q '^API_KEY=' mailcow.conf; then
  # The caller is the host reaching the published port, so mailcow's
  # nginx sees the connection arrive from its own bridge gateway — .1
  # of whatever IPV4_NETWORK generate_config.sh settled on. That is
  # 172.22.1 by default but NOT always: the generator moves the subnet
  # when it collides with a docker network that already exists, and a
  # hardcoded gateway then fails the API's IP ACL with an "api access
  # denied for ip" that reads exactly like a wrong key.
  MC_NET="$(grep '^IPV4_NETWORK=' mailcow.conf | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '[:space:]')"
  printf 'API_KEY=%s\nAPI_ALLOW_FROM=%s.1,127.0.0.1\n' \
    "$(openssl rand -hex 20)" "${MC_NET:-172.22.1}" >> mailcow.conf
  docker compose up -d
fi
MC_API_KEY="$(grep '^API_KEY=' mailcow.conf | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2-)"
MC_API="https://127.0.0.1:18443/api/v1"
MC_BODY="$(mktemp)"
MC_CODE=000
# The API lives on the HTTPS vhost. mailcow's HTTP port 301-redirects
# to it unconditionally, and curl without -L returns the redirect's
# HTML body instead of JSON — so every call over HTTP silently failed
# (jq found no fields), add/domain and add/dkim never ran, and DKIM was
# reported "not ready" forever. Hit HTTPS directly, -k for self-signed.
#
# Status into a variable, body into a file, and never a non-zero exit.
# With `curl -f` the only thing that reached the install log was
# "curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404": the body — which
# is mailcow's own reason for refusing ("route not found",
# "authentication failed", "Cannot find attributes in post data") — was
# discarded, so the failure was undiagnosable, and the bare exit status
# killed the entire 22-step install under `set -e` at step 7, before
# the other services and before the install key was revoked.
mc_api() {
  MC_CODE="$(curl -sSk --max-time 20 -o "$MC_BODY" -w '%{http_code}' -K - \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" "$@" <<< "header = \"X-API-Key: $MC_API_KEY\"")" || :
  case "$MC_CODE" in ''|*[!0-9]*) MC_CODE=000 ;; esac
  [ "$MC_CODE" -ge 200 ] && [ "$MC_CODE" -lt 300 ]
}
# Why the last call failed, in one bounded line: an HTML error page
# instead of JSON must not flood the log the app streams.
mc_why() { printf 'HTTP %s %s' "$MC_CODE" "$(tr -d '\r\n' < "$MC_BODY" | cut -c1-300)"; }
log "Mailcow: добавление домена example.com и его DKIM-ключа через API"
# A deadline rather than a fixed number of tries: each attempt can
# itself burn the 20 s curl timeout, so counting attempts bounded this
# wait at 25 minutes of total silence, not the 5 it was meant to be.
MC_READY=0
MC_TRY=0
MC_DEADLINE=$(($(date +%s) + 300))
while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$MC_DEADLINE" ]; do
  if mc_api "$MC_API/get/domain/all"; then MC_READY=1; break; fi
  # Heartbeat every ~30 s. The API needs a while after the containers
  # report healthy, and a wait that prints nothing at all is
  # indistinguishable from a hung install in the app's progress view.
  MC_TRY=$((MC_TRY + 1))
  if [ "$((MC_TRY % 6))" -eq 0 ]; then
    log "Mailcow: ждём, пока поднимется API ($(mc_why))"
  fi
  sleep 5
done
if [ "$MC_READY" -eq 1 ]; then
  # Every mail domain (the primary one plus any additional
  # domains) with its own DKIM key. Both steps are idempotent — created
  # only when missing, so re-runs never touch an existing configuration,
  # and a domain removed from the app is left alone on the server rather
  # than deleted with its mailboxes.
  # The list is fed through a here-document rather than a quoted word
  # list: it reads the names literally, so no shell quoting question
  # arises at all, and it stays the same shape for one domain or ten.
  while IFS= read -r MC_DOMAIN; do
    [ -n "$MC_DOMAIN" ] || continue
    if ! mc_api "$MC_API/get/domain/$MC_DOMAIN" || ! jq -e '.domain_name' < "$MC_BODY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      mc_api -X POST -d "{\"domain\":\"$MC_DOMAIN\",\"description\":\"Managed by gryonixNexus\",\"aliases\":\"400\",\"defquota\":\"3072\",\"maxquota\":\"10240\",\"quota\":\"10240\",\"mailboxes\":\"50\",\"active\":\"1\",\"restart_sogo\":\"10\"}" \
        "$MC_API/add/domain" \
        || log "Mailcow: не удалось добавить домен $MC_DOMAIN через API — добавьте его в админке (Configuration → Domains). ($(mc_why))"
    fi
    if ! mc_api "$MC_API/get/dkim/$MC_DOMAIN" || ! jq -e '.pubkey' < "$MC_BODY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      mc_api -X POST -d "{\"domains\":\"$MC_DOMAIN\",\"dkim_selector\":\"dkim\",\"key_size\":2048}" \
        "$MC_API/add/dkim" \
        || log "Mailcow: не удалось создать DKIM-ключ для $MC_DOMAIN через API — создайте его в админке (Configuration → ARC/DKIM keys). ($(mc_why))"
    fi
  done <<'EOF_MC_DOMAINS'
example.com
EOF_MC_DOMAINS
  # The panel's `admin` ships with a published password. Replace it once
  # the API answers (the admin row exists by then) and keep the new one
  # in a root-only file the report reads; a failed call keeps the default
  # and the report says so. Re-runs reuse the stored password.
  MC_ADMIN_FILE="/opt/mailcow-dockerized/.gryonixnexus-admin-password"
  MC_ADMIN_PASS="$(cat "$MC_ADMIN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  [ -n "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" ] || MC_ADMIN_PASS="$(openssl rand -hex 12)"
  MC_REQ="$(mktemp)"
  printf '{"items":["admin"],"attr":{"password":"%s","password2":"%s"}}' "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" > "$MC_REQ"
  if mc_api -X POST -d @"$MC_REQ" \
       "$MC_API/edit/admin" \
     && jq -e 'if type == "array" then all(.[]; .type == "success") else .type == "success" end' < "$MC_BODY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    (umask 077; printf '%s\n' "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" > "$MC_ADMIN_FILE")
  else
    log "Mailcow admin password: the default one stays ($(mc_why))"
  fi
  rm -f "$MC_REQ"
else
  log "Mailcow: API не ответил — домен и DKIM-ключ НЕ созданы. Сам mailcow работает: добавьте домен в админке (Configuration → Domains) или перезапустите установку. ($(mc_why))"
fi
rm -f "$MC_BODY"

# Automatic trusted TLS for SMTP/IMAPS. Caddy fronts only the web UI;
# mailcow's mail daemons (Postfix/Dovecot) serve their OWN certificate,
# so without this they present a self-signed one and mail clients warn.
# Sync Caddy's issued certificate for mail.example.com into mailcow's ssl
# assets and reload the mail daemons — once now (a no-op until Caddy has
# issued it) and then on a timer so renewals are picked up automatically.
cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh <<'EOF_MC_CERTSYNC'
#!/bin/bash
set -eu
DOMAIN="mail.example.com"
MAILCOW="/opt/mailcow-dockerized"
DEST="$MAILCOW/data/assets/ssl"
CADDY_DATA="/var/lib/caddy/.local/share/caddy/certificates"
SRC_CRT="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.crt" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
SRC_KEY="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.key" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
if [ -z "$SRC_CRT" ] || [ -z "$SRC_KEY" ]; then exit 0; fi
if cmp -s "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem" && cmp -s "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"; then exit 0; fi
cp "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem"
cp "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"
cd "$MAILCOW"
docker compose restart postfix-mailcow dovecot-mailcow nginx-mailcow >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
EOF_MC_CERTSYNC
chmod 700 /opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.service <<'EOF_MC_CERTSVC'
[Unit]
Description=Sync Caddy TLS certificate into Mailcow (SMTP/IMAPS)
After=docker.service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh
EOF_MC_CERTSVC
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.timer <<'EOF_MC_CERTTIMER'
[Unit]
Description=Periodic Caddy to Mailcow TLS certificate sync
[Timer]
OnActiveSec=5min
OnUnitActiveSec=1h
Persistent=true
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF_MC_CERTTIMER
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.timer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
/opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh || true

# Root-owned DKIM dump: every domain and alias domain, missing keys created.
cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-dkim.sh <<'EOF_GD_DKIM'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
CONF="/opt/mailcow-dockerized/mailcow.conf"
[ -r "$CONF" ] || { echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM_DONE"; exit 0; }
MC_KEY="$(grep '^API_KEY=' "$CONF" | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2-)"
API="https://127.0.0.1:18443/api/v1"
mc() { curl -fsSk --max-time 20 -K - "$@" <<< "header = \"X-API-Key: $MC_KEY\""; }
DOMAINS="$({ mc "$API/get/domain/all" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[].domain_name // empty' 2>/dev/null || true; mc "$API/get/alias-domain/all" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[].alias_domain // empty' 2>/dev/null || true; } | sort -u)"
dkim_of() { mc "$API/get/dkim/$1" 2>/dev/null | jq -r "select(type == \"object\") | .$2 // empty" 2>/dev/null || true; }
for D in $DOMAINS; do
  if [ -z "$(dkim_of "$D" dkim_txt)" ]; then
    mc -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"domains\":\"$D\",\"dkim_selector\":\"dkim\",\"key_size\":2048}" "$API/add/dkim" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  TXT="$(dkim_of "$D" dkim_txt)"
  SEL="$(dkim_of "$D" dkim_selector)"
  if [ -n "$TXT" ]; then echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM ${SEL:-dkim}._domainkey.$D $TXT"; fi
done
echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM_DONE"
EOF_GD_DKIM
chmod 750 /opt/gryonixnexus-dkim.sh
fi

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 11/15"
if [ -z "${GRYONIXNEXUS_SKIP_SERVICES:-}" ]; then
log "Установка Caddy"
rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
if ! command -v caddy >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! id caddy >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  caddy_arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"
  case "$caddy_arch" in armhf) caddy_arch=armv6 ;; armel) caddy_arch=armv5 ;; esac
  caddy_tag="$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/releases/latest)"
  caddy_tag="${caddy_tag##*/}"
  caddy_deb="caddy_${caddy_tag#v}_linux_${caddy_arch}.deb"
  caddy_url="https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/releases/download/$caddy_tag"
  caddy_tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
  curl -fsSL -o "$caddy_tmp/$caddy_deb" "$caddy_url/$caddy_deb"
  curl -fsSL -o "$caddy_tmp/sums" "$caddy_url/caddy_${caddy_tag#v}_checksums.txt"
  (cd "$caddy_tmp" && grep "  $caddy_deb\$" sums | sha512sum -c -)
  DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confdef -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold install -yq --no-install-recommends --reinstall "$caddy_tmp/$caddy_deb"
  id caddy >/dev/null
  rm -rf "$caddy_tmp"
fi
fi

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 12/15"
if [ -z "${GRYONIXNEXUS_SKIP_SERVICES:-}" ]; then
log "Caddy: обратный прокси для веб-сервисов"
# Every site imports the admin guard, so the file must exist even when
# no VPN panel installs the lockdown wrapper (empty = public; re-runs
# keep the current state — a missing import is a fatal Caddy error).
# Mode spelled out rather than left to the umask: caddy runs as its own
# user and cannot read a root-only /etc/caddy at all.
install -d -m 755 /etc/caddy
[ -f /etc/caddy/gryonixnexus-admin-guard ] || : > /etc/caddy/gryonixnexus-admin-guard
cat > /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.gryonixnexus <<'EOF_CADDYFILE'
{
	order respond before forward_auth
	servers {
		protocols h1 h2
	}
}

mail.example.com {
    # gryonixnexus: mailcow
    @gryonixnexus_open path /SOGo/dav /SOGo/dav/* /.well-known/caldav /.well-known/carddav /principals /principals/* /Microsoft-Server-ActiveSync /Microsoft-Server-ActiveSync/*
    handle @gryonixnexus_open {
        reverse_proxy https://127.0.0.1:18443 {
            header_up Host {host}
            transport http {
                tls_insecure_skip_verify
            }
        }
    }
    handle {
        import /etc/caddy/gryonixnexus-admin-guard
        reverse_proxy https://127.0.0.1:18443 {
            header_up Host {host}
            transport http {
                tls_insecure_skip_verify
            }
        }
    }
}
EOF_CADDYFILE
# Every block on this host that is NOT this deployment's, kept verbatim
# and appended below ours. Blocks are separated by a blank line and open
# with their names — the shape this file is written in on both routes,
# and the one the agent splits on. A block is ours when its header is
# one of ours or its owner line names a service of ours; the global
# options block is dropped, because ours already carries it first.
# Anything left claiming a name we serve stops the run: two blocks on
# one name make Caddy refuse the whole file, which would take down every
# site on the machine at the next restart.
if [ -f /etc/caddy/Caddyfile ]; then
  caddy_clash=$(awk -v ourids='mailcow' \
                    -v out=/etc/caddy/Caddyfile.gryonixnexus-kept '
    function flush(   i, names, count, parts, id, line, keep) {
      if (n == 0) return
      names = block[1]
      sub(/[ \t]*\{[ \t]*$/, "", names)
      if (pass == 1) {
        if (names != "") {
          header[block[1]] = 1
          count = split(names, parts, ",")
          for (i = 1; i <= count; i++) {
            gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", parts[i])
            mine[tolower(parts[i])] = 1
          }
        }
        n = 0
        return
      }
      keep = 1
      if (names == "") keep = 0
      else if (block[1] in header) keep = 0
      else {
        for (i = 2; i <= n; i++) {
          line = block[i]
          gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", line)
          if (index(line, "# gryonixnexus: ") == 1) {
            id = substr(line, length("# gryonixnexus: ") + 1)
            gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", id)
            if (index("," ourids ",", "," id ",") > 0) keep = 0
          }
        }
      }
      if (keep) {
        count = split(names, parts, ",")
        for (i = 1; i <= count; i++) {
          gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", parts[i])
          if (tolower(parts[i]) in mine && !(parts[i] in seen)) {
            seen[parts[i]] = 1
            clashes = clashes (clashes == "" ? "" : ", ") parts[i]
          }
        }
        print "" > out
        for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) print block[i] > out
      }
      n = 0
    }
    # The end of a file is a block boundary too, and it is not marked by a
    # blank line: our file ends with the brace of its last site. Flushed here,
    # while `pass` still names the file the block came out of — FILENAME has
    # already moved on by the time the first line of the next one is read, and
    # reading it would file our last site as a stranger AND swallow the first
    # block of the file that follows.
    #
    # NO APOSTROPHES anywhere in this program: it is quoted into the script
    # inside single quotes, and one of them ends the program where it stands.
    # `bash -n` then reports an unterminated quote at the END of a 900-line
    # script, which says nothing about where it came from.
    FNR == 1 { flush(); pass++ }
    /^[ \t]*$/ { flush(); next }
    { block[++n] = $0 }
    END { flush(); if (clashes != "") print clashes }
  ' /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.gryonixnexus /etc/caddy/Caddyfile)
  if [ -n "$caddy_clash" ]; then
    rm -f /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.gryonixnexus /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.gryonixnexus-kept
    fail "на этом сервере эти имена уже обслуживает другой сайт, а два блока на одно имя заставляют Caddy отвергнуть весь файл: $caddy_clash"
  fi
  if [ -s /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.gryonixnexus-kept ]; then
    cat /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.gryonixnexus-kept >> /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.gryonixnexus
  fi
  rm -f /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.gryonixnexus-kept
fi
backup /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
mv /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.gryonixnexus /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
systemctl enable caddy >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if ! systemctl reload caddy 2>/dev/null && ! systemctl restart caddy; then
  journalctl -u caddy -n 25 --no-pager -o cat 2>/dev/null || true
  ss -ltnp 'sport = :80 or sport = :443' 2>/dev/null || true
  fail "Caddy не запустился; выше его журнал и то, что занимает порты 80/443"
fi
fi

log "Установка помощника управления контейнерами для панели сервера"
backup /opt/gryonixnexus-container-ctl.sh
cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-container-ctl.sh <<'EOF_CONTAINER_CTL'

log "Панель управления: обёртка бэкапа Mailcow (/opt/mailcow-dockerized/bot-backup.sh)"
install -d '/opt/mailcow-dockerized'
backup /opt/mailcow-dockerized/bot-backup.sh
cat > /opt/mailcow-dockerized/bot-backup.sh <<'EOF_MC_BACKUP'
#!/bin/bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — mailcow backup wrapper for the Server Dashboard.
# sudo strips env vars (env_reset): MAILCOW_BACKUP_LOCATION is set here.
set -euo pipefail

#!/bin/bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — restore a service from a backup.
# Usage: gryonixnexus-restore.sh <mailcow> <archive>
#        GPG passphrase (encrypted archives only) on stdin.
set -euo pipefail

SERVICE="${1:-}"
ARCHIVE="${2:-}"

MAILCOW_PATH='/opt/mailcow-dockerized'
MAILCOW_BACKUPS='/opt/backups/mailcow'
VW_CONTAINER='vaultwarden'
VW_DATA='/opt/vaultwarden/data'
VW_BACKUPS='/opt/backups/vaultwarden'
STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"

# The archive must sit inside a backup directory this deployment owns.
# Without the check a whitelisted wrapper would happily unpack ANY
# root-readable file over a service's data directory.
case "$ARCHIVE" in
  *..*) echo "invalid path: ${ARCHIVE}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
case "$ARCHIVE" in
  "$MAILCOW_BACKUPS"/*|"$VW_BACKUPS"/*) ;;
  *) echo "path outside the backup directories: ${ARCHIVE}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
[ -e "$ARCHIVE" ] || { echo "no such backup: ${ARCHIVE}" >&2; exit 2; }

restore_mailcow() {
  [ -x "$MAILCOW_PATH/helper-scripts/backup_and_restore.sh" ] \
    || { echo "mailcow не найден в /opt/mailcow-dockerized" >&2; exit 1; }
  # mailcow's helper restores from a DIRECTORY inside its backup
  # location and picks it from a numbered menu. Stage the chosen backup
  # alone in a scratch location so that menu has exactly one entry.
  local stage="$MAILCOW_BACKUPS/.restore-$STAMP"
  mkdir -p "$stage"
  chmod 0777 "$stage"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2064
  trap "rm -rf '$stage'" EXIT
  local plain="$ARCHIVE"
  case "$ARCHIVE" in
    *.gpg)
      plain="$stage/.restore.tar.gz"
      gpg --batch --quiet --yes --decrypt --passphrase-fd 0 \
          --pinentry-mode loopback --output "$plain" "$ARCHIVE" \
        || { echo "could not decrypt the backup (wrong passphrase?)" >&2; exit 1; }
      ;;
  esac
  if [ -d "$ARCHIVE" ]; then
    cp -a "$ARCHIVE" "$stage/"
  else
    tar -xzf "$plain" -C "$stage"
    rm -f "$stage/.restore.tar.gz"
  fi
  export MAILCOW_BACKUP_LOCATION="$stage"
  # Bounded input, never `yes` (SIGPIPE under pipefail kills the pipeline).
  # The helper asks exactly two questions and then restores ONCE:
  # "Select a restore point" -> 1, the only staged backup; "Select a
  # dataset to restore" -> 0, the "[ 0 ] - all" entry, which expands to
  # every dataset in the backup (restore() loops over its arguments).
  # Feeding component indices one after another instead — as this did —
  # restores a SINGLE component and discards the rest of the input when
  # the helper exits, and which component index 1 refers to is whatever
  # `ls -f` returns first, so the survivor varied per run while the
  # wrapper still reported success.
  # The trailing "n" answers the vmail branch's "Force a resync now?";
  # extra input is harmless, a missing answer would depend on EOF.
  # Under `timeout` because an unrecognised prompt would otherwise wait
  # for a human that is never coming.
  printf '1\n0\nn\n' \
    | timeout 3600 "$MAILCOW_PATH/helper-scripts/backup_and_restore.sh" restore
}

restore_vaultwarden() {
  local plain="$ARCHIVE" tmp="" stage="" root="" previous="" saved=0
  case "$ARCHIVE" in
    *.gpg)
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
      # shellcheck disable=SC2064
      trap "rm -rf '$tmp'" EXIT
      plain="$tmp/restore.tar.gz"
      # --passphrase-fd 0: the secret arrives on stdin, never in argv.
      gpg --batch --quiet --yes --decrypt --passphrase-fd 0 \
          --pinentry-mode loopback --output "$plain" "$ARCHIVE" \
        || { echo "could not decrypt the backup (wrong passphrase?)" >&2; exit 1; }
      ;;
  esac
  # Verify BEFORE touching live data: a truncated upload must not cost
  # the user the data they still have.
  tar -tzf "$plain" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || { echo "the backup archive is not readable" >&2; exit 1; }
  # Unpacked aside; only the archived data directory is moved in.
  root="$(tar -tzf "$plain" | sed -n '1{s|^\./||;s|/*$||;p;}')"
  case "/$root/" in
    //|*/../*|*/./*) echo "the archive carries no vaultwarden data" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$VW_DATA")"
  stage="$(mktemp -d "$(dirname "$VW_DATA")/.restore-XXXXXX")"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2064
  trap "rm -rf '$stage' '$tmp'" EXIT
  tar --numeric-owner -xzf "$plain" -C "$stage" \
    || { echo "the backup archive is not readable" >&2; exit 1; }
  if [ ! -d "$stage/$root" ] || [ -L "$stage/$root" ]; then
    echo "the archive carries no vaultwarden data" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  docker stop "$VW_CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  # The old data is moved aside, never deleted: if the move fails it is
  # the only way back, and the container must come up again either way.
  previous="${VW_DATA}.pre-restore-$STAMP"
  if [ -d "$VW_DATA" ]; then mv "$VW_DATA" "$previous"; saved=1; fi
  if mv "$stage/$root" "$VW_DATA"; then
    if [ "$saved" -eq 1 ]; then echo "previous data kept at ${previous}"; fi
  else
    echo "restore failed, rolling back to the previous data" >&2
    rm -rf "$VW_DATA"
    if [ "$saved" -eq 1 ]; then mv "$previous" "$VW_DATA"; fi
    docker start "$VW_CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    exit 1
  fi
  docker start "$VW_CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}



case "$SERVICE" in
  mailcow) restore_mailcow ;;
  vaultwarden) restore_vaultwarden ;;

  *) echo "unsupported service: ${SERVICE}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
# A streamed command carries no exit status back to the app, so success
# is announced with a fixed ASCII marker (never the localized line —
# the app must not have to know which language the script was made in).
echo "Восстановление завершено."
echo 'GRYONIXNEXUS_RESTORE_DONE'
EOF_RESTORE
chmod 750 '/opt/gryonixnexus-restore.sh'
install -d '/opt/backups/mailcow/incoming'
chgrp "$(id -gn 'admin')" '/opt/backups/mailcow/incoming'
chmod 0770 '/opt/backups/mailcow/incoming'

log "Установка помощника резервного копирования для панели сервера"

cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh <<'EOF_BACKUP_CTL'
#!/bin/bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — backup housekeeping for the Server Dashboard.
# Usage: gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh delete <path>
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh set-schedule <off|every:<n><h|d>@<HH:MM>> <retention> [services...]
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh set-passphrase   (passphrase on stdin)
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh run
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh backup <service> [--encrypt|--no-encrypt]
#                                       (GPG passphrase on stdin when encrypting)
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh estimate <service>
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh set-destination <kind> <host> <port> <user> <path> <bucket> <keep>
#                                       (credential on stdin, optional)
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh show-destination
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh test-destination
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh set-drives <both|local|drive> <1|0> [uuids...]
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh show-drives
set -euo pipefail

ACTION="${1:-}"
CONFIG='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup.conf'
PASSFILE='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup.pass'
DESTCONF='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup-dest.conf'
DESTKEY='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup-dest.key'
DESTPUB='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup-dest.key.pub'
DESTSTATUS='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup-dest.status'
RETENTION=7
SERVICES='mailcow'
SCHEDULE=off
# The control user. Finished archives are chowned to it: the app
# downloads and shares them, and what keeps other accounts away is the
# 0750 on the enclosing backup root, not the file's owner.
OWNER='admin'
# Encryption state of the CURRENT run. The passphrase lives in a shell
# variable and reaches gpg down a pipe — never in argv, which is
# world-readable through /proc.
GD_ENCRYPT=0
GD_PASS=""

load_config() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  [ -f "$CONFIG" ] && . "$CONFIG"
  # A config from an older build may not set every value.
  : "${SCHEDULE:=off}" "${RETENTION:=7}" "${SERVICES:=mailcow}"
  case "$RETENTION" in ''|*[!0-9]*|0) RETENTION=1 ;; esac
}

# Where finished archives are sent, if anywhere. Its own file and its
# own loader: a host that never chose a destination keeps every default
# below, which together mean "leave the archive where it is".
DEST_KIND=none
DEST_HOST=""
DEST_PORT=22
DEST_USER=""
DEST_PATH=""
DEST_BUCKET=""
DEST_KEEP=0
load_destination() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  [ -f "$DESTCONF" ] && . "$DESTCONF"
  : "${DEST_KIND:=none}" "${DEST_PORT:=22}" "${DEST_KEEP:=0}"
}

# **Where a copy of this machine's archives lands so they survive the
# machine.** Called after every archive this wrapper finishes, by the
# timer and by the app's own button alike — one body, both callers, the
# rule this whole file is built on.
#
# Failure NEVER fails the backup: the archive on this disk is real and
# already written, and refusing it because a bucket was unreachable
# would turn a bad night into no backup at all. What a failure does is
# get RECORDED, because a copy that silently never leaves is the exact
# defect this exists to end.
gd_ship() {
  local out="$1" service="${2:-check}" error="" ok=0
  load_destination
  [ "$DEST_KIND" = "none" ] && return 0
  # One folder per machine and service, so rotation stays inside it.
  local machine
  machine="$(hostname -s 2>/dev/null || echo server)-$(cut -c1-8 /etc/machine-id 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  local folder="${DEST_PATH%/}/$machine/$service"
  case "$DEST_KIND" in
    ssh)
      if [ -z "$DEST_HOST" ] || [ -z "$DEST_USER" ] || [ ! -s "$DESTKEY" ]; then
        error="the destination is incomplete (host, user or key missing)"
      else
        # **A known_hosts this machine can actually write.** Run from the agent's unit,
        # ssh cannot create /root/.ssh — ProtectHome=yes and
        # ProtectSystem=full — so `accept-new` pinned nothing and every
        # shipment carried "Could not create directory /root/.ssh" into
        # the status file, where it reads as the failure. This path is
        # inside the agent's ReadWritePaths and is root-owned, so the
        # timer and the app's button pin the same key in the same file.
        local known="${DESTCONF%/*}/autobackup-dest.known_hosts"
        [ -e "$known" ] || ( umask 077 && : > "$known" )
        # `accept-new`, not `no`: the first sight of the far side is
        # pinned, and a CHANGED key after that stops the copy — which
        # is the one moment somebody must be told rather than obeyed.
        error="$(ssh -i "$DESTKEY" -p "$DEST_PORT" \
                  -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \
                  -o UserKnownHostsFile="$known" \
                  -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=20 \
                  "$DEST_USER@$DEST_HOST" "mkdir -p '$folder'" 2>&1)" \
          && error="$(scp -i "$DESTKEY" -P "$DEST_PORT" \
                  -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \
                  -o UserKnownHostsFile="$known" \
                  -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=20 \
                  "$out" "$DEST_USER@$DEST_HOST:$folder/" 2>&1)" \
          && ok=1
        # **A warning is not a failure.** ssh writes advice to stderr on
        # runs that worked, and this field is what the app shows as the
        # reason the copy did not leave; keeping it would report a
        # successful shipment as a broken one.
        [ "$ok" -eq 1 ] && error=""
        if [ "$ok" -eq 1 ] && [ "$DEST_KEEP" -gt 0 ]; then
          # Rotation on the FAR side, and only there: what this machine
          # keeps is RETENTION, and the two are different numbers on
          # purpose — a phone-sized disk here, a big one there.
          ssh -i "$DESTKEY" -p "$DEST_PORT" -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \
              -o UserKnownHostsFile="$known" \
              -o BatchMode=yes "$DEST_USER@$DEST_HOST" \
              "ls -1t '$folder' 2>/dev/null | tail -n +$((DEST_KEEP + 1)) | while read -r old; do rm -rf -- '$folder'/\"\$old\"; done" \
              >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        fi
      fi
      ;;
    s3)
      if ! command -v rclone >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        error="rclone is not installed on this server"
      elif [ ! -s "$DESTKEY" ]; then
        error="no credentials stored for the bucket"
      else
        # The credentials reach rclone as ENVIRONMENT, never argv:
        # /proc/<pid>/cmdline is world-readable and an access key in it
        # is an access key given away.
        error="$(
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$(cut -d: -f1 "$DESTKEY")" \
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$(cut -d: -f2- "$DESTKEY")" \
          RCLONE_CONFIG_GD_TYPE=s3 \
          RCLONE_CONFIG_GD_PROVIDER=Other \
          RCLONE_CONFIG_GD_ENV_AUTH=true \
          RCLONE_CONFIG_GD_ENDPOINT="$DEST_HOST" \
          rclone copy "$out" "gd:$DEST_BUCKET/$folder/" 2>&1
        )" && ok=1
      fi
      ;;
    *) error="unknown destination kind: $DEST_KIND" ;;
  esac
  {
    echo "AT=$(date +%s)"
    echo "OK=$ok"
    # One line, and the far side's own words: three different repairs
    # hide behind "it failed". QUOTED, and with quotes of its own
    # removed — see `do_test_destination` on what reading this file
    # as shell used to cost.
    # **Carriage returns too, not just newlines.** ssh ends its own
    # warnings with CR, and a reader that renders them the way a
    # terminal does — the agent's does, for progress bars — keeps only
    # what follows the last one and throws the rest away. The marker line vanished and the app was told the
    # copy failed, with no reason, while the file had landed.
    echo "ERROR='$(printf '%s' "$error" | tr '\r\n\t' '   ' | tr -d "'" | cut -c1-400)'"
  } > "$DESTSTATUS"
  chmod 644 "$DESTSTATUS"
  return 0
}

# The key this server ships WITH, made once and never replaced: the
# public half is already authorized on the far side, and a new pair
# would silently stop every copy.
gd_ensure_dest_key() {
  [ -s "$DESTKEY" ] && return 0
  # **The folder first.** A server that never had the agent installed
  # has no /etc/gryonixnexus, and ssh-keygen into a folder that is not
  # there failed with its output thrown away: `set-destination` stopped
  # on the chmod that followed and answered rc 1 with not one word.
  # The app's own screen showed
  # "could not save" and nothing else.
  install -d -m 755 "$(dirname "$DESTKEY")"
  rm -f "$DESTKEY" "$DESTPUB"
  if ! ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N '' -C 'gryonixnexus-backup' -f "$DESTKEY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "could not create the key this server ships backups with" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  chmod 600 "$DESTKEY"
  chmod 644 "$DESTPUB" 2>/dev/null || true
}

do_set_destination() {
  local kind="${1:-none}" host="${2:-}" port="${3:-22}" user="${4:-}"
  local path="${5:-}" bucket="${6:-}" keep="${7:-0}"
  case "$kind" in
    none|ssh|s3) ;;
    *) echo "unsupported destination: ${kind}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  case "$port$keep" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "invalid port or keep count" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  case "$host$user$path$bucket" in
    *[\'\"\\\`\$]*|*$'\n'*|*$'\r'*)
      echo "the destination may not contain quotes, backslashes, \$, backticks or line breaks" >&2
      exit 2 ;;
  esac
  # A secret on stdin, never argv — the same rule the passphrase
  # follows one function down.
  if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
    local secret
    secret="$(cat)"
    if [ -n "$secret" ]; then
      install -d -m 755 "$(dirname "$DESTKEY")"
      ( umask 077 && printf '%s' "$secret" > "$DESTKEY" )
      chmod 600 "$DESTKEY"
    fi
  fi
  [ "$kind" = "ssh" ] && gd_ensure_dest_key
  install -d -m 755 "$(dirname "$DESTCONF")"
  cat > "$DESTCONF" <<EOF_DEST
DEST_KIND=$kind
DEST_HOST='$host'
DEST_PORT=$port
DEST_USER='$user'
DEST_PATH='$path'
DEST_BUCKET='$bucket'
DEST_KEEP=$keep
EOF_DEST
  # 0640 and owned by root: it names a host and an account, which is
  # the owner's business and not every account's on this machine. The
  # app reads it through this wrapper, which runs as root.
  chmod 640 "$DESTCONF"
  # Printed so the app can authorize it on the far side without a
  # second call — a public key, and nothing else, is safe on stdout.
  [ -s "$DESTPUB" ] && printf 'GRYONIXNEXUS_DEST_PUBKEY %s\n' "$(cat "$DESTPUB")"
}

# Everything `show-destination` answers, in one read: the app draws the
# destination, the public key to authorize and what the last shipment
# did on a single screen.
do_show_destination() {
  load_destination
  printf 'DEST_KIND=%s\nDEST_HOST=%s\nDEST_PORT=%s\nDEST_USER=%s\nDEST_PATH=%s\nDEST_BUCKET=%s\nDEST_KEEP=%s\n' \
    "$DEST_KIND" "$DEST_HOST" "$DEST_PORT" "$DEST_USER" "$DEST_PATH" "$DEST_BUCKET" "$DEST_KEEP"
  [ -s "$DESTPUB" ] && printf 'DEST_PUBKEY=%s\n' "$(cat "$DESTPUB")"
  [ -s "$DESTSTATUS" ] && cat "$DESTSTATUS"
  return 0
}

# One small file, sent the same way a real archive is. The only way to
# learn a destination is wrong BEFORE the nightly run trusts it.
do_test_destination() {
  load_destination
  if [ "$DEST_KIND" = "none" ]; then
    echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DEST_TEST 0 no destination is set"
    return 0
  fi
  local probe
  probe="$(mktemp /tmp/gryonixnexus-dest-XXXXXX.txt)"
  date -u +'gryonixNexus destination check %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' > "$probe"
  gd_ship "$probe" check
  rm -f "$probe"
  # Read back out of the status file rather than kept in a variable:
  # what the app will see later is exactly what it is told now.
  local ok="0" error=""
  # **Parsed, never sourced.** This file carries the FAR SIDE's own
  # words, and reading it with `.` made them shell: a message with
  # "(ED25519)" in it broke the read outright, and one carrying $(…)
  # would have run here as root.
  if [ -f "$DESTSTATUS" ]; then
    ok="$(sed -n 's/^OK=//p' "$DESTSTATUS" | head -1)"
    error="$(sed -n "s/^ERROR='\(.*\)'\$/\1/p" "$DESTSTATUS" | head -1)"
  fi
  ok="${ok:-0}"
  echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DEST_TEST $ok $error"
}

# USB drives that take a copy of every archive. A host that never
# chose one keeps every archive here, exactly as before.
DRIVECONF='/etc/gryonixnexus/backup-drives.conf'
DRIVESTATUS='/etc/gryonixnexus/backup-drives.status'
DRIVELAST='/etc/gryonixnexus/backup-drives.last'
DRIVEROOT='/srv/gryonix-backup'
DRIVE_MODE=both
DRIVE_ENCRYPT=1
DRIVES=""
GD_DRIVE_ERROR=""
load_drives() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  [ -f "$DRIVECONF" ] && . "$DRIVECONF"
  : "${DRIVE_MODE:=both}" "${DRIVE_ENCRYPT:=1}"
}

# Where fstab mounts one drive, whether or not it is plugged in.
gd_drive_fstab() {
  findmnt --fstab -rno TARGET -S "UUID=$1" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
}

# The drive's mount point, only when it is mounted and marked.
gd_drive_target() {
  local target
  target="$(gd_drive_fstab "$1")"
  case "$target" in "$DRIVEROOT"/*) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
  # Never a bare folder: writing there fills the system disk.
  mountpoint -q "$target" || return 0
  grep -qx "$1" "$target/.gryonix-backup-drive" 2>/dev/null || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$target"
}

# Mounts a drive plugged in after boot, through systemd.
gd_drive_ready() {
  local target
  target="$(gd_drive_target "$1")"
  if [ -z "$target" ] && [ -b "/dev/disk/by-uuid/$1" ]; then
    target="$(gd_drive_fstab "$1")"
    case "$target" in
      "$DRIVEROOT"/*)
        systemctl start "$(systemd-escape -p --suffix=mount "$target")" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
    esac
    target="$(gd_drive_target "$1")"
  fi
  printf '%s' "$target"
}

# The drive's name: the last part of its mount point.
gd_drive_name() {
  local target
  target="$(gd_drive_fstab "$1")"
  if [ -n "$target" ]; then printf '%s' "${target##*/}"; else printf '%s' "$1"; fi
}

# Why a write to a drive failed.
gd_drive_why() {
  local avail
  case ",$(findmnt -no OPTIONS --target "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)," in
    *,ro,*) echo "the drive went read-only; check it"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  avail="$(df -B1 --output=avail "$1" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 | tr -cd '0-9')"
  if [ "${avail:-0}" -lt 1048576 ]; then
    echo "the drive is full"
  else
    echo "the drive could not be written"
  fi
}

# Copies one archive to a drive, encrypting it when asked.
gd_drive_write() {
  local src="$1" dest="$2" pass=""
  GD_DRIVE_ERROR=""
  if [ "${dest%.gpg}" = "$dest" ] || [ "${src%.gpg}" != "$src" ]; then
    cp "$src" "$dest" 2>/dev/null && return 0
    GD_DRIVE_ERROR="$(gd_drive_why "${dest%/*}")"
    return 1
  fi
  pass="$GD_PASS"
  [ -n "$pass" ] || pass="$(cat "$PASSFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$pass" ]; then
    GD_DRIVE_ERROR="no backup passphrase is stored for encrypted copies"
    return 1
  fi
  printf '%s' "$pass" | gpg --batch --quiet --yes --symmetric \
       --cipher-algo AES256 --passphrase-fd 0 --pinentry-mode loopback \
       --output "$dest" "$src" 2>/dev/null && return 0
  GD_DRIVE_ERROR="$(gd_drive_why "${dest%/*}")"
  return 1
}

# Keeps the newest RETENTION copies in one folder.
gd_drive_rotate() {
  { ls -1t "$1" 2>/dev/null || true; } | tail -n +$((RETENTION + 1)) \
    | while IFS= read -r old; do rm -rf -- "${1:?}/$old"; done || true
}

# What the last drive copy did, read by show-drives.
gd_drive_status() {
  install -d -m 755 "${DRIVESTATUS%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true
  {
    echo "DRIVE_AT=$(date +%s)"
    if [ -z "$1" ]; then echo "DRIVE_OK=1"; else echo "DRIVE_OK=0"; fi
    echo "DRIVE_ERROR='$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr '\r\n\t' '   ' | tr -d "'" | sed 's/^ *//' | cut -c1-400)'"
  } > "$DRIVESTATUS" 2>/dev/null || true
  chmod 644 "$DRIVESTATUS" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Records when a drive last took a copy.
gd_drive_seen() {
  if { grep -v "^$1 " "$DRIVELAST" 2>/dev/null || true; echo "$1 $(date +%s)"; } \
       > "$DRIVELAST.new" 2>/dev/null; then
    mv -f "$DRIVELAST.new" "$DRIVELAST" 2>/dev/null || true
    chmod 644 "$DRIVELAST" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}

# Writes one copy to one drive; prints where it landed, or why not.
gd_drive_put() {
  local out="$1" folder="$2/$3" name="$4"
  if ! install -d -m 700 "$folder" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "the drive could not be written"
    return 1
  fi
  # Leftovers of a copy cut short when the drive was pulled.
  rm -f "$folder"/.partial-* 2>/dev/null || true
  if gd_drive_write "$out" "$folder/.partial-$name" \
     && mv -f "$folder/.partial-$name" "$folder/$name" 2>/dev/null; then
    sync -f "$folder/$name" 2>/dev/null || true
    chmod 600 "$folder/$name" 2>/dev/null || true
    gd_drive_rotate "$folder"
    printf '%s\n' "$folder/$name"
    return 0
  fi
  rm -f "$folder/.partial-$name" 2>/dev/null || true
  printf '%s\n' "${GD_DRIVE_ERROR:-the drive could not be written}"
  return 1
}

# **A copy of each archive on every chosen USB drive.** A missing
# or full drive never fails the backup; it is recorded instead.
gd_drive_copy() {
  local out="$1" service="$2" name uuid target landed first="" failed=""
  load_drives
  if [ -z "$DRIVES" ] || [ "$DRIVE_MODE" = "local" ]; then return 0; fi
  name="$(basename "$out")"
  if [ "$DRIVE_ENCRYPT" -eq 1 ] && [ "${name%.gpg}" = "$name" ]; then name="$name.gpg"; fi
  for uuid in $DRIVES; do
    target="$(gd_drive_ready "$uuid")"
    if [ -z "$target" ]; then
      failed="$failed $(gd_drive_name "$uuid"): not connected;"
      continue
    fi
    if landed="$(gd_drive_put "$out" "$target" "$service" "$name")"; then
      printf '%s %s %s\n' 'GRYONIXNEXUS_DRIVE_COPY' "$uuid" "$landed"
      [ -n "$first" ] || first="$landed"
      gd_drive_seen "$uuid"
    else
      failed="$failed ${target##*/}: $landed;"
    fi
  done
  gd_drive_status "$failed"
  # Drives only: the local archive goes once a drive holds it.
  if [ "$DRIVE_MODE" = "drive" ] && [ -n "$first" ]; then
    rm -f "$out"
    printf '%s %s %s\n' 'GRYONIXNEXUS_BACKUP_DONE' \
      "$(stat -c %s "$first" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" "$first"
  fi
  return 0
}

# Copies the newest archive an external tool wrote.
gd_drive_copy_newest() {
  local newest
  newest="$({ ls -1t "$1/$2"-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -n 1)"
  [ -n "$newest" ] || return 0
  gd_drive_copy "$newest" "$2"
  # Drives only: the unpacked folder leaves with its archive.
  if [ ! -e "$newest" ] && [ -d "${newest%.tar.gz}" ]; then rm -rf "${newest%.tar.gz}"; fi
}

do_set_drives() {
  local mode="${1:-both}" encrypt="${2:-1}" checked="" uuid
  shift 2 || true
  case "$mode" in
    both|local|drive) ;;
    *) echo "unsupported drive mode: ${mode}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  case "$encrypt" in
    0|1) ;;
    *) echo "invalid encryption flag: ${encrypt}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  for uuid in "$@"; do
    case "$uuid" in
      ''|*[!0-9A-Fa-f-]*) echo "invalid drive id: ${uuid}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
    checked="$checked $uuid"
  done
  install -d -m 755 "$(dirname "$DRIVECONF")"
  cat > "$DRIVECONF" <<EOF_DRIVES
DRIVE_MODE=$mode
DRIVE_ENCRYPT=$encrypt
DRIVES='${checked# }'
EOF_DRIVES
  chmod 644 "$DRIVECONF"
  # A newly chosen drive counts from now.
  for uuid in $checked; do
    grep -q "^$uuid " "$DRIVELAST" 2>/dev/null || gd_drive_seen "$uuid"
  done
}

# Settings, each drive's state and the last copy, in one read.
do_show_drives() {
  local uuid target size avail
  load_drives
  printf 'DRIVE_MODE=%s\nDRIVE_ENCRYPT=%s\nDRIVES=%s\n' "$DRIVE_MODE" "$DRIVE_ENCRYPT" "$DRIVES"
  if [ -s "$PASSFILE" ]; then echo 'DRIVE_PASS=1'; else echo 'DRIVE_PASS=0'; fi
  for uuid in $DRIVES; do
    target="$(gd_drive_target "$uuid")"
    size=0
    avail=0
    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
      read -r size avail < <(df -B1 --output=size,avail "$target" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || true
      printf 'DRIVE=%s 1 %s %s %s\n' "$uuid" "${size:-0}" "${avail:-0}" "$target"
    else
      printf 'DRIVE=%s 0 0 0 %s\n' "$uuid" "$(gd_drive_fstab "$uuid")"
    fi
  done
  [ -s "$DRIVESTATUS" ] && cat "$DRIVESTATUS"
  return 0
}

# --- per-service locking (see LockSections) --------------------------

GD_LOCK_BUSY=75

gd_with_lock() {
  local id="$1"
  shift
  install -d -m 700 '/var/lib/gryonixnexus/locks'
  local fd
  exec {fd}>"/var/lib/gryonixnexus/locks/$id.lock"
  if ! flock -n "$fd"; then
    echo "$id: another backup or update for this service is already running, skipping" >&2
    return "$GD_LOCK_BUSY"
  fi
  "$@"
}

# --- helpers shared by every generated service body -----------------

gd_compose_stop() {
  local project="$1"
  shift
  docker compose -p "$project" stop "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

gd_compose_start() {
  local project="$1"
  shift
  docker compose -p "$project" start "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

# Container id of one compose service; empty when it is not running.
gd_container() {
  docker compose -p "$1" ps -q "$2" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
}

# A tar of a live database directory is a corrupt backup, so the
# database is dumped through its own client instead. The credentials
# come from the container's OWN environment — compose already put them
# there — because passing them from here would place the password in
# the argv of `docker exec`, readable by every account on the host.
gd_dump_postgres() {
  local cid
  cid="$(gd_container "$1" "$2")"
  if [ -z "$cid" ]; then
    echo "the $1 database container is not running" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! docker exec "$cid" sh -c \
       'PGPASSWORD="$POSTGRES_PASSWORD" exec pg_dump --clean --if-exists -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"' \
       > "$3"; then
    echo "the $1 database dump failed" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  [ -s "$3" ] || { echo "the $1 database dump is empty" >&2; return 1; }
}

# --single-transaction is what makes a dump of a RUNNING InnoDB
# database trustworthy: one consistent snapshot, no instance-wide lock.
# mariadb-dump on current images, mysqldump on older ones.
#
# A fourth argument names the database explicitly, for a service that
# keeps several in one engine and whose container therefore sets no
# MYSQL_DATABASE at all; without it the container's own variable is
# used, as it always was. Only the NAME travels here — the password is
# still read inside the container, never put in the argv of docker exec
# where /proc hands it to every account on the host.
gd_dump_mysql() {
  local cid
  cid="$(gd_container "$1" "$2")"
  if [ -z "$cid" ]; then
    echo "the $1 database container is not running" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! docker exec "$cid" sh -c \
       'if command -v mariadb-dump >/dev/null 2>&1; then D=mariadb-dump; else D=mysqldump; fi; MYSQL_PWD="$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD" exec "$D" --single-transaction --quick -u root "${1:-$MYSQL_DATABASE}"' \
       sh "${4:-}" > "$3"; then
    echo "the $1 database dump failed" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  [ -s "$3" ] || { echo "the $1 database dump is empty" >&2; return 1; }
}

# Keeps the newest RETENTION archives of one service — encrypted and
# plain together, they are one series. The pipeline is guarded: with
# fewer archives than RETENTION `ls` finds nothing to list and would
# fail the whole run under pipefail, which is every first run.
gd_rotate() {
  { ls -1t "$1/$2"-*.tar.gz "$1/$2"-*.tar.gz.gpg 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | tail -n +$((RETENTION + 1)) | xargs -r rm -f
}

# Encrypt (or not), put the archive in place, rotate, announce.
gd_finish() {
  local name="$1" dir="$2" plain="$3" work="$4" out=""
  if [ ! -s "$plain" ]; then
    rm -rf "$work"
    echo "the $name archive is empty" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if [ "$GD_ENCRYPT" -eq 1 ]; then
    out="$dir/$(basename "$plain").gpg"
    if ! printf '%s' "$GD_PASS" | gpg --batch --quiet --yes --symmetric \
         --cipher-algo AES256 --passphrase-fd 0 --pinentry-mode loopback \
         --output "$out" "$plain"; then
      rm -rf "$work"
      echo "could not encrypt the $name backup" >&2
      return 1
    fi
  else
    out="$dir/$(basename "$plain")"
    mv "$plain" "$out"
  fi
  # The plain archive never outlives the encrypted one.
  rm -rf "$work"
  chmod 600 "$out"
  chown "$OWNER" "$out" 2>/dev/null || true
  gd_rotate "$dir" "$name"
  # A streamed command carries no exit status back to the app, so the
  # archive announces itself: marker, size in bytes, path.
  printf '%s %s %s\n' 'GRYONIXNEXUS_BACKUP_DONE' \
    "$(stat -c %s "$out" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" "$out"
  # And then it leaves the machine, if a destination was chosen. After
  # the marker on purpose: the archive exists and is announced whatever
  # the far side does.
  gd_ship "$out" "$name"
  # A copy on each USB drive, after the far side.
  gd_drive_copy "$out" "$name"
}

# --- per-service bodies (generated from each service's BackupSpec) ---

backup_mailcow() {
  '/opt/mailcow-dockerized/bot-backup.sh'
  gd_drive_copy_newest '/opt/backups/mailcow' 'mailcow'
}

# The ONE dispatch both callers go through: the timer's `run` and the
# app's `backup`. Two copies of these bodies is exactly the drift this
# wrapper exists to prevent.
gd_run_service() {
  case "$1" in
    mailcow) gd_with_lock 'backup-mailcow' backup_mailcow ;;
    *) echo "unsupported service: $1" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}

# Whether a run of this service encrypts unless the caller says
# otherwise. Secret stores yes; bulk media no — GPG over a photo
# library costs hours of CPU on a Raspberry Pi.
gd_default_encrypt() {
  case "$1" in
    mailcow) echo 0 ;;
    *) echo 0 ;;
  esac
}

do_delete() {
  local path="${1:-}"
  # The path must sit inside a backup directory this deployment owns.
  # Without the check a whitelisted wrapper would delete ANY file.
  case "$path" in
    *..*) echo "invalid path: ${path}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  case "$path" in
    "/opt/backups/mailcow"/*) ;;
    "$DRIVEROOT"/*/*/*) ;;
    *) echo "path outside the backup directories: ${path}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  [ -e "$path" ] || { echo "no such backup: ${path}" >&2; exit 2; }
  rm -rf "$path"
}

do_run() {
  load_config
  local failed=""
  for svc in $SERVICES; do
    # Each service runs in its own subshell, and the `||` keeps errexit
    # from firing on a failure: an unattended run must not let one
    # broken service cancel the backups of every service after it.
    (
      GD_ENCRYPT="$(gd_default_encrypt "$svc")"
      GD_PASS=""
      if [ "$GD_ENCRYPT" -eq 1 ]; then
        # Unattended, so there is nobody to ask: the stored passphrase
        # is the only source. Without it the service refuses rather
        # than quietly writing its secrets out in the clear.
        if [ ! -s "$PASSFILE" ]; then
          echo "no backup passphrase stored for $svc" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        GD_PASS="$(cat "$PASSFILE")"
      fi
      gd_run_service "$svc"
    ) || failed="$failed $svc"
  done
  if [ -n "$failed" ]; then
    echo "backup failed for:$failed" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

# One service, on demand. Same bodies the timer runs; the only
# difference is where the passphrase comes from.
do_backup() {
  local svc="${1:-}"
  shift || true
  load_config
  GD_ENCRYPT="$(gd_default_encrypt "$svc")"
  for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
      --encrypt) GD_ENCRYPT=1 ;;
      --no-encrypt) GD_ENCRYPT=0 ;;
      *) echo "unsupported option: ${arg}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
  done
  if [ "$GD_ENCRYPT" -eq 1 ]; then
    # On stdin, never argv. A terminal means nobody piped anything in,
    # and reading would hang forever.
    if [ ! -t 0 ]; then GD_PASS="$(cat)"; fi
    # No passphrase given: fall back to the stored one, so an
    # encrypted run is possible without re-typing it.
    if [ -z "$GD_PASS" ] && [ -s "$PASSFILE" ]; then GD_PASS="$(cat "$PASSFILE")"; fi
    if [ -z "$GD_PASS" ]; then
      echo "an encrypted backup needs a passphrase on stdin" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
  fi
  gd_run_service "$svc"
}

# What a backup of this service would cost, in bytes, and what the
# backup filesystem still has free. Read-only, and the only reason the
# app can warn BEFORE starting an hours-long run.
do_estimate() {
  local svc="${1:-}" dir="" total=0 free="" sz=""
  local -a paths=()
  case "$svc" in
    mailcow) dir='/opt/backups/mailcow'; paths=('/opt/mailcow-dockerized' '/var/lib/docker/volumes/mailcowdockerized_'*) ;;
    *) echo "unsupported service: ${svc}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  install -d -m 750 "$dir"
  local p
  for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
    [ -e "$p" ] || continue
    sz="$(du -sb "$p" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)" || sz=""
    total=$((total + ${sz:-0}))
  done
  free="$(df -B1 --output=avail "$dir" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 | tr -cd '0-9')"
  printf '%s %s %s\n' 'GRYONIXNEXUS_BACKUP_ESTIMATE' "$total" "${free:-0}"
}

do_set_schedule() {
  # <schedule> is `off` or `every:<n><unit>@<HH:MM>` — the interval and
  # the time of day the user picked. Parsed here rather than taking a
  # raw OnCalendar expression: the wrapper is whitelisted in sudoers,
  # so it must not accept arbitrary systemd input from the client.
  local schedule="${1:-off}" retention="${2:-7}"
  shift 2 || true
  local services="$*"
  local oncal=""
  case "$schedule" in
    off) ;;
    every:*)
      local spec="${schedule#every:}"
      local every="${spec%@*}" at="${spec#*@}"
      local n="${every%[hd]}" unit="${every##*[0-9]}"
      case "$n" in
        ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "invalid interval: ${every}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
      esac
      [ "$n" -ge 1 ] || { echo "invalid interval: ${every}" >&2; exit 2; }
      case "$at" in
        [0-2][0-9]:[0-5][0-9]) ;;
        *) echo "invalid time: ${at}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
      esac
      [ "${at%%:*}" -le 23 ] || { echo "invalid time: ${at}" >&2; exit 2; }
      case "$unit" in
        h)
          # Every n hours, aligned to the chosen minute.
          if [ "$n" -ge 24 ]; then
            oncal="*-*-* ${at}:00"
          else
            oncal="*-*-* 00/${n}:${at#*:}:00"
          fi
          ;;
        d)
          # Every n days at the chosen time. systemd has no "every n
          # days" for n > 1, so those run daily-aligned on a day step.
          if [ "$n" -le 1 ]; then
            oncal="*-*-* ${at}:00"
          else
            oncal="*-*-01/${n} ${at}:00"
          fi
          ;;
        *) echo "invalid interval unit: ${every}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
      esac
      ;;
    *) echo "unsupported schedule: ${schedule}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  case "$retention" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "invalid retention: ${retention}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  [ "$retention" -ge 1 ] || { echo "invalid retention: ${retention}" >&2; exit 2; }
  # Only services this wrapper knows about may end up in the config.
  local checked=""
  for svc in $services; do
    for known in mailcow; do
      if [ "$svc" = "$known" ]; then checked="$checked $svc"; fi
    done
  done
  install -d -m 755 "$(dirname "$CONFIG")"
  cat > "$CONFIG" <<EOF_CONF
SCHEDULE=$schedule
RETENTION=$retention
SERVICES='${checked# }'
EOF_CONF
  # World-readable on purpose: it holds no secrets (the passphrase is
  # a separate 0600 file) and the app reads it without sudo.
  chmod 644 "$CONFIG"
  if [ "$schedule" = "off" ]; then
    systemctl disable --now 'gryonixnexus-autobackup.timer' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  else
    mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system
    cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-autobackup.timer <<EOF_TIMER
[Unit]
Description=gryonixNexus scheduled backups
[Timer]
OnCalendar=$oncal
# Servers are not up 24/7 — a missed window must still run.
Persistent=true
# Small jitter only: the user picked a specific time, so the run must
# not wander an hour away from it.
RandomizedDelaySec=5m
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF_TIMER
    systemctl daemon-reload
    # A bad OnCalendar would leave the timer permanently inactive —
    # catch it here, while the app is still listening. Only when the
    # tool is actually present: its ABSENCE must not reject a schedule
    # that is fine (minimal images ship without systemd-analyze).
    if command -v systemd-analyze >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      if ! systemd-analyze calendar "$oncal" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "invalid schedule expression: ${oncal}" >&2; exit 2
      fi
    fi
    systemctl enable --now 'gryonixnexus-autobackup.timer' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}

do_set_passphrase() {
  install -d -m 755 "$(dirname '/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup.pass')"
  # From stdin, never argv: argv is world-readable in /proc.
  local pass
  pass="$(cat)"
  if [ -z "$pass" ]; then echo "an empty passphrase is refused" >&2; exit 2; fi
  ( umask 077 && printf '%s' "$pass" > '/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup.pass' )
  chmod 600 '/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup.pass'
}

case "$ACTION" in
  delete) do_delete "${2:-}" ;;
  run) do_run ;;
  backup) shift; do_backup "$@" ;;
  estimate) do_estimate "${2:-}" ;;
  set-schedule) shift; do_set_schedule "$@" ;;
  set-passphrase) do_set_passphrase ;;
  set-destination) shift; do_set_destination "$@" ;;
  show-destination) do_show_destination ;;
  test-destination) do_test_destination ;;
  set-drives) shift; do_set_drives "$@" ;;
  show-drives) do_show_drives ;;
  *) echo "unsupported action: ${ACTION}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
echo 'GRYONIXNEXUS_BACKUP_CTL_DONE'
EOF_BACKUP_CTL
chmod 750 '/opt/gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh'
# 755: the schedule config inside is read by the app without sudo; the
# passphrase file next to it carries its own 0600.
install -d -m 755 /etc/gryonixnexus
backup /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-autobackup.service
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-autobackup.service <<'EOF_AUTOBACKUP_UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=gryonixNexus scheduled backup run
After=docker.service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/opt/gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh run
EOF_AUTOBACKUP_UNIT
systemctl daemon-reload
# The timer itself is created only when the user turns the schedule on.

chown root:root '/opt/gryonixnexus-agent-bootstrap.sh'

log "Установка помощника удаления для панели сервера"

cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-uninstall.sh <<'EOF_UNINSTALL'
#!/bin/bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — remove services or the whole gryonixNexus install.
# Usage: gryonixnexus-uninstall.sh <service|vpn|--all> [--purge-data] [--purge-backups]
# Default keeps data and backups on disk; the flags delete them (independently).
set -euo pipefail

TARGET="${1:-}"
PURGE_DATA=0
PURGE_BACKUPS=0
shift || true
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --purge-data) PURGE_DATA=1 ;;
    --purge-backups) PURGE_BACKUPS=1 ;;
  esac
done

compose_down() {
  if [ "$PURGE_DATA" -eq 1 ]; then
    # --rmi all also reclaims the images, but only the ones THIS
    # project's services use — the scoped replacement for the
    # `docker system prune -af` that used to run once at the end and
    # took every unused image and stopped container on the host with
    # it, ours or not. Images still referenced elsewhere are skipped
    # by docker itself.
    docker compose -p "$1" down --remove-orphans --volumes --rmi all >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  else
    docker compose -p "$1" down --remove-orphans >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}

# Unmounts fast storage bound inside each path, then deletes it.
purge_path() {
  local target mount source
  for target in "$@"; do
    [ -e "$target" ] || continue
    while read -r mount; do
      source="$(awk -v m="$mount" '$2 == m && $3 == "none" {print $1}' /etc/fstab)"
      umount "$mount" 2>/dev/null || true
      sed -i "\|[[:space:]]${mount}[[:space:]]none[[:space:]]|d" /etc/fstab
      if [ -n "$source" ]; then rm -rf "$source"; fi
    done < <(awk -v t="$target/" 'index($2, t) == 1 {print $2}' /proc/mounts | sort -r)
    rm -rf "$target"
  done
}

# Removes one site block from the Caddyfile. The header is the exact
# first line of the block as writeCaddyfile emits it (top-level `}` on
# its own line closes it) — wrapper and Caddyfile are regenerated
# together on every setup run, so the format cannot drift between them.
remove_caddy_site() {
  local f=/etc/caddy/Caddyfile
  [ -f "$f" ] || return 0
  awk -v start="$1 {" '
    $0 == start {skip=1; next}
    skip && $0 == "}" {skip=0; next}
    !skip {print}
  ' "$f" > "$f.gryonixnexus" && mv "$f.gryonixnexus" "$f"
  systemctl reload caddy 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Drops exactly the sudoers lines named — baked in by the generator
# from the SAME sudoersLines a service was whitelisted with, never
# rediscovered here. Staged and validated with visudo, the same way
# the whitelist is written: a set of lines that fails to parse (should
# never happen — they are asked in the format already on disk) leaves
# the whitelist untouched rather than risk one sudo cannot read.
remove_sudoers_lines() {
  local f=/etc/sudoers.d/gryonixnexus-control
  [ -f "$f" ] || return 0
  local tmp="$f.gryonixnexus"
  printf '%s\n' "$@" | grep -vFxf - "$f" > "$tmp" || true
  if [ -s "$tmp" ] && visudo -cf "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    mv "$tmp" "$f"
  else
    rm -f "$tmp"
  fi
}

uninstall_mailcow() {
  compose_down 'mailcowdockerized'
  remove_caddy_site 'mail.example.com'
  systemctl disable --now gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.timer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.service /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.timer /opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh
  systemctl daemon-reload || true
  rm -f '/opt/mailcow-dockerized/bot-backup.sh' '/opt/mailcow-dockerized'/bot-backup.sh.bak.* || true
  rm -f /opt/gryonixnexus-dkim.sh
  if [ "$PURGE_DATA" -eq 1 ]; then
    purge_path '/opt/mailcow-dockerized'
  fi
  if [ "$PURGE_BACKUPS" -eq 1 ]; then
    rm -rf '/opt/backups/mailcow'
  fi
  remove_sudoers_lines \
    'admin ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/docker compose -p mailcowdockerized ps' \
    'admin ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/docker compose -p mailcowdockerized restart' \
    'admin ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/docker compose -p mailcowdockerized start' \
    'admin ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/docker compose -p mailcowdockerized stop' \
    'admin ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /opt/gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh' \
    'admin ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /opt/gryonixnexus-restore.sh' \
    'admin ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/docker compose -p mailcowdockerized logs --tail 500 --timestamps' \
    'admin ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /opt/gryonixnexus-dkim.sh'
}

uninstall_all() {

  # setup, so it outlives the services unless it is stopped here.
  systemctl disable --now 'gryonixnexus-autoupdate.timer' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-autoupdate.timer /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-autoupdate.service
  rm -f '/etc/gryonixnexus/autoupdate.conf' '/var/lib/gryonixnexus/autoupdate-status.txt'
  rm -f '/opt/gryonixnexus-update-ctl.sh'

  # setup, so it outlives the services unless it is stopped here.
  systemctl disable --now 'gryonixnexus-autobackup.timer' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-autobackup.timer /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-autobackup.service

  rm -f '/opt/gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh'

  if [ -f /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexusd.service ]; then
    systemctl disable --now 'gryonixnexusd.service' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    rm -f '/etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexusd.service'
    systemctl daemon-reload || true
  fi

  rm -rf '/var/lib/gryonixnexus/agent'

  systemctl disable --now 'gryonixnexus-mdns.service' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f '/etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-mdns.service' '/usr/local/lib/gryonixnexus/mdns-aliases.sh' '/etc/caddy/gryonixnexus-home-network.caddy'
  # The agent's system updater and its start and shutdown units.
  systemctl disable --now 'gryonixnexus-update-at-start.service' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f '/etc/gryonixnexus/update-at-start.conf'
  systemctl disable --now 'gryonixnexus-update-at-stop.service' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  systemctl disable --now 'gryonixnexus-system-scheduled.timer' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f '/opt/gryonixnexus-system-ctl.sh' '/etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-update-at-start.service' '/etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-update-at-stop.service' '/var/log/gryonixnexus-system-update.log'
  rm -f '/etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-system-scheduled.timer' '/etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-system-scheduled.service' '/etc/gryonixnexus/system-schedule.conf'
  # The daemon before the rename (gryonixd). install-agent.sh removes
  # it, but a host that never re-ran the bootstrap still has it, and
  # its unit is Restart=always too.
  if [ -f /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus.service ]; then
    systemctl disable --now 'gryonixnexus.service' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    rm -f '/etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus.service'
    systemctl daemon-reload || true
  fi
  rm -f '/usr/local/bin/gryonixd' '/run/gryonixd.sock'
  # Host metrics collector + its history
  systemctl disable --now gryonixnexus-metrics >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-metrics.service /opt/gryonixnexus-metrics-collector.sh
  systemctl daemon-reload || true
  rm -rf /var/lib/gryonixnexus
  # Caddy: only the sites this app wrote are removed
  rest="$(mktemp)"
  { [ -f /etc/caddy/Caddyfile ] && awk '
    BEGIN{d=0;b="";own=0}
    d==0&&b==""&&index($0,"{")==0{print;next}
    {b=b $0 "\n"; if(index($0,"# gryonixnexus:"))own=1; t=$0; o=gsub(/[{]/,"",t); t=$0; c=gsub(/[}]/,"",t); d+=o-c;
     if(d<=0){ if(!own) printf "%s",b; b=""; own=0; d=0}}
    END{printf "%s",b}' /etc/caddy/Caddyfile > "$rest"; } || : > "$rest"
  if grep -Eq '^[^#[:space:]{}].*[{][[:space:]]*$' "$rest"; then
    cat "$rest" > /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
    { caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl reload caddy >/dev/null 2>&1; } || true

    systemctl disable --now caddy >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

  systemctl disable --now 'gryonixnexus-tunnel-watchdog.timer' 'gryonixnexus-tunnel-watchdog.service' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-tunnel-watchdog.timer /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-tunnel-watchdog.service '/opt/gryonixnexus-tunnel-watchdog.sh'

  # takes the route with it (ExecStop), and the unit goes the way every
  # other root-owned file this product wrote goes — the DDNS lesson.
  systemctl disable --now gryonixnexus-tunnel-endpoint.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-tunnel-endpoint.service
  systemctl daemon-reload || true
  rm -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-gryonixnexus-tunnel.conf
  systemctl reload ssh 2>/dev/null || systemctl reload sshd 2>/dev/null || true
  # Policy routing that sends relayed replies back through the
  # tunnel — armed by install(), re-synced by its own timer.
  systemctl disable --now 'gryonixnexus-relay-route-sync.timer' 'gryonixnexus-relay-route-sync.service' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-relay-route-sync.timer /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-relay-route-sync.service
  systemctl daemon-reload || true
  rm -f '/opt/gryonixnexus-relay-route-sync.sh'
  ip rule del fwmark '0x1' table '100' 2>/dev/null || true
  ip route flush table '100' 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-gryonixnexus-rpfilter.conf
  # No host-wide `docker system prune` here: image reclamation is done
  # per compose project by compose_down --rmi all, which cannot
  # reach Docker state this deployment did not create.
  # Dashboard wrappers, then our own whitelist last — after this line
  # the app's sudo access is gone, which is the point.
  rm -f '/opt/gryonixnexus-container-ctl.sh' '/opt/gryonixnexus-restore.sh'
  # The agent bootstrap wrapper and whatever sources it unpacked. A
  # root-owned script the erase leaves behind is the DDNS lesson: the
  # erased machine still carrying something only root can remove.
  rm -f '/opt/gryonixnexus-agent-bootstrap.sh'
  rm -rf '/opt/gryonixnexus-agent-src'
  # Backup copies the setup makes before overwriting a managed file.
  rm -f /etc/nftables.conf.bak.* /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf.bak.* /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-*.service.bak.* /opt/gryonixnexus-*.bak.* /opt/vaultwarden-update.sh.bak.* /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.bak.* /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-*.timer.bak.* /etc/sysctl.d/99-gryonixnexus-rpfilter.conf.bak.* || true
  # SSH password login comes back BEFORE the app key is stripped below,
  # so this machine is never left with neither way in.
  rm -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-gryonixnexus-no-password.conf
  systemctl reload ssh 2>/dev/null || systemctl reload sshd 2>/dev/null || true
  APP_KEY='ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFake gryonixnexus-app'
  USER_HOME="$(getent passwd 'admin' | cut -d: -f6 || true)"
  if [ -n "$USER_HOME" ] && [ -f "$USER_HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys" ]; then
    grep -vxF "$APP_KEY" "$USER_HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys" > "$USER_HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys.gryonixnexus" || true
    mv "$USER_HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys.gryonixnexus" "$USER_HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys"
    chmod 600 "$USER_HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys"
    # Root wrote the replacement, and sshd reads authorized_keys as
    # the account: leaving it root-owned makes the file unreadable to
    # sshd and kills every OTHER key the account has. Same reason the
    # revoke step chowns; see revokeInstallKey.
    chown 'admin' "$USER_HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys"
  fi
  rm -f /etc/sudoers.d/gryonixnexus-control
  rm -f '/opt/gryonixnexus-uninstall.sh'
}

  install -d /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d
  printf 'PerSourcePenaltyExemptList %s\n' '10.8.0.1' > /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-gryonixnexus-tunnel.conf
  systemctl reload ssh 2>/dev/null || systemctl reload sshd 2>/dev/null || true
fi

log "SSH: закрываем вход по паролю — ключ приложения уже на этом хосте"
SSHD_APP_KEY='ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFake gryonixnexus-app'
SSHD_USER_HOME="$(getent passwd 'admin' | cut -d: -f6 || true)"
SSHD_KEYS="$SSHD_USER_HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys"
SSHD_CLOSE=0
if command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -n "$SSHD_USER_HOME" ] && [ -s "$SSHD_KEYS" ]; then
  if grep -qxF "$SSHD_APP_KEY" "$SSHD_KEYS"; then SSHD_CLOSE=1; fi
fi
if [ "$SSHD_CLOSE" -eq 1 ]; then
  # **Every step here is allowed to fail without taking the install
  # with it.** The script runs under `set -e`, and the services are up
  # by the time this runs: a host whose /etc could not be written is a
  # host that keeps password login, not a failed installation — and
  # aborting here would lose the report and the install-key revocation
  # that come after it.
  SSHD_WROTE=1
  install -d -m 755 /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d || SSHD_WROTE=0
  # A single-quoted literal rather than a heredoc: the terminator would
  # have to sit at column 0 inside this indented block, and the body is
  # shared byte-for-byte with the agent, which keeps it free of the one
  # character that could end this literal early.
  printf '%s' '# Managed by gryonixNexus.
#
# Written only after the app key was proven present on the control user of
# this host. Numbered 10 so it is obtained BEFORE 50-cloud-init.conf: sshd
# keeps the FIRST value it sees for a keyword, and cloud images ship
# PasswordAuthentication yes in that file.
#
# Remove this file and reload ssh to take passwords again.
PasswordAuthentication no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
' > '/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-gryonixnexus-no-password.conf.staged' || SSHD_WROTE=0
  chmod 644 '/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-gryonixnexus-no-password.conf.staged' 2>/dev/null || SSHD_WROTE=0
  mv '/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-gryonixnexus-no-password.conf.staged' '/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-gryonixnexus-no-password.conf' 2>/dev/null || SSHD_WROTE=0
  if [ "$SSHD_WROTE" -eq 0 ] || [ ! -f '/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-gryonixnexus-no-password.conf' ]; then
    rm -f '/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-gryonixnexus-no-password.conf.staged'
    echo "Вход по паролю SSH ОСТАЁТСЯ включённым: файл конфигурации вообще не удалось записать на этот хост"
  elif sshd -t; then
    systemctl reload ssh 2>/dev/null || systemctl reload sshd 2>/dev/null || true
    # **The only proof that survives contact with a real host.** A file
    # on disk says nothing about the MERGED configuration: sshd keeps
    # the FIRST value it obtains for a keyword, and a cloud image whose
    # own sshd_config.d file says yes would leave every step above
    # successful and the door open. sshd -T prints what it resolved.
    SSHD_EFFECTIVE="$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' || true)"
    case "$SSHD_EFFECTIVE" in
      *"passwordauthentication no"*)
        case "$SSHD_EFFECTIVE" in
          *"kbdinteractiveauthentication no"*) ;;
          *) echo "Вход по паролю SSH ОСТАЁТСЯ включённым: sshd всё ещё принимает пароли, хотя файл на месте — значит побеждает что-то более раннее в его конфигурации, обычно собственный файл sshd_config.d облачного образа" ;;
        esac
        ;;
      *) echo "Вход по паролю SSH ОСТАЁТСЯ включённым: sshd всё ещё принимает пароли, хотя файл на месте — значит побеждает что-то более раннее в его конфигурации, обычно собственный файл sshd_config.d облачного образа" ;;
    esac
  else
    rm -f '/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-gryonixnexus-no-password.conf'
    echo "Вход по паролю SSH ОСТАЁТСЯ включённым: sshd отверг конфигурацию с этим файлом, и файл убран обратно"
  fi
else
  echo "Вход по паролю SSH ОСТАЁТСЯ включённым: ключа приложения нет у управляющего пользователя, а закрывать дверь до подтверждения ключа — потерять хост"
fi

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 14/15"
echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_REPORT_BEGIN"
set +e

GD_REPORT_TMP="$(mktemp)"

for s in nftables docker caddy; do

echo "Не забудьте DNS-записи из dns-records.txt — без них Caddy не выпустит сертификаты."

echo "=== ДОСТУПЫ СЕРВИСОВ (сохраните) ==="
echo "Mailcow:      https://mail.example.com  (каталог: /opt/mailcow-dockerized)"
echo "  Администратор: admin"

set -e

echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_STEP 15/15"
if [ -z "${GRYONIXNEXUS_SKIP_SERVICES:-}" ]; then
log "Отзыв временного root-доступа приложения (ключ установки)"
APP_KEY='ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFakeFake gryonixnexus-app'
CONTROL_USER='admin'
revoke_key_for() {
  # Explicit ifs rather than `[ … ] && …` chains: this runs under
  # `set -e`, where a chain whose test fails carries that status on.
  if [ "$1" = "$CONTROL_USER" ]; then return 0; fi
  home_dir="$(getent passwd "$1" | cut -d: -f6 || true)"
  if [ -z "$home_dir" ]; then return 0; fi
  keys="$home_dir/.ssh/authorized_keys"
  if [ ! -f "$keys" ]; then return 0; fi
  if ! grep -qxF "$APP_KEY" "$keys"; then return 0; fi
  grep -vxF "$APP_KEY" "$keys" > "$keys.gryonixnexus" || true
  mv "$keys.gryonixnexus" "$keys"
  chmod 600 "$keys"
  # The rewrite runs as root, so the file it leaves behind is
  # root-owned — and sshd opens authorized_keys AS THE ACCOUNT, not as
  # root. A root-owned 0600 file is unreadable to it ("Could not open
  # user 'x' authorized keys … Permission denied"), so revoking the
  # app's key takes EVERY OTHER key on that account with it: the
  # owner's own key stops working at the last step of an install that
  # just reported success, and a `sudo -n` install locks them out of
  # the account they installed from. Ownership has to be put back

#!/usr/sbin/nft -f
# Managed by gryonixNexus — single-server firewall (default-deny).
flush ruleset

table inet filter {
    chain input {
        type filter hook input priority filter; policy drop;
        iif "lo" accept
        ct state established,related accept
        ct state invalid drop
        meta l4proto icmp icmp type { echo-request, destination-unreachable, time-exceeded, parameter-problem } limit rate 10/second accept
        meta l4proto ipv6-icmp accept
        tcp dport 22 meter gryonixnexus_ssh_throttle4 { ip saddr timeout 60s limit rate 10/minute burst 5 packets } accept comment "SSH, per-source throttle"
        tcp dport 22 meter gryonixnexus_ssh_throttle6 { ip6 saddr timeout 60s limit rate 10/minute burst 5 packets } accept comment "SSH, per-source throttle"

        tcp dport { 25, 80, 143, 443, 465, 587, 993, 2222, 4190 } accept comment "mail + HTTP for ACME"
        udp dport { 51821 } accept comment "VPN clients"
        jump gryonixnexus_services
    }

        # Filled by the control-plane agent when it installs a service that

        # this file). Empty means nothing extra is open.
        chain gryonixnexus_services {
        }    # No forward chain: Docker hooks its own drop-policy forward
    # chain with per-container accepts; a second drop-policy

}
