def api_email_put():
    data = request.json or {}
    current = smtp_conf()
    conf = {
        "host": (data.get("host") or "").strip()[:200],
        "port": int(data.get("port") or 587),
        "security": data.get("security") if data.get("security") in ("starttls", "ssl", "none") else "starttls",
        "username": (data.get("username") or "").strip()[:200],
        "sender": (data.get("sender") or "").strip()[:200],
        # An omitted password keeps the stored one — the UI never sees it,
        # so it cannot send it back.
        "password": data.get("password") if data.get("password") else current.get("password", ""),
    }
    save(SMTP_CONF, conf)
    return jsonify({"ok": True, "smtp": public_smtp(conf)})

@app.post("/api/email/test")
@require_admin
def api_email_test():
    me = current_user()
    target = (request.json or {}).get("to") or me.get("email")
    if not target:
        return jsonify({"error": "Add an e-mail address to your account first."}), 400
    if not send_mail(target, "Gryonix VPN test", "Your VPN panel can send e-mail."):
        return jsonify({"error": "Sending failed. Check the server, port and credentials."}), 502
    return jsonify({"ok": True})

@app.post("/forgot")
@serialized
def forgot():
    ip = client_ip()
    # Throttled like the login form: this endpoint is unauthenticated.
    if rate_limited("forgot", ip):
        return jsonify({"error": "Too many attempts. Please wait a few minutes."}), 429
    note_fail("forgot", ip)
    wanted = ((request.json or {}).get("username") or "").strip()
    user = find_user_by_name(wanted) or next(
        (u for u in users() if u.get("email", "").lower() == wanted.lower() and u.get("email")), None)
    if user and user.get("email"):
        token = issue_reset(user)
        # The link is built from the panel's own configured hostname, never
        # from the Host header: a spoofed Host must not steer a valid reset
        # token to an attacker's domain. WG_HOST is the vhost Caddy serves
        # this panel on (and the upstream speaks plain HTTP behind the
        # proxy, so url_root would also get the scheme wrong).
        link = "https://" + WG_HOST + "/reset?token=" + token
        send_mail(user["email"], "Reset your VPN panel password",
                  "Someone asked to reset the password for your VPN panel account "
                  f"({user['username']}).\n\nOpen this link within the hour to choose a new one:\n"
                  f"{link}\n\nIf that was not you, ignore this message — nothing has changed.")
    # Always the same answer: whether an account or a mailbox exists is not
    # something a stranger gets to find out.
    return jsonify({"ok": True})

@app.get("/reset")
def reset_page():
    return send_file("/app/reset.html")

@app.post("/reset")
@serialized
def reset_apply():
    data = request.json or {}
    password = data.get("password") or ""
    if len(password) < 8:
        return jsonify({"error": "The password must be at least 8 characters."}), 400
    user = consume_reset(data.get("token"))
    if not user:
        return jsonify({"error": "This link has expired. Ask for a new one."}), 400
    all_users = users()
    for u in all_users:
        if u["id"] == user["id"]:
            set_password(u, password)
    save(USERS, all_users)
    # Whoever holds an older session for this account is signed out, which is
    # the point of a reset asked for by someone who lost the password.
    return jsonify({"ok": True})

@app.post("/api/account/password")
@require_auth
@serialized
def api_own_password():
    data = request.json or {}
    me = current_user()
    if not verify_pw(data.get("current") or "", me):
        return jsonify({"error": "The current password is wrong."}), 403
    new = data.get("password") or ""
    if len(new) < 8:
        return jsonify({"error": "The password must be at least 8 characters."}), 400
    all_users = users()
    for u in all_users:
        if u["id"] == me["id"]:
            set_password(u, new)
            # The session doing the changing carries on; every other one that
            # was opened with the old password stops here.
            session["pv"] = u["pw_ver"]
    save(USERS, all_users)
    return jsonify({"ok": True})

@app.get("/api/<proto>/clients/<cid>/qr")
@require_auth
def api_qr(proto, cid):
    if proto not in HANDLERS: abort(404)
    if not owns(proto, cid): abort(403)
    png = subprocess.run(["qrencode", "-t", "PNG", "-m", "1", "-s", "6", "-o", "-"],
                         input=HANDLERS[proto][3](cid).encode(), capture_output=True).stdout
    return Response(png, mimetype="image/png")

    svc = load(f"{DATA}/services.json", {"services": []})

        ensure_server(); wg_up(ensure_server())
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=80)

#!/bin/bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — VPN-only access switch for admin web panels.
# on = every site; only host... = just those sites (per-service
# selection); off = public again. Every Caddy site imports the guard,
# so a host matcher inside it narrows which vhosts actually block.
set -euo pipefail
GUARD=/etc/caddy/gryonixnexus-admin-guard
# Shown to blocked visitors so a locked panel is a clear "denied"
# page, not an empty-bodied 403 that browsers render as a blank
# white screen. It names WireGuard specifically: whoever reads this
# page is most often already connected to the VPN — on AmneziaWG or
# one of the proxy protocols, which do not carry admin traffic — so
# "connect to the VPN" would be advice they already followed.
# ASCII only and no quotes: it rides through a Caddyfile heredoc and
# lands inside a double-quoted respond argument.
DENY='Access denied. The admin panels are reachable only over the VPN. Connect to your VPN and try again.'
reload_caddy() { systemctl reload caddy 2>/dev/null || systemctl restart caddy || true; }
write_guard() {
  hosts="$1"
  # Scenario-A hairpin allow-source. VPN clients on the containerised
  # protocols (amneziaWG / OpenVPN / shadowsocks / xray) that open an
  # admin panel served on THIS host's own public IP loop back through
  # the protocol/host NAT and reach Caddy SNAT'd to that public IP — a
  # source private_ranges does not cover, so the guard used to 403 a
  # genuinely VPN-side client (only the panel's own WireGuard, which
  # arrives from a private address, got through). No off-box client can
  # forge our own public IP as its source — the TCP return path comes
  # straight back to us — so our own global addresses are a safe allow.
  # This is the scenario-A counterpart to the 10.8.0.254 relay hairpin.
  selfip=$(
    { ip -4 -o addr show scope global; ip -6 -o addr show scope global; } 2>/dev/null \
      | awk '{ split($4, a, "/"); ip = a[1]; print ip (index(ip, ":") ? "/128" : "/32") }' \
      | paste -sd' ' -
  )
  # Cloudflare Tunnel visitors come from loopback; its header marks them.
  {
    if [ -n "$hosts" ]; then
      printf '@gryonixnexus_relay {\n'
      printf '    host %s\n' "$hosts"
      printf '    remote_ip 10.8.0.0/24\n'
      printf '    not remote_ip 10.8.0.254/32\n'
      printf '}\n'
      printf 'respond @gryonixnexus_relay "%s" 403\n' "$DENY"
      printf '@gryonixnexus_public {\n'
      printf '    host %s\n' "$hosts"
      printf '    not remote_ip private_ranges %s\n' "$selfip"
      printf '}\n'
      printf 'respond @gryonixnexus_public "%s" 403\n' "$DENY"
      printf '@gryonixnexus_tunnel {\n'
      printf '    host %s\n' "$hosts"
      printf '    header Cf-Connecting-IP *\n'
      printf '}\n'
      printf 'respond @gryonixnexus_tunnel "%s" 403\n' "$DENY"
    else
      printf '@gryonixnexus_relay {\n'
      printf '    remote_ip 10.8.0.0/24\n'
      printf '    not remote_ip 10.8.0.254/32\n'
      printf '}\n'
      printf 'respond @gryonixnexus_relay "%s" 403\n' "$DENY"
      printf '@gryonixnexus_public not remote_ip private_ranges %s\n' "$selfip"
      printf 'respond @gryonixnexus_public "%s" 403\n' "$DENY"
      printf '@gryonixnexus_tunnel header Cf-Connecting-IP *\n'
      printf 'respond @gryonixnexus_tunnel "%s" 403\n' "$DENY"
    fi
  } > "$GUARD"
  reload_caddy
}
case "${1:-status}" in
  on)
    write_guard ""
    echo on ;;
  only)
    shift
    [ "$#" -ge 1 ] || { echo "usage: $0 only host..." >&2; exit 64; }
    for h in "$@"; do
      case "$h" in
        *[!A-Za-z0-9.-]*|"") echo "invalid host: $h" >&2; exit 64 ;;
      esac
    done
    write_guard "$*"
    echo "only $*" ;;
  off)
    : > "$GUARD"
    reload_caddy
    echo off ;;
  status)
    if [ ! -s "$GUARD" ]; then
      echo off
    elif grep -q 'host ' "$GUARD"; then
      echo "only $(grep -m1 'host ' "$GUARD" | sed 's/^ *host //')"
    else
      echo on
    fi ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: $0 on|off|only host...|status" >&2; exit 64 ;;
esac

# and appended below ours. Blocks are separated by a blank line and open
# with their names — the shape this file is written in on both routes,
# and the one the agent splits on. A block is ours when its header is
# one of ours or its owner line names a service of ours; the global
# options block is dropped, because ours already carries it first.
# Anything left claiming a name we serve stops the run: two blocks on
# one name make Caddy refuse the whole file, which would take down every
# site on the machine at the next restart.

        return

          line = block[i]

          gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", parts[i])

#!/bin/bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — restore a service from a backup.
# Usage: gryonixnexus-restore.sh <mailcow|vaultwarden|nextcloud|immich|forgejo|gitlab|vpn-panel> <archive>
#        GPG passphrase (encrypted archives only) on stdin.
set -euo pipefail

SERVICE="${1:-}"
ARCHIVE="${2:-}"

MAILCOW_PATH='/opt/mailcow-dockerized'
MAILCOW_BACKUPS='/opt/backups/mailcow'
VW_CONTAINER='vaultwarden'
VW_DATA='/opt/vaultwarden/data'
VW_BACKUPS='/opt/backups/vaultwarden'
STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"

# The archive must sit inside a backup directory this deployment owns.
# Without the check a whitelisted wrapper would happily unpack ANY
# root-readable file over a service's data directory.
case "$ARCHIVE" in
  *..*) echo "invalid path: ${ARCHIVE}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
case "$ARCHIVE" in
  "$MAILCOW_BACKUPS"/*|"$VW_BACKUPS"/*|"/opt/backups/nextcloud"/*|"/opt/backups/immich"/*|"/opt/backups/forgejo"/*|"/opt/backups/gitlab"/*|"/opt/backups/vpn-panel"/*) ;;
  *) echo "path outside the backup directories: ${ARCHIVE}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
[ -e "$ARCHIVE" ] || { echo "no such backup: ${ARCHIVE}" >&2; exit 2; }

gd_compose_stop() {
  local project="$1"
  shift
  docker compose -p "$project" stop "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

gd_compose_start() {
  local project="$1"
  shift
  docker compose -p "$project" start "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

# Everything the project has, so the service is up again whatever the
# restore did — the same guarantee the vaultwarden arm gives.
gd_compose_start_all() {
  docker compose -p "$1" start >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

gd_container() {
  docker compose -p "$1" ps -q "$2" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
}

# A container that has just been started reports "up" long before its
# engine accepts connections, and a dump loaded into it then fails with
# a connection error that reads exactly like a corrupt backup.
gd_db_wait() {
  local cid="$1" engine="$2" deadline
  deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 180 ))
  while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$deadline" ]; do
    case "$engine" in
      postgres)
        if docker exec "$cid" sh -c 'exec pg_isready -q -U "$POSTGRES_USER"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          return 0
        fi
        ;;
      mysql)
        if docker exec "$cid" sh -c 'if command -v mariadb-admin >/dev/null 2>&1; then A=mariadb-admin; else A=mysqladmin; fi; MYSQL_PWD="$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD" exec "$A" ping -u root' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          return 0
        fi
        ;;
    esac
    sleep 3
  done
  return 1
}

# The credentials come from the container's OWN environment (compose
# put them there), never from the argv of docker exec — that is
# world-readable through /proc on the host.
gd_load_postgres() {
  local cid
  cid="$(gd_container "$1" "$2")"
  if [ -z "$cid" ]; then echo "the $1 database container is not running" >&2; return 1; fi
  if ! gd_db_wait "$cid" postgres; then echo "the $1 database never became ready" >&2; return 1; fi
  if [ ! -s "$3" ]; then echo "the archive carries no $1 database dump" >&2; return 1; fi
  # ON_ERROR_STOP: without it psql replays half a dump and still exits
  # 0, i.e. reports a restore that did not happen.
  if ! docker exec -i "$cid" sh -c \
       'PGPASSWORD="$POSTGRES_PASSWORD" exec psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"' \
       < "$3"; then
    echo "the $1 database could not be loaded" >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

# The fourth argument mirrors gd_dump_mysql: a service that keeps
# several databases in one engine names each one, and the load has to
# put each dump back where it came from.
gd_load_mysql() {
  local cid
  cid="$(gd_container "$1" "$2")"
  if [ -z "$cid" ]; then echo "the $1 database container is not running" >&2; return 1; fi
  if ! gd_db_wait "$cid" mysql; then echo "the $1 database never became ready" >&2; return 1; fi
  if [ ! -s "$3" ]; then echo "the archive carries no $1 database dump" >&2; return 1; fi
  if ! docker exec -i "$cid" sh -c \
       'if command -v mariadb >/dev/null 2>&1; then C=mariadb; else C=mysql; fi; MYSQL_PWD="$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD" exec "$C" -u root "${1:-$MYSQL_DATABASE}"' \
       sh "${4:-}" < "$3"; then
    echo "the $1 database could not be loaded" >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

restore_mailcow() {
  [ -x "$MAILCOW_PATH/helper-scripts/backup_and_restore.sh" ] \
    || { echo "mailcow not found in /opt/mailcow-dockerized" >&2; exit 1; }
  # mailcow's helper restores from a DIRECTORY inside its backup
  # location and picks it from a numbered menu. Stage the chosen backup
  # alone in a scratch location so that menu has exactly one entry.
  local stage="$MAILCOW_BACKUPS/.restore-$STAMP"
  mkdir -p "$stage"
  chmod 0777 "$stage"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2064
  trap "rm -rf '$stage'" EXIT
  local plain="$ARCHIVE"
  case "$ARCHIVE" in
    *.gpg)
      plain="$stage/.restore.tar.gz"
      gpg --batch --quiet --yes --decrypt --passphrase-fd 0 \
          --pinentry-mode loopback --output "$plain" "$ARCHIVE" \
        || { echo "could not decrypt the backup (wrong passphrase?)" >&2; exit 1; }
      ;;
  esac
  if [ -d "$ARCHIVE" ]; then
    cp -a "$ARCHIVE" "$stage/"
  else
    tar -xzf "$plain" -C "$stage"
    rm -f "$stage/.restore.tar.gz"
  fi
  export MAILCOW_BACKUP_LOCATION="$stage"
  # Bounded input, never `yes` (SIGPIPE under pipefail kills the pipeline).
  # The helper asks exactly two questions and then restores ONCE:
  # "Select a restore point" -> 1, the only staged backup; "Select a
  # dataset to restore" -> 0, the "[ 0 ] - all" entry, which expands to
  # every dataset in the backup (restore() loops over its arguments).
  # Feeding component indices one after another instead — as this did —
  # restores a SINGLE component and discards the rest of the input when
  # the helper exits, and which component index 1 refers to is whatever
  # `ls -f` returns first, so the survivor varied per run while the
  # wrapper still reported success.
  # The trailing "n" answers the vmail branch's "Force a resync now?";
  # extra input is harmless, a missing answer would depend on EOF.
  # Under `timeout` because an unrecognised prompt would otherwise wait
  # for a human that is never coming.
  printf '1\n0\nn\n' \
    | timeout 3600 "$MAILCOW_PATH/helper-scripts/backup_and_restore.sh" restore
}

restore_vaultwarden() {
  local plain="$ARCHIVE" tmp="" stage="" root="" previous="" saved=0
  case "$ARCHIVE" in
    *.gpg)
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
      # shellcheck disable=SC2064
      trap "rm -rf '$tmp'" EXIT
      plain="$tmp/restore.tar.gz"
      # --passphrase-fd 0: the secret arrives on stdin, never in argv.
      gpg --batch --quiet --yes --decrypt --passphrase-fd 0 \
          --pinentry-mode loopback --output "$plain" "$ARCHIVE" \
        || { echo "could not decrypt the backup (wrong passphrase?)" >&2; exit 1; }
      ;;
  esac
  # Verify BEFORE touching live data: a truncated upload must not cost
  # the user the data they still have.
  tar -tzf "$plain" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || { echo "the backup archive is not readable" >&2; exit 1; }
  # Unpacked aside; only the archived data directory is moved in.
  root="$(tar -tzf "$plain" | sed -n '1{s|^\./||;s|/*$||;p;}')"
  case "/$root/" in
    //|*/../*|*/./*) echo "the archive carries no vaultwarden data" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$VW_DATA")"
  stage="$(mktemp -d "$(dirname "$VW_DATA")/.restore-XXXXXX")"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2064
  trap "rm -rf '$stage' '$tmp'" EXIT
  tar --numeric-owner -xzf "$plain" -C "$stage" \
    || { echo "the backup archive is not readable" >&2; exit 1; }
  if [ ! -d "$stage/$root" ] || [ -L "$stage/$root" ]; then
    echo "the archive carries no vaultwarden data" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  docker stop "$VW_CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  # The old data is moved aside, never deleted: if the move fails it is
  # the only way back, and the container must come up again either way.
  previous="${VW_DATA}.pre-restore-$STAMP"
  if [ -d "$VW_DATA" ]; then mv "$VW_DATA" "$previous"; saved=1; fi
  if mv "$stage/$root" "$VW_DATA"; then
    if [ "$saved" -eq 1 ]; then echo "previous data kept at ${previous}"; fi
  else
    echo "restore failed, rolling back to the previous data" >&2
    rm -rf "$VW_DATA"
    if [ "$saved" -eq 1 ]; then mv "$previous" "$VW_DATA"; fi
    docker start "$VW_CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    exit 1
  fi
  docker start "$VW_CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

restore_nextcloud() {
  local plain="$ARCHIVE" tmp="" stage="" previous="" saved=0 rc=0

    *.gpg)

           --pinentry-mode loopback --output "$plain" "$ARCHIVE"; then
        rm -rf "$tmp"
        echo "could not decrypt the backup (wrong passphrase?)" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      ;;
  esac
  # Verified BEFORE anything is stopped: a truncated upload must not
  # cost the user the data they still have.
  if ! tar -tzf "$plain" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    echo "the backup archive is not readable" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # Staged on the SERVICE's own filesystem, so putting the data back
  # is a rename rather than a second copy of the whole directory.
  stage="$(mktemp -d '/opt/nextcloud/.restore-XXXXXX')"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2064
  trap "rm -rf '$stage' '$tmp'" EXIT
  tar --numeric-owner -xzf "$plain" -C "$stage"
  if [ ! -d "$stage/data" ]; then
    echo "the archive carries no nextcloud data" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  gd_compose_stop 'nextcloud' 'app'
  # The old data is moved aside, never deleted: if the move back
  # fails it is the only way home.
  previous='/opt/nextcloud/data'".pre-restore-$STAMP"
  if [ -d '/opt/nextcloud/data' ]; then mv '/opt/nextcloud/data' "$previous"; saved=1; fi
  if mv "$stage/data" '/opt/nextcloud/data'; then
    if [ "$saved" -eq 1 ]; then echo "previous data kept at ${previous}"; fi
  else
    echo "restore failed, rolling back to the previous data" >&2
    rm -rf '/opt/nextcloud/data'
    if [ "$saved" -eq 1 ]; then mv "$previous" '/opt/nextcloud/data'; fi
    gd_compose_start_all 'nextcloud'
    exit 1
  fi
  # The database container has to be up to take its dump back;
  # the rest of the project stays down until it is loaded.
  gd_compose_start 'nextcloud' 'db'
  gd_load_mysql 'nextcloud' 'db' "$stage/gryonixnexus-db/nextcloud.sql" || rc=1
  # Up again on every path, restored or not.
  gd_compose_start_all 'nextcloud'
  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "the nextcloud database could not be restored" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh <<'EOF_BACKUP_CTL'
#!/bin/bash
# Managed by gryonixNexus — backup housekeeping for the Server Dashboard.
# Usage: gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh delete <path>
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh set-schedule <off|every:<n><h|d>@<HH:MM>> <retention> [services...]
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh set-passphrase   (passphrase on stdin)
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh run
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh backup <service> [--encrypt|--no-encrypt]
#                                       (GPG passphrase on stdin when encrypting)
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh estimate <service>
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh set-destination <kind> <host> <port> <user> <path> <bucket> <keep>
#                                       (credential on stdin, optional)
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh show-destination
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh test-destination
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh set-drives <both|local|drive> <1|0> [uuids...]
#        gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh show-drives
set -euo pipefail

ACTION="${1:-}"
CONFIG='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup.conf'
PASSFILE='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup.pass'
DESTCONF='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup-dest.conf'
DESTKEY='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup-dest.key'
DESTPUB='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup-dest.key.pub'
DESTSTATUS='/etc/gryonixnexus/autobackup-dest.status'
RETENTION=7
SERVICES='mailcow vaultwarden nextcloud immich forgejo gitlab vpn-panel'
SCHEDULE=off
# The control user. Finished archives are chowned to it: the app
# downloads and shares them, and what keeps other accounts away is the
# 0750 on the enclosing backup root, not the file's owner.
OWNER='admin'
# Encryption state of the CURRENT run. The passphrase lives in a shell
# variable and reaches gpg down a pipe — never in argv, which is
# world-readable through /proc.
GD_ENCRYPT=0
GD_PASS=""

load_config() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  [ -f "$CONFIG" ] && . "$CONFIG"
  # A config from an older build may not set every value.
  : "${SCHEDULE:=off}" "${RETENTION:=7}" "${SERVICES:=mailcow vaultwarden nextcloud immich forgejo gitlab vpn-panel}"
  case "$RETENTION" in ''|*[!0-9]*|0) RETENTION=1 ;; esac
}

# Where finished archives are sent, if anywhere. Its own file and its
# own loader: a host that never chose a destination keeps every default
# below, which together mean "leave the archive where it is".
DEST_KIND=none
DEST_HOST=""
DEST_PORT=22
DEST_USER=""
DEST_PATH=""
DEST_BUCKET=""
DEST_KEEP=0
load_destination() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  [ -f "$DESTCONF" ] && . "$DESTCONF"
  : "${DEST_KIND:=none}" "${DEST_PORT:=22}" "${DEST_KEEP:=0}"
}

# **Where a copy of this machine's archives lands so they survive the
# machine.** Called after every archive this wrapper finishes, by the
# timer and by the app's own button alike — one body, both callers, the
# rule this whole file is built on.
#
# Failure NEVER fails the backup: the archive on this disk is real and
# already written, and refusing it because a bucket was unreachable
# would turn a bad night into no backup at all. What a failure does is
# get RECORDED, because a copy that silently never leaves is the exact
# defect this exists to end.
gd_ship() {
  local out="$1" service="${2:-check}" error="" ok=0
  load_destination
  [ "$DEST_KIND" = "none" ] && return 0
  # One folder per machine and service, so rotation stays inside it.
  local machine
  machine="$(hostname -s 2>/dev/null || echo server)-$(cut -c1-8 /etc/machine-id 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  local folder="${DEST_PATH%/}/$machine/$service"
  case "$DEST_KIND" in
    ssh)
      if [ -z "$DEST_HOST" ] || [ -z "$DEST_USER" ] || [ ! -s "$DESTKEY" ]; then
        error="the destination is incomplete (host, user or key missing)"
      else
        # **A known_hosts this machine can actually write.** Run from the agent's unit,
        # ssh cannot create /root/.ssh — ProtectHome=yes and
        # ProtectSystem=full — so `accept-new` pinned nothing and every
        # shipment carried "Could not create directory /root/.ssh" into
        # the status file, where it reads as the failure. This path is
        # inside the agent's ReadWritePaths and is root-owned, so the
        # timer and the app's button pin the same key in the same file.
        local known="${DESTCONF%/*}/autobackup-dest.known_hosts"
        [ -e "$known" ] || ( umask 077 && : > "$known" )
        # `accept-new`, not `no`: the first sight of the far side is
        # pinned, and a CHANGED key after that stops the copy — which
        # is the one moment somebody must be told rather than obeyed.
        error="$(ssh -i "$DESTKEY" -p "$DEST_PORT" \
                  -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \
                  -o UserKnownHostsFile="$known" \
                  -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=20 \
                  "$DEST_USER@$DEST_HOST" "mkdir -p '$folder'" 2>&1)" \
          && error="$(scp -i "$DESTKEY" -P "$DEST_PORT" \
                  -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \
                  -o UserKnownHostsFile="$known" \
                  -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=20 \
                  "$out" "$DEST_USER@$DEST_HOST:$folder/" 2>&1)" \
          && ok=1
        # **A warning is not a failure.** ssh writes advice to stderr on
        # runs that worked, and this field is what the app shows as the
        # reason the copy did not leave; keeping it would report a
        # successful shipment as a broken one.
        [ "$ok" -eq 1 ] && error=""
        if [ "$ok" -eq 1 ] && [ "$DEST_KEEP" -gt 0 ]; then
          # Rotation on the FAR side, and only there: what this machine
          # keeps is RETENTION, and the two are different numbers on
          # purpose — a phone-sized disk here, a big one there.
          ssh -i "$DESTKEY" -p "$DEST_PORT" -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \
              -o UserKnownHostsFile="$known" \
              -o BatchMode=yes "$DEST_USER@$DEST_HOST" \
              "ls -1t '$folder' 2>/dev/null | tail -n +$((DEST_KEEP + 1)) | while read -r old; do rm -rf -- '$folder'/\"\$old\"; done" \
              >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        fi
      fi
      ;;
    s3)
      if ! command -v rclone >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        error="rclone is not installed on this server"
      elif [ ! -s "$DESTKEY" ]; then
        error="no credentials stored for the bucket"
      else
        # The credentials reach rclone as ENVIRONMENT, never argv:
        # /proc/<pid>/cmdline is world-readable and an access key in it
        # is an access key given away.
        error="$(
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$(cut -d: -f1 "$DESTKEY")" \
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$(cut -d: -f2- "$DESTKEY")" \
          RCLONE_CONFIG_GD_TYPE=s3 \
          RCLONE_CONFIG_GD_PROVIDER=Other \
          RCLONE_CONFIG_GD_ENV_AUTH=true \
          RCLONE_CONFIG_GD_ENDPOINT="$DEST_HOST" \
          rclone copy "$out" "gd:$DEST_BUCKET/$folder/" 2>&1
        )" && ok=1
      fi
      ;;
    *) error="unknown destination kind: $DEST_KIND" ;;
  esac
  {
    echo "AT=$(date +%s)"
    echo "OK=$ok"
    # One line, and the far side's own words: three different repairs
    # hide behind "it failed". QUOTED, and with quotes of its own
    # removed — see `do_test_destination` on what reading this file
    # as shell used to cost.
    # **Carriage returns too, not just newlines.** ssh ends its own
    # warnings with CR, and a reader that renders them the way a
    # terminal does — the agent's does, for progress bars — keeps only
    # what follows the last one and throws the rest away. The marker line vanished and the app was told the
    # copy failed, with no reason, while the file had landed.
    echo "ERROR='$(printf '%s' "$error" | tr '\r\n\t' '   ' | tr -d "'" | cut -c1-400)'"
  } > "$DESTSTATUS"
  chmod 644 "$DESTSTATUS"
  return 0
}

# The key this server ships WITH, made once and never replaced: the
# public half is already authorized on the far side, and a new pair
# would silently stop every copy.
gd_ensure_dest_key() {
  [ -s "$DESTKEY" ] && return 0
  # **The folder first.** A server that never had the agent installed
  # has no /etc/gryonixnexus, and ssh-keygen into a folder that is not
  # there failed with its output thrown away: `set-destination` stopped
  # on the chmod that followed and answered rc 1 with not one word.
  # The app's own screen showed
  # "could not save" and nothing else.
  install -d -m 755 "$(dirname "$DESTKEY")"
  rm -f "$DESTKEY" "$DESTPUB"
  if ! ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N '' -C 'gryonixnexus-backup' -f "$DESTKEY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "could not create the key this server ships backups with" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  chmod 600 "$DESTKEY"
  chmod 644 "$DESTPUB" 2>/dev/null || true
}

do_set_destination() {
  local kind="${1:-none}" host="${2:-}" port="${3:-22}" user="${4:-}"
  local path="${5:-}" bucket="${6:-}" keep="${7:-0}"
  case "$kind" in
    none|ssh|s3) ;;
    *) echo "unsupported destination: ${kind}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  case "$port$keep" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "invalid port or keep count" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  case "$host$user$path$bucket" in
    *[\'\"\\\`\$]*|*$'\n'*|*$'\r'*)
      echo "the destination may not contain quotes, backslashes, \$, backticks or line breaks" >&2
      exit 2 ;;
  esac
  # A secret on stdin, never argv — the same rule the passphrase
  # follows one function down.
  if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
    local secret
    secret="$(cat)"
    if [ -n "$secret" ]; then
      install -d -m 755 "$(dirname "$DESTKEY")"
      ( umask 077 && printf '%s' "$secret" > "$DESTKEY" )
      chmod 600 "$DESTKEY"
    fi
  fi
  [ "$kind" = "ssh" ] && gd_ensure_dest_key
  install -d -m 755 "$(dirname "$DESTCONF")"
  cat > "$DESTCONF" <<EOF_DEST
DEST_KIND=$kind
DEST_HOST='$host'
DEST_PORT=$port
DEST_USER='$user'
DEST_PATH='$path'
DEST_BUCKET='$bucket'
DEST_KEEP=$keep
EOF_DEST
  # 0640 and owned by root: it names a host and an account, which is
  # the owner's business and not every account's on this machine. The
  # app reads it through this wrapper, which runs as root.
  chmod 640 "$DESTCONF"
  # Printed so the app can authorize it on the far side without a
  # second call — a public key, and nothing else, is safe on stdout.
  [ -s "$DESTPUB" ] && printf 'GRYONIXNEXUS_DEST_PUBKEY %s\n' "$(cat "$DESTPUB")"
}

# Everything `show-destination` answers, in one read: the app draws the
# destination, the public key to authorize and what the last shipment
# did on a single screen.
do_show_destination() {
  load_destination
  printf 'DEST_KIND=%s\nDEST_HOST=%s\nDEST_PORT=%s\nDEST_USER=%s\nDEST_PATH=%s\nDEST_BUCKET=%s\nDEST_KEEP=%s\n' \
    "$DEST_KIND" "$DEST_HOST" "$DEST_PORT" "$DEST_USER" "$DEST_PATH" "$DEST_BUCKET" "$DEST_KEEP"
  [ -s "$DESTPUB" ] && printf 'DEST_PUBKEY=%s\n' "$(cat "$DESTPUB")"
  [ -s "$DESTSTATUS" ] && cat "$DESTSTATUS"
  return 0
}

# One small file, sent the same way a real archive is. The only way to
# learn a destination is wrong BEFORE the nightly run trusts it.
do_test_destination() {
  load_destination
  if [ "$DEST_KIND" = "none" ]; then
    echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DEST_TEST 0 no destination is set"
    return 0
  fi
  local probe
  probe="$(mktemp /tmp/gryonixnexus-dest-XXXXXX.txt)"
  date -u +'gryonixNexus destination check %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' > "$probe"
  gd_ship "$probe" check
  rm -f "$probe"
  # Read back out of the status file rather than kept in a variable:
  # what the app will see later is exactly what it is told now.
  local ok="0" error=""
  # **Parsed, never sourced.** This file carries the FAR SIDE's own
  # words, and reading it with `.` made them shell: a message with
  # "(ED25519)" in it broke the read outright, and one carrying $(…)
  # would have run here as root.
  if [ -f "$DESTSTATUS" ]; then
    ok="$(sed -n 's/^OK=//p' "$DESTSTATUS" | head -1)"
    error="$(sed -n "s/^ERROR='\(.*\)'\$/\1/p" "$DESTSTATUS" | head -1)"
  fi
  ok="${ok:-0}"
  echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DEST_TEST $ok $error"
}

# USB drives that take a copy of every archive. A host that never
# chose one keeps every archive here, exactly as before.
DRIVECONF='/etc/gryonixnexus/backup-drives.conf'
DRIVESTATUS='/etc/gryonixnexus/backup-drives.status'
DRIVELAST='/etc/gryonixnexus/backup-drives.last'
DRIVEROOT='/srv/gryonix-backup'
DRIVE_MODE=both
DRIVE_ENCRYPT=1
DRIVES=""
GD_DRIVE_ERROR=""
load_drives() {
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  [ -f "$DRIVECONF" ] && . "$DRIVECONF"
  : "${DRIVE_MODE:=both}" "${DRIVE_ENCRYPT:=1}"
}

# Where fstab mounts one drive, whether or not it is plugged in.
gd_drive_fstab() {
  findmnt --fstab -rno TARGET -S "UUID=$1" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
}

# The drive's mount point, only when it is mounted and marked.
gd_drive_target() {
  local target
  target="$(gd_drive_fstab "$1")"
  case "$target" in "$DRIVEROOT"/*) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
  # Never a bare folder: writing there fills the system disk.
  mountpoint -q "$target" || return 0
  grep -qx "$1" "$target/.gryonix-backup-drive" 2>/dev/null || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$target"
}

# Mounts a drive plugged in after boot, through systemd.
gd_drive_ready() {
  local target
  target="$(gd_drive_target "$1")"
  if [ -z "$target" ] && [ -b "/dev/disk/by-uuid/$1" ]; then
    target="$(gd_drive_fstab "$1")"
    case "$target" in
      "$DRIVEROOT"/*)
        systemctl start "$(systemd-escape -p --suffix=mount "$target")" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
    esac
    target="$(gd_drive_target "$1")"
  fi
  printf '%s' "$target"
}

# The drive's name: the last part of its mount point.
gd_drive_name() {
  local target
  target="$(gd_drive_fstab "$1")"
  if [ -n "$target" ]; then printf '%s' "${target##*/}"; else printf '%s' "$1"; fi
}

# Why a write to a drive failed.
gd_drive_why() {
  local avail
  case ",$(findmnt -no OPTIONS --target "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)," in
    *,ro,*) echo "the drive went read-only; check it"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  avail="$(df -B1 --output=avail "$1" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 | tr -cd '0-9')"
  if [ "${avail:-0}" -lt 1048576 ]; then
    echo "the drive is full"
  else
    echo "the drive could not be written"
  fi
}

# Copies one archive to a drive, encrypting it when asked.
gd_drive_write() {
  local src="$1" dest="$2" pass=""
  GD_DRIVE_ERROR=""
  if [ "${dest%.gpg}" = "$dest" ] || [ "${src%.gpg}" != "$src" ]; then
    cp "$src" "$dest" 2>/dev/null && return 0
    GD_DRIVE_ERROR="$(gd_drive_why "${dest%/*}")"
    return 1
  fi
  pass="$GD_PASS"
  [ -n "$pass" ] || pass="$(cat "$PASSFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$pass" ]; then
    GD_DRIVE_ERROR="no backup passphrase is stored for encrypted copies"
    return 1
  fi
  printf '%s' "$pass" | gpg --batch --quiet --yes --symmetric \
       --cipher-algo AES256 --passphrase-fd 0 --pinentry-mode loopback \
       --output "$dest" "$src" 2>/dev/null && return 0
  GD_DRIVE_ERROR="$(gd_drive_why "${dest%/*}")"
  return 1
}

# Keeps the newest RETENTION copies in one folder.
gd_drive_rotate() {
  { ls -1t "$1" 2>/dev/null || true; } | tail -n +$((RETENTION + 1)) \
    | while IFS= read -r old; do rm -rf -- "${1:?}/$old"; done || true
}

# What the last drive copy did, read by show-drives.
gd_drive_status() {
  install -d -m 755 "${DRIVESTATUS%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true
  {
    echo "DRIVE_AT=$(date +%s)"
    if [ -z "$1" ]; then echo "DRIVE_OK=1"; else echo "DRIVE_OK=0"; fi
    echo "DRIVE_ERROR='$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr '\r\n\t' '   ' | tr -d "'" | sed 's/^ *//' | cut -c1-400)'"
  } > "$DRIVESTATUS" 2>/dev/null || true
  chmod 644 "$DRIVESTATUS" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Records when a drive last took a copy.
gd_drive_seen() {
  if { grep -v "^$1 " "$DRIVELAST" 2>/dev/null || true; echo "$1 $(date +%s)"; } \
       > "$DRIVELAST.new" 2>/dev/null; then
    mv -f "$DRIVELAST.new" "$DRIVELAST" 2>/dev/null || true
    chmod 644 "$DRIVELAST" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}

# Writes one copy to one drive; prints where it landed, or why not.
gd_drive_put() {
  local out="$1" folder="$2/$3" name="$4"
  if ! install -d -m 700 "$folder" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "the drive could not be written"
    return 1
  fi
  # Leftovers of a copy cut short when the drive was pulled.
  rm -f "$folder"/.partial-* 2>/dev/null || true
  if gd_drive_write "$out" "$folder/.partial-$name" \
     && mv -f "$folder/.partial-$name" "$folder/$name" 2>/dev/null; then
    sync -f "$folder/$name" 2>/dev/null || true
    chmod 600 "$folder/$name" 2>/dev/null || true
    gd_drive_rotate "$folder"
    printf '%s\n' "$folder/$name"
    return 0
  fi
  rm -f "$folder/.partial-$name" 2>/dev/null || true
  printf '%s\n' "${GD_DRIVE_ERROR:-the drive could not be written}"
  return 1
}

# **A copy of each archive on every chosen USB drive.** A missing
# or full drive never fails the backup; it is recorded instead.
gd_drive_copy() {
  local out="$1" service="$2" name uuid target landed first="" failed=""
  load_drives
  if [ -z "$DRIVES" ] || [ "$DRIVE_MODE" = "local" ]; then return 0; fi
  name="$(basename "$out")"
  if [ "$DRIVE_ENCRYPT" -eq 1 ] && [ "${name%.gpg}" = "$name" ]; then name="$name.gpg"; fi
  for uuid in $DRIVES; do
    target="$(gd_drive_ready "$uuid")"
    if [ -z "$target" ]; then
      failed="$failed $(gd_drive_name "$uuid"): not connected;"
      continue
    fi
    if landed="$(gd_drive_put "$out" "$target" "$service" "$name")"; then
      printf '%s %s %s\n' 'GRYONIXNEXUS_DRIVE_COPY' "$uuid" "$landed"
      [ -n "$first" ] || first="$landed"
      gd_drive_seen "$uuid"
    else
      failed="$failed ${target##*/}: $landed;"
    fi
  done
  gd_drive_status "$failed"
  # Drives only: the local archive goes once a drive holds it.
  if [ "$DRIVE_MODE" = "drive" ] && [ -n "$first" ]; then
    rm -f "$out"
    printf '%s %s %s\n' 'GRYONIXNEXUS_BACKUP_DONE' \
      "$(stat -c %s "$first" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" "$first"
  fi
  return 0
}

# Copies the newest archive an external tool wrote.
gd_drive_copy_newest() {
  local newest
  newest="$({ ls -1t "$1/$2"-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -n 1)"
  [ -n "$newest" ] || return 0
  gd_drive_copy "$newest" "$2"
  # Drives only: the unpacked folder leaves with its archive.
  if [ ! -e "$newest" ] && [ -d "${newest%.tar.gz}" ]; then rm -rf "${newest%.tar.gz}"; fi
}

do_set_drives() {
  local mode="${1:-both}" encrypt="${2:-1}" checked="" uuid
  shift 2 || true
  case "$mode" in
    both|local|drive) ;;
    *) echo "unsupported drive mode: ${mode}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  case "$encrypt" in
    0|1) ;;
    *) echo "invalid encryption flag: ${encrypt}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  for uuid in "$@"; do
    case "$uuid" in
      ''|*[!0-9A-Fa-f-]*) echo "invalid drive id: ${uuid}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
    checked="$checked $uuid"
  done
  install -d -m 755 "$(dirname "$DRIVECONF")"
  cat > "$DRIVECONF" <<EOF_DRIVES
DRIVE_MODE=$mode
DRIVE_ENCRYPT=$encrypt
DRIVES='${checked# }'
EOF_DRIVES
  chmod 644 "$DRIVECONF"
  # A newly chosen drive counts from now.
  for uuid in $checked; do
    grep -q "^$uuid " "$DRIVELAST" 2>/dev/null || gd_drive_seen "$uuid"
  done
}

# Settings, each drive's state and the last copy, in one read.
do_show_drives() {
  local uuid target size avail
  load_drives
  printf 'DRIVE_MODE=%s\nDRIVE_ENCRYPT=%s\nDRIVES=%s\n' "$DRIVE_MODE" "$DRIVE_ENCRYPT" "$DRIVES"
  if [ -s "$PASSFILE" ]; then echo 'DRIVE_PASS=1'; else echo 'DRIVE_PASS=0'; fi
  for uuid in $DRIVES; do
    target="$(gd_drive_target "$uuid")"
    size=0
    avail=0
    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
      read -r size avail < <(df -B1 --output=size,avail "$target" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || true
      printf 'DRIVE=%s 1 %s %s %s\n' "$uuid" "${size:-0}" "${avail:-0}" "$target"
    else
      printf 'DRIVE=%s 0 0 0 %s\n' "$uuid" "$(gd_drive_fstab "$uuid")"
    fi
  done
  [ -s "$DRIVESTATUS" ] && cat "$DRIVESTATUS"
  return 0
}

# --- per-service locking (see LockSections) --------------------------

GD_LOCK_BUSY=75

gd_with_lock() {
  local id="$1"
  shift
  install -d -m 700 '/var/lib/gryonixnexus/locks'
  local fd
  exec {fd}>"/var/lib/gryonixnexus/locks/$id.lock"
  if ! flock -n "$fd"; then
    echo "$id: another backup or update for this service is already running, skipping" >&2
    return "$GD_LOCK_BUSY"
  fi
  "$@"
}

# --- helpers shared by every generated service body -----------------

gd_compose_stop() {
  local project="$1"
  shift
  docker compose -p "$project" stop "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

gd_compose_start() {
  local project="$1"
  shift
  docker compose -p "$project" start "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

# Container id of one compose service; empty when it is not running.
gd_container() {
  docker compose -p "$1" ps -q "$2" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
}

# A tar of a live database directory is a corrupt backup, so the
# database is dumped through its own client instead. The credentials
# come from the container's OWN environment — compose already put them
# there — because passing them from here would place the password in
# the argv of `docker exec`, readable by every account on the host.
gd_dump_postgres() {
  local cid
  cid="$(gd_container "$1" "$2")"
  if [ -z "$cid" ]; then
    echo "the $1 database container is not running" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! docker exec "$cid" sh -c \
       'PGPASSWORD="$POSTGRES_PASSWORD" exec pg_dump --clean --if-exists -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"' \
       > "$3"; then
    echo "the $1 database dump failed" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  [ -s "$3" ] || { echo "the $1 database dump is empty" >&2; return 1; }
}

# --single-transaction is what makes a dump of a RUNNING InnoDB
# database trustworthy: one consistent snapshot, no instance-wide lock.
# mariadb-dump on current images, mysqldump on older ones.
#
# A fourth argument names the database explicitly, for a service that
# keeps several in one engine and whose container therefore sets no
# MYSQL_DATABASE at all; without it the container's own variable is
# used, as it always was. Only the NAME travels here — the password is
# still read inside the container, never put in the argv of docker exec
# where /proc hands it to every account on the host.
gd_dump_mysql() {
  local cid
  cid="$(gd_container "$1" "$2")"
  if [ -z "$cid" ]; then
    echo "the $1 database container is not running" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! docker exec "$cid" sh -c \
       'if command -v mariadb-dump >/dev/null 2>&1; then D=mariadb-dump; else D=mysqldump; fi; MYSQL_PWD="$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD" exec "$D" --single-transaction --quick -u root "${1:-$MYSQL_DATABASE}"' \
       sh "${4:-}" > "$3"; then
    echo "the $1 database dump failed" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  [ -s "$3" ] || { echo "the $1 database dump is empty" >&2; return 1; }
}

# Keeps the newest RETENTION archives of one service — encrypted and
# plain together, they are one series. The pipeline is guarded: with
# fewer archives than RETENTION `ls` finds nothing to list and would
# fail the whole run under pipefail, which is every first run.
gd_rotate() {
  { ls -1t "$1/$2"-*.tar.gz "$1/$2"-*.tar.gz.gpg 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | tail -n +$((RETENTION + 1)) | xargs -r rm -f
}

# Encrypt (or not), put the archive in place, rotate, announce.
gd_finish() {
  local name="$1" dir="$2" plain="$3" work="$4" out=""
  if [ ! -s "$plain" ]; then
    rm -rf "$work"
    echo "the $name archive is empty" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if [ "$GD_ENCRYPT" -eq 1 ]; then
    out="$dir/$(basename "$plain").gpg"
    if ! printf '%s' "$GD_PASS" | gpg --batch --quiet --yes --symmetric \
         --cipher-algo AES256 --passphrase-fd 0 --pinentry-mode loopback \
         --output "$out" "$plain"; then
      rm -rf "$work"
      echo "could not encrypt the $name backup" >&2
      return 1
    fi
  else
    out="$dir/$(basename "$plain")"
    mv "$plain" "$out"
  fi
  # The plain archive never outlives the encrypted one.
  rm -rf "$work"
  chmod 600 "$out"
  chown "$OWNER" "$out" 2>/dev/null || true
  gd_rotate "$dir" "$name"
  # A streamed command carries no exit status back to the app, so the
  # archive announces itself: marker, size in bytes, path.
  printf '%s %s %s\n' 'GRYONIXNEXUS_BACKUP_DONE' \
    "$(stat -c %s "$out" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" "$out"
  # And then it leaves the machine, if a destination was chosen. After
  # the marker on purpose: the archive exists and is announced whatever
  # the far side does.
  gd_ship "$out" "$name"
  # A copy on each USB drive, after the far side.
  gd_drive_copy "$out" "$name"
}

backup_vaultwarden() {
  local stamp plain
  stamp="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
  plain='/opt/backups/vaultwarden/vaultwarden-backup.tar.gz'
  docker stop 'vaultwarden' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  local archived=0
  tar -czf "$plain" '/opt/vaultwarden/data' 2>/dev/null && archived=1
  # The container comes back up no matter what the archive did.
  docker start 'vaultwarden' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  if [ "$archived" -ne 1 ] || [ ! -s "$plain" ]; then
    rm -f "$plain"
    echo "the vaultwarden archive could not be written" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! printf '%s' "$GD_PASS" | gpg --batch --quiet --yes --symmetric \
       --cipher-algo AES256 --passphrase-fd 0 --pinentry-mode loopback \
       --output "$plain.$stamp.gpg" "$plain"; then
    rm -f "$plain"
    echo "could not encrypt the vaultwarden backup" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  # The plain archive never outlives the encrypted one.
  rm -f "$plain"
  chmod 600 "$plain.$stamp.gpg"
  chown "$OWNER" "$plain.$stamp.gpg" 2>/dev/null || true
  # Rotation: keep the newest RETENTION encrypted archives. The
  # pipeline is guarded — with fewer archives than RETENTION,

  { ls -1t '/opt/backups/vaultwarden'/*.gpg 2>/dev/null || true; } \
    | tail -n +$((RETENTION + 1)) | xargs -r rm -f
  printf '%s %s %s\n' 'GRYONIXNEXUS_BACKUP_DONE' \
    "$(stat -c %s "$plain.$stamp.gpg" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" "$plain.$stamp.gpg"
